title: Ruff Shift Recharge: Feasibility and Acceptability of Canine-Assisted Breaks for Night-Shift Psychiatric Nurses.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of canine-assisted breaks for night-shift psychiatric nurses and the practicality of participant measures and canine welfare monitoring in inpatient staff-focused animal-assisted activity (AAA) research. METHODS: N Night-shift nurses ( = 11) were offered voluntary drop-in AAA breaks over 3 weeks at an inpatient psychiatric facility. Feasibility indicators included enrollment, attendance, survey completion, canine welfare monitoring, and adverse events. Acceptability indicators included session duration, observed engagement, and participant feedback. Mood was assessed before and after each break using the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule. Burnout and well-being were assessed 1 week before and after the intervention period. Outcomes were summarized descriptively. Therapy dog welfare was monitored through structured observation and repeated Canine Behavioral Assessment and Research Questionnaire assessments. RESULTS: M Eight nurses participated in 21 AAA breaks; durations ranged from 2 to 47 min ( = 22.3 min). Break-embedded data collection and canine welfare monitoring did not disrupt workflow, but follow-up survey attrition limited postintervention data. Feedback respondents described improved mood and energy and reduced stress. None of the 21 AAA breaks were terminated for canine stress. One site visit ended 30 min early after stress occurred without participants present. CONCLUSIONS: Drop-in AAA breaks were deliverable and acceptable to participating nurses at this site. Findings do not establish effectiveness, comparative advantage, mechanism, sustainability, or generalizability. Future studies should retain structured canine welfare monitoring and include usual-break and active nonanimal comparison conditions.

title: Real-world characteristics of endovascular treatment for middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture: a prospective multicenter registry study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of endovascular treatment (EVT) in middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion remains inconclusive, particularly in rural areas with aging populations. We characterized EVT and medical management (MM) for M2 occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, and explored clinical factors associated with outcomes. METHODS: We analyzed a prospective multicenter acute ischemic stroke registry (July 2020-June 2022; 11 stroke centers). Patients with M2 occlusion were classified into EVT or MM groups; characteristics, workflow metrics, and outcomes were described and referenced against previously reported series. RESULTS: Among 210 patients, 34 had M2 occlusion (EVT, n=10; MM, n=24). At 90 days, functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) was 40.0% (EVT) and 45.8% (MM); symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, 0% and 4.2%; mortality, 20.0% and 12.5%; successful reperfusion, 70.0% (EVT). Both groups were older than in previous reports (median 81 years). The EVT group also received rt-PA less often (30.0%) and had longer puncture-to-reperfusion times (81 minutes), whereas the MM group had lower pre-stroke independence (67%) and higher mortality, despite lower severity. CONCLUSION: Advanced age, delayed reperfusion, and greater pre-stroke dependency distinguished this rural cohort from previous reports and likely account for its outcomes, underscoring the need for locally tailored patient selection for EVT in M2 occlusion.

METHODS: We analyzed a prospective multicenter acute ischemic stroke registry (July 2020-June 2022; 11 stroke centers).

title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results. METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points. RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

title: Risk of recurrence in patients with provoked venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) provoked by transient risk factors is generally considered low risk, supporting short-term anticoagulation. However, this paradigm is based on heterogeneous definitions of provoking factors. In this prospective cohort study, we evaluated recurrence risk using the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis classification of major and minor transient risk factors. Patients with symptomatic deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism who completed ≥3 months of anticoagulation were followed after treatment discontinuation. Patients with cancer, major thrombophilia, pregnancy-associated VTE, or indication for extended anticoagulation were excluded. The primary outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE. Cumulative incidence was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. The study was terminated early due to unexpectedly high recurrence risk among patients with major provoking factors. Between 2019 and 2025, 242 patients were followed for a median of 23.9 months; 72 had major and 170 had minor transient risk factors. Recurrent VTE occurred in 13 patients with major and 7 with minor risk factors. At 24 months, recurrence risk was 9.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 6.0-14.0) overall and 19.7% (11.0-30.2) after major and 5.0% (2.2-9.5) after minor risk factors. No recurrence occurred in 81 women with hormone-associated VTE; after their exclusion, the recurrence risk among patients with other minor risk factors increased to 9.1% (95% CI, 4.0-17.0). Recurrence after provoked VTE is not uniformly low and varies substantially by the type of transient risk factor. These findings challenge current treatment paradigms and support individualized decisions regarding anticoagulation duration.

However, this paradigm is based on heterogeneous definitions of provoking factors. In this prospective cohort study, we evaluated recurrence risk using the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis classification of major and minor transient risk factors.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Exposure and Long-Term Outcomes in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Real-World Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asymptomatic carotid stenosis is a prevalent manifestation of atherosclerotic disease and, despite contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy, remains associated with downstream cerebrovascular events and mortality. Given the vascular and cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1As), we evaluated whether GLP-1A exposure is associated with lower long-term event rates in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults (≥18 years) with carotid stenosis (January 1, 2016, to September 30, 2025) were included; patients with prior/baseline cerebrovascular events and those undergoing carotid revascularization within 6 months were excluded to operationalize an asymptomatic cohort. GLP-1A exposure was defined as any GLP-1A use within 6 months after carotid stenosis diagnosis; nonexposed patients served as comparators. Cohorts were propensity score-matched 1:1, and outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: After matching, 30,332 patients were included in each cohort. GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of ischemic stroke (hazard ratio [HR] 0.63, 0.71, and 0.73 at 1, 3, and 5 years; 5-year cumulative event probability 5.55% versus 6.85%), hemorrhagic stroke (HR 0.63, 0.69, and 0.74; 2.04% versus 2.35%), large vessel occlusion stroke (HR 0.70, 0.77, and 0.81; 2.04% versus 2.27%), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.42, 0.58, and 0.64; 17.11% versus 21.49%). The composite of ischemic stroke or mortality was also lower (HR 0.48, 0.61, and 0.66; 20.88% versus 25.85% at 5 years) in the GLP-1A-exposed cohort. CONCLUSIONS: In a large real-world cohort with asymptomatic carotid stenosis, GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of stroke subtypes, large vessel occlusion stroke, and mortality across 1-5 years. These observational findings warrant prospective validation to clarify causality and optimal integration into contemporary medical management.

Given the vascular and cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1As), we evaluated whether GLP-1A exposure is associated with lower long-term event rates in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis. title: Global landscape and evolution of limb-salvage reconstruction with prostheses for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours: A bibliometric analysis.
abstract: PurposeTo delineate the evolution, collaborative structure, clinically relevant themes, and emerging priorities of limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours.MethodsEnglish-language articles and reviews published from 1 January 1995 to 31 October 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on 31 October 2025. Co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and burst analyses were conducted using CiteSpace 6.4.1 and VOSviewer 1.6.20.ResultsOf 2,606 retrieved records, 2,283 underwent title and abstract screening and 997 were included. Publication output increased, peaking at 84 in 2023. The United States led publication output and cumulative citations, while China ranked second by output. Keyword analyses indicated that research attention expanded from surgical strategy selection for specific tumour types and anatomical sites to include long-term prosthetic survival, complications and functional outcomes. Recent research themes included technologies such as 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and finite element analysis, with "3d printing" showing the strongest keyword burst (strength 9.49; 2021-2025). Research output was concentrated in a small number of centres and journals. Frequently co-cited publications provided standardised methods for assessing limb function and classifying endoprosthetic failure.ConclusionsLong-term prosthetic survival, complications, function and quality of life remain central themes in limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction. Technologies supporting individualised reconstruction, including 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and emerging robot-assisted techniques, are attracting increasing research interest. Future multicentre comparative studies should use standardised outcome measures and long-term follow-up to evaluate prosthesis design, fixation and selection, as well as strategies for preventing and managing reconstructive failure.

title: Cilengitide limits syndromic and sporadic thoracic aortic aneurysm by targeting specific αV integrin.
abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, still lacking an etiologic therapy. Aberrant activation of TGF-β and dysregulation of mechanotransduction signalling in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a key role in the pathology. However, a precise picture of molecular mechanisms in the disease is still unclear. Integrins containing the αV subunit are central in pro-fibrotic pathways mediated by TGF-β and mechanotransduction signalling pathways, but their role as a potential therapeutic target in syndromic and sporadic TAAs still needs investigation. We showed higher expression levels of αV integrin in both types of human TAAs and that the αV integrin inhibitor Cilengitide limits pro-fibrotic events in patient-derived VSMCs. In vivo results defined Cilengitide as the most effective and promising drug for the treatment of TAAs in humans.

title: Ruptured pheochromocytoma during preoperative doxazosin treatment.
abstract: Rupture of pheochromocytoma is rare but represents a life-threatening complication. A 43-year-old man with episodic hypertension, palpitations, and chest discomfort was incidentally found, during a computed tomography (CT) aortogram performed to rule out aortic dissection, to have a 5.2-cm right adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Biochemical testing confirmed catecholamine excess. He was started on oral doxazosin 1 mg daily, which was titrated to 2 mg daily after 1 week, followed by oral bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily in preparation for surgery. Five weeks later, he presented with severe right-sided abdominal pain and a blood pressure of 215/111 mmHg. Abdominal CT angiography showed interval enlargement of the adrenal mass with posterior rupture and a retroperitoneal hematoma without active bleeding. He was stabilized with conservative management and subsequently underwent robotic right adrenalectomy. Histopathology confirmed pheochromocytoma with necrosis, without angioinvasion or lymphatic invasion, and with negative margins. Pheochromocytoma rupture can occur despite appropriate α-blockade, and spontaneous hemorrhage remains the most likely proposed mechanism, although α-blockade may be a contributing factor in selected cases.

title: Ascending Aorta Dilation in the Fontan: To Intervene or Not.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ascending aorta dilation is a known finding in the congenital heart disease population and specifically in patients who have undergone single ventricle palliation. CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent single ventricle palliations and had severe ascending aorta dilation. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis. DISCUSSION: There are case reports of aortic dissection, but true risk remains unknown. Weighing the risks of surgery versus conservative management in patients with single ventricle physiology is challenging. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Surgical intervention on dilated aortas in patients with single ventricle physiology is perilous but possible in the correct circumstances.

title: Beyond Access Flow: The FLASH Multiorgan Framework for Assessing High-Flow Arteriovenous Fistulas in Hemodialysis.
abstract: High-flow arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) impose a continuous hemodynamic burden on patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis, yet access blood flow (Qa) alone does not determine their cardiovascular significance. High access blood flow, high-output physiology, and clinically relevant cardiovascular intolerance represent related but distinct states whose expression depends on the interaction among access-related hemodynamic exposure, systemic flow response, cardiovascular reserve, volume status, and downstream cardiovascular consequences. This review proposes a clinically oriented, multiorgan framework for evaluating patients in whom an AVF is suspected of contributing to cardiovascular deterioration. Assessment begins with the clinical and dialysis context and integrates five interconnected domains: FISTULA, characterizing access-related hemodynamic exposure; LOAD, evaluating the systemic circulatory response; ASSESSMENT OF EXTRAVASCULAR LUNG WATER, identifying pulmonary congestion; SYSTEMIC VENOUS CONGESTION, assessing systemic venous consequences; and HEART, evaluating cardiac adaptation and maladaptation. Integration across these domains may reveal overlapping clinical-hemodynamic patterns, including preserved tolerance despite high flow, predominantly hyperdynamic physiology, cardiac maladaptation, systemic venous- or pulmonary-predominant consequences, and multicompartmental involvement. Discordance between systemic venous and pulmonary findings may provide physiologically relevant information rather than represent conflicting evidence. Serial reassessment after ultrafiltration, clinical change, or access-flow modification further emphasizes the dynamic nature of these patterns. The framework is intended to support physiologic interpretation rather than establish AVF causality, define new diagnostic categories, or propose treatment thresholds. Ultimately, assessment should move beyond asking how much blood flows through the fistula toward determining how the individual patient responds to that flow.

High access blood flow, high-output physiology, and clinically relevant cardiovascular intolerance represent related but distinct states whose expression depends on the interaction among access-related hemodynamic exposure, systemic flow response, cardiovascular reserve, volume status, and downstream cardiovascular consequences. This review proposes a clinically oriented, multiorgan framework for evaluating patients in whom an AVF is suspected of contributing to cardiovascular deterioration.

title: Comparative evaluation of handheld vs. high-end ultrasound systems for TIPSS hemodynamic assessment: first impressions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPSS) procedures require reliable post-interventional hemodynamic monitoring to detect shunt dysfunction, for which Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred modality. Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed. Blood flow measurements were obtained and compared using a high-end ultrasound system (Resona R9, Mindray) and modern handheld ultrasound device (Vscan Air™ CL, GE). The TIPSS was evaluated using B-mode and color Doppler sonography. Image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale and flow parameters using statistical analysis. The image quality and the difference between the two devices were analyzed using correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression models including TIPSS flow values, skin-to-TIPSS distance, and TIPSS dwell time. RESULTS: Both devices produced clinically interpretable images. However, the high-end device yielded superior image quality in 16 of 23 cases (p < 0.001). Significant correlations were observed between the difference in mean TIPSS flow measurements obtained by the two devices (Δ mean TIPSS flow) and corresponding average flow values measured by the two devices (Kendall's τ = 0.656; p < 0.001). Significant associations with Δ TIPSS mean flow were identified for skin-to-TIPSS distance (τ = 0.39; p = 0.014) and TIPSS dwell time (τ = -0.39; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, both mean TIPSS flow measured by the high-end system and skin-to-TIPSS distance remained significantly associated with Δ TIPSS mean flow. The TIPSS mean flow measured by the high-end system correlated with TIPSS dwell time (τ = 0.38; p = 0.021). Bland-Altman analysis revealed that handheld measurements tended to overestimate low flows and underestimate high flows. CONCLUSION: Handheld ultrasound devices show promising potential for TIPSS surveillance; however, they could lead to distorted flow deviations. Contemporary handheld devices may nevertheless be useful in selected point-of-care settings but cannot yet replace high-end systems for precise hemodynamic monitoring. Larger prospective studies are required. TRIAL REGISTRATION: No clinical trial registration was performed, as this study is a single-center retrospective observational analysis based on existing clinical data. The study did not involve prospective patient enrollment, international procedures, or assignment to treatment groups. Therefore, registration in a clinical trial registry was not applicable.

Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Cardiovascular disturbances and ward hypotension after major vascular surgery: a single-centre prospective cohort study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery. RESULTS: We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.

We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery.

title: Increased prevalence of hypertension in paediatric turner syndrome: a retrospective study.
abstract: th th th Girls and women with Turner Syndrome (TS) are known to be at increased risk of aortic dissection, a condition for which hypertension is a modifiable risk factor. Our aim was to determine the frequency of hypertension in girls attending a tertiary paediatric TS clinic and its association with clinical characteristics. Retrospective analysis of clinical data was conducted for girls with TS attending the dedicated paediatric TS clinic at the Royal Hospital for Children Glasgow, between 1976-2023. Blood pressure (BP) was converted to centiles according to age and height. Hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs ≥ 95centile and pre-hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs between the 90-95centiles, with measurements on 2 consecutive occasions. 184 girls with TS were included and BP data were available for a total of 172 (93%) with a median (range) age at the time of BP attainment of 12 (4, 18) years. Of these, 38 (22%) had congenital heart disease and 48 (28%) had an existing renal anomaly. The prevalence of hypertensive range BP at clinic within this cohort was 50% (n = 86), with median age of onset at 12 (4, 17) years of age. Pre-hypertensive range BPs were identified in 12 (7%). In total, 14/86 (15%) had ongoing high BP and were prescribed anti-hypertensive treatment. There is an increased prevalence of hypertension within the paediatric TS population compared to the general paediatric population. Early management of blood pressure in this group is likely to reduce cardiovascular disease burden.

title: Posterior cerebral artery dissection: clinical and angiographic spectrum, management, and outcomes in a retrospective 14-patient case series.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Posterior cerebral artery (PCA) dissection is a rare cerebrovascular disorder with heterogeneous clinical and angiographic presentations. Because evidence is largely limited to small case series and individual reports, optimal diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 14 patients with angiographically confirmed PCA dissection or dissecting PCA aneurysms identified at a single center between January 2016 and December 2025. Clinical presentation, angiographic characteristics, treatment strategy, procedural complications, and available clinical and vascular imaging follow-up were analyzed. RESULTS: The median age was 43.5 years (IQR, 33.8-56.3; range, 20-63 years). Hemorrhagic presentation occurred in 8 patients (57.1%), including 6 with subarachnoid hemorrhage (42.9%). Two patients were managed conservatively, 3 underwent conventional stenting alone, 5 underwent flow-diverter treatment, 2 underwent coil embolization without an implanted stent, and 2 underwent conventional stenting combined with coil embolization. Most patients achieved favorable clinical and angiographic outcomes. One patient remained severely disabled (mRS 5), and one patient developed fatal post-procedural subarachnoid hemorrhage after flow-diverter treatment. CONCLUSIONS: PCA dissection is a rare and clinically heterogeneous condition that may present with hemorrhagic or nonhemorrhagic manifestations. Management should be individualized according to rupture status, lesion morphology, vascular anatomy, collateral circulation, and the feasibility of parent-vessel preservation. Conservative management and different endovascular strategies may be appropriate in selected patients, but the small retrospective nature of available series precludes conclusions regarding superiority of any single treatment approach.

Because evidence is largely limited to small case series and individual reports, optimal diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 14 patients with angiographically confirmed PCA dissection or dissecting PCA aneurysms identified at a single center between January 2016 and December 2025.

title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Is Associated With Heart Failure in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] in peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains uncertain. METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively studied 138 patients with intermittent claudication undergoing endovascular therapy. Patients were classified by Lp(a) level (≥30 vs. <30 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a higher incidence of MACE (31.1% vs. 9.6%; P=0.002), predominantly driven by heart failure. It independently predicted MACE (HR 4.23) and heart failure (HR 5.12), but not cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with heart failure-driven MACE after endovascular therapy in patients with PAD.

title: Early prediction of surgical site complications after vascular groin incision using postoperative drainage kinetics: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Groin incisions in vascular surgery are associated with a considerable incidence of postoperative surgical site complications (SSCs), with lymphatic complications such as lymphorrhea and lymphocele representing a frequent and clinically relevant source of morbidity. Previous studies have identified postoperative drainage volume as a potential surrogate marker for impaired lymphatic healing and subsequent wound complications. Based on these observations, researchers have proposed standardized drainage management strategies to help identify high-risk patients early and guide timely intervention. This study retrospectively evaluates postoperative outcomes after implementing this strategy. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort analysis included 106 patients with 114 vertical groin incisions undergoing open vascular procedures requiring femoral exposure between June 2023 and June 2024. We defined SSCs according to a previously published classification. We defined the groin incision as the unit of analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence of clinically relevant SSCs (grades 2-4). Secondary outcomes included drainage characteristics, drain removal timing, lymphatic interventions, and risk factors for lymphatic complications. RESULTS: Postoperative drainage volumes were significantly associated with clinically relevant surgical site complications (SSC grade 2-4). Drainage on POD 1 was not significantly associated with complications. Higher drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards were significantly associated with complications, with increasing effect sizes over time (POD 2: OR 1.048, p = 0.022; POD 3: OR 1.047, p = 0.023; POD 4: OR 1.178, p < 0.001). Cumulative drainage up to POD 4 demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (OR 1.024, p = 0.0006; c = 0.831). Overall, 43.0% of groin incisions developed clinically relevant SSC. CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative drainage kinetics enable early identification of patients at risk for clinically relevant lymphatic complications after vascular groin surgery. While drainage of POD 1 is not predictive, drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards allow reliable risk stratification with progressively increasing predictive accuracy. POD 2 drainage output is a clinically relevant predictor of subsequent lymphatic complications. A POD2 drainage output ≥80 mL/24 h may support early identification of high-risk patients and facilitate timely interdisciplinary planning of targeted lymphatic interventions.

title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis. METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed. RESULTS: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies. CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints. METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively. RESULTS: Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%). CONCLUSION: A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.

METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale).

title: Sociodemographic predictors of postpartum anticoagulant selection in pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) requires anticoagulation into the postpartum period that overlaps with breastfeeding initiation. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) and vitamin K antagonists (VKA) are compatible with breastfeeding, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are currently not recommended. Postpartum anticoagulant selection may be influenced by safety, convenience and access, potentially contributing to racial and socioeconomic inequities in care. We evaluated the impact of race and sociodemographic factors on postpartum anticoagulant selection in a publicly funded healthcare system. METHODS: This is a population-based cohort study using linked administrative health data in Ontario, Canada. We included Ontario Drug Benefit (ODB) recipients with pregnancy-associated VTE diagnosed between 2012 and 2022 who received ≥1 anticoagulant prescription within 6 months postpartum. Primary outcome was the exclusive receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulants (LMWH/VKA). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) were determined to identify factors associated with breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant use. RESULTS: Of 113 ODB-eligible individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE, 62.8% received ≥6 weeks of postpartum anticoagulation. During the 6-month postpartum period, 25.7% transitioned to a DOAC. No significant association was observed between race and receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulation. However, individuals in the most materially deprived neighbourhoods were significantly less likely to receive a breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant compared with those in less deprived areas (aOR 0.20, 95% CI 0.07-0.58). CONCLUSIONS: In this population-based cohort, 1 in 4 individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE received a DOAC within 6 months postpartum. Postpartum anticoagulant selection was affected by socioeconomic status. These findings highlight the need to explore structural factors influencing anticoagulant selection to advance equitable postpartum care.

Postpartum anticoagulant selection may be influenced by safety, convenience and access, potentially contributing to racial and socioeconomic inequities in care.

title: Feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the amber peripheral liquid embolic system: results from stage I of the first-in-human OPAL study.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the early safety and technical feasibility of Amber 20 for peripheral vascular embolization in a prospective, multicenter, first-in-human stage I study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled. The primary endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events (SAEs) within 24 h. Secondary endpoints included overall adverse events (AEs) and technical success, defined as complete vascular occlusion or devascularization on final angiography. RESULTS: Fifteen patients (60% female; median age 56 years) underwent embolization using Amber 20. Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases (15/15). No device-related SAEs or AEs were reported within 24 h. Five patient (33%) experienced a mild adverse event (postembolization syndrome) related to the procedure. All adverse events resolved without sequelae. No device deficiencies were observed. CONCLUSION: In this first-in-human, multicenter study, Amber 20 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and high technical success rate for peripheral vascular embolization. These preliminary findings support its potential as an effective liquid embolic agent, warranting further evaluation in larger studies with longer follow-up (stage II).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled.

title: National incidence and predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism after inpatient lumbar fusion, 2016-2022.
abstract: PURPOSE: To estimate the national incidence of in-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission and identify independent comorbidity predictors. METHODS: Adult (≥ 18 years) inpatient admissions undergoing lumbar fusion were identified in the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2022 using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE during the index admission. Characteristics were compared between VTE and non-VTE admissions, and multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression evaluated independent predictors. Significance was set at the P < 0.05 level. RESULTS: Across 631,165 weighted inpatient lumbar fusion admissions, in-hospital VTE incidence was 0.6%. VTE admissions were older (age distribution, P < 0.001), more frequently male (P = 0.003), and more often involved multilevel fusion (78.5% vs. 74.2%, P = 0.007). On multivariable analysis, the largest adjusted associations were observed for other neurologic disorders (OR 3.76, 95% CI 2.93-4.83, P < 0.001), coagulopathy (OR 3.70, 95% CI 2.89-4.75, P < 0.001), weight loss (OR 3.57, 95% CI 2.35-5.42, P < 0.001), pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.82-4.23, P < 0.001), and paralysis (OR 2.78, 95% CI 2.09-3.71, P < 0.001). Additional predictors included solid tumor without metastasis (OR 1.97, P = 0.022), cerebrovascular disease (OR 1.90, P = 0.003), peripheral vascular disease (OR 1.58, P = 0.002), obesity (OR 1.75, P < 0.001), seizure disorders (OR 1.74, P = 0.016), congestive heart failure (OR 1.71, P < 0.001), and deficiency anemia (OR 1.64, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission was uncommon but concentrated among patients with distinct high-risk comorbidity profiles. These findings support risk-stratified inpatient surveillance and prevention strategies during hospitalization.

METHODS: Adult (≥ 18 years) inpatient admissions undergoing lumbar fusion were identified in the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2022 using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE during the index admission.

title: Robotic mini-thoracotomy approach to aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement.
abstract: Fully endoscopic robotic-assisted aortic valve replacement has emerged as a safe, reproducible and effective minimally invasive approach with favourable clinical outcomes. In patients undergoing aortic valve surgery, concomitant ascending aortic aneurysms should be addressed whenever indicated, as failure to do so may lead to serious long-term aortic complications. Currently these patients must undergo some form of sternotomy to address both pathologies. The use of a totally robotic minithoracotomy approach for concomitant aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported. This video tutorial highlights a robotic approach for combined aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement, representing a pioneering step in the evolution of complex robotically assisted aortic surgery. Our vision is to develop a robotic aortic surgery programme that maintains the safety, efficacy and durability of conventional techniques while significantly expediting postoperative recovery for selected patients.

title: Two-year patency rates of drug-coated balloon angioplasty for radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula juxta-anastomotic stenosis: A single-center study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The study aims to assess primary and secondary patency rates and the need for reintervention after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty performed for juxta-anastomotic AVF stenoses. METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients who underwent DCB angioplasty for AVF stenosis between May 2019 and December 2023. Information on reinterventions was obtained from medical records, while AVF functional patency was assessed through Duplex Ultrasound Scanning. The primary outcomes measured were patency rates at 6, 12, and 24 months. RESULTS: The study included 69 patients. The average age was 61.4 ± 12.7 years, with 45 (65.2%) being male. Primary patency rates were 72.5% (50/69), 46.4% (32/69), and 30.4% (21/69) at 6, 12, 24 months, respectively. Secondary patency rates were 85.5% (59/69), 59.4% (41/69), and 46.4% (32/69). DISCUSSION: DCB angioplasty shows acceptable mid-term primary patency and sustained longer-term secondary patency for treating juxta-anastomotic stenosis in primary RC AVFs. Notably, the secondary patency rates indicate that re-interventions can help preserve the access circuit.

title: Sirtuins in cellular senescence and cardiovascular diseases: From mechanistic basis to activator development and translational perspectives.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.
englishSummary: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses.

title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain. METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes. RESULTS: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64). DISCUSSION: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors. RESULTS: p p p Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52,= 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58,= 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11,= 0.049). DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored.

title: Ruptured Mycotic Internal Carotid Artery Pseudoaneurysm Presenting as Massive Hematemesis in a Child.
abstract: Massive hematemesis in children may rarely originate from vascular etiologies such as mycotic internal carotid artery pseudoaneurysm. Early suspicion and multidisciplinary management are crucial. Our case highlights the importance of considering vascular etiologies in unexplained bleeding and demonstrates that endovascular stenting can provide effective, life-saving treatment.

title: + NLRP3Macrophages: Central Inflammatory Nodes of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm and Potential Cellular Target of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids.
abstract: + + Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a fatal inflammatory vascular disease without effective clinical treatments. Dietary patterns regulate aortic inflammation, and Mediterranean diet-derived omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFA) exert anti-inflammatory effects, yet their cellular targets in AAA remain unclear. We integrated three single-cell RNA-seq cohorts (12 AAA, 3 controls) and constructed a human aortic cell atlas with 64,258 cells. Pseudo-bulk analysis and CoVarNet multicellular network analysis revealed a core remodeling axis: protective FOLR2resident macrophages were depleted, while a unique AAA-enriched NLRP3inflammatory macrophage population (M08_Mph_NLRP3) formed the hub of pathological inflammatory networks. Three bulk transcriptomic cohorts and five complementary enrichment approaches verified this signature. An LPS/OX-LDL/IL-1β-stimulated THP-1 model recapitulated AAA macrophage pathological changes including NLRP3 inflammasome overactivation, enhanced proliferation and migration. Further functional tests demonstrated ω-3 PUFA markedly blocked inflammasome cascade, reduced IL-1β/IL-18 release and reversed all macrophage pathological phenotypes. This study identifies M08_Mph_NLRP3 as the important inflammatory mediator of AAA and provides single-cell and in vitro functional evidence supporting ω-3 PUFA as a candidate nutritional agent targeting NLRP3-driven vascular inflammation.

title: Early-onset Pulmonary Embolism After Prolonged Combined Cosmetic Breast Surgery: 2 Case Reports and a Literature Review.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) after aesthetic breast surgery is considered rare, and patients are often perceived as low risk. However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures. Procedures lasted 225 and 370 minutes, respectively. Dyspnea, chest discomfort, or palpitations occurred within 48 hours postoperatively. D-dimer was elevated, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed acute PE, including a saddle embolus in 1 patient. Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin followed by rivaroxaban led to clinical improvement without observed recurrence at the short-term follow-up. A focused literature review identified additional thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast surgery, most within the first postoperative week. Early-onset PE can complicate prolonged, combined cosmetic breast surgery even in patients classified as intermediate risk. Pharmacologic venous thromboembolism prophylaxis before symptom onset could not be reliably ascertained from available records. These cases support a protocolized, Caprini-informed pathway that specifies routine mechanical measures and clear indications, agent/dose, and timing for chemoprophylaxis, with explicit documentation and vigilance for early postoperative cardiopulmonary symptoms.

title: Segmental arterial mediolysis: An underrecognized rare vascular disease requiring an interprofessional diagnostic and therapeutic pathway.
abstract: Segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM) is a rare, non-inflammatory, non-atherosclerotic arteriopathy that predominantly affects the visceral circulation and may cause dissection, aneurysm, hemorrhage, or ischemia. Its diagnosis is challenging because imaging findings overlap with fibromuscular dysplasia, vasculitis, connective tissue disorders, atherosclerosis, and mycotic aneurysm. This narrative review synthesizes the available evidence into an interprofessional diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. The proposed framework links radiological suspicion with structured exclusion of major mimics, multidisciplinary vascular assessment, treatment selection, management of hemodynamic instability, and longitudinal imaging surveillance. Conservative management is appropriate for stable patients without active hemorrhage, whereas endovascular treatment is generally preferred when intervention is required and anatomically feasible, with surgery reserved for failed stabilization or uncontrolled bleeding. Because current evidence is largely observational and case-based, the pathway should be regarded as a literature-based framework requiring prospective validation rather than a validated clinical guideline.

title: CCL19 emerges as a regional signal in human abdominal aortic aneurysm through targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of the aneurysmal wall and neck.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: The molecular mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression remain incompletely understood and may vary across anatomically distinct regions of the diseased aorta. We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology. METHODS: Paired aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck tissues were obtained from 18 patients with AAA. Inflammatory proteins were quantified using the Olink Target 48 cytokine panel, with 45 proteins retained for analysis after quality-control filtering. Directional RNA sequencing was subsequently performed on matched tissue samples to characterize the expression of genes corresponding to the proteins included in the proteomic analysis and to assess concordance between transcriptomic and proteomic differences. RESULTS: Proteomic analysis identified three differentially expressed proteins (IL6, IL15, CCL19) between aneurysmal wall and neck. Transcriptomic analysis of the corresponding genes identified three differentially expressed transcripts (CCL19, CCL11, LTA). CCL19 was consistently elevated at both the protein and transcript levels in aneurysmal wall, whereas the remaining molecular alterations were specific to either the proteomic or transcriptomic analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Aneurysm wall and neck tissues showed largely similar inflammatory molecular profiles, with only a limited number of regional differences identified either on the protein or transcript level. CCL19 being the only concordant signal in both proteomic and transcriptomic analysis.

title: Evolving management of upper extremity pseudoaneurysms: Role of observation and nonsurgical management.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While the natural history and treatment algorithm of femoral pseudoaneurysms has been well established, the management of Upper Extremity Pseudoaneurysm (UEPSA) is not clearly defined. We sought to evaluate our 30-year experience and management strategies of this pathology. METHODS: We reviewed 93 patients that were identified utilizing ICD9/10 codes from an initial 384 patients with the diagnosis of aneurysm of the upper extremity from 1992 to 2023. Patients with UEPSA secondary to iatrogenic arterial interrogation were analyzed by duplex based follow-up until successful thrombosis or subsequent intervention was performed. Dialysis access pseudoaneurysms or trauma related UEPSAs were excluded for analysis. RESULTS: A total of 93 patients were identified with a UEPSA (39 brachial, 43 radial, 6 axillary, 5 ulnar arteries); 12 additional patients were identified who had only a patent neck at the time of formal vascular laboratory imaging and were excluded from treatment strategy analysis (11 radial, 1 brachial). The mean time between iatrogenic event and vascular surgery evaluation was 22 days. Fifty-nine (63.4%) underwent surgical repair, 27 (29.0%) received conservative management, and 7 (7.5%) underwent thrombin injection. Of the 93 treatment group patients that were analyzed, separated into sizes, patients with pseudoaneurysms less than 2cm there were a total of 21/93 (22.5%) patients managed conservatively, and 16/93 (17.2%) patients managed surgically; in contrast for those with greater than 2cm UEPSAs, 6/93 (6.5%) patients were managed conservatively, 43/93 (46.2%) were managed surgically, and 7/93 (7.5%) with thrombin injection. Comparing the first 15 years of the study period there were 27 iatrogenic UEPSAs noted with only 3/27 (11.1%) managed conservatively, while after 2010 there were 66 iatrogenic pseudoaneurysms with 24/66 (36.4%) managed conservatively. Of the UEPSAs managed conservatively, only 3/24 (12.5%) failed conservative management and were recommended to pursue intervention. CONCLUSIONS: Upper extremity pseudoaneurysms with significant symptomatic hematomas, suspected infection, and/or nerve related symptoms should undergo surgical exploration and repair. A consideration for conservative management of small pseudoaneurysms <2cm without the above presentation, observation and surveillance may be considered with more than 90% achieving successful spontaneous thrombosis.

title: Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes With the E-tegra™ Stent Graft System for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: Endoleaks, Limb Patency, Reinterventions, Aneurysm Sac Behaviour, and Mid-Term Follow-Up.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To systematically synthesize the published clinical evidence regarding endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the E-tegra™ stent graft system, evaluating technical success, endoleaks, limb patency, reinterventions, aneurysm sac behavior, and mid-term follow-up outcomes. METHODS: Conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 framework, systematic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane databases. Observational studies and registry reports reporting clinical outcomes of adults undergoing EVAR with the E-tegra system were included. Because of cohort overlap and heterogeneous endpoint definitions, data were synthesized narratively and descriptively without formal quantitative pooling. RESULTS: Three eligible publications were identified, representing 209 unique patients across two underlying cohorts: the multicenter TIGRE registry (147 patients) and an independent single-center series (62 patients). Primary technical success was high, reaching 99.3% in the registry and 100% in the single-center cohort, with zero perioperative mortality across both. At mid-term follow-up (ranging from 18 months to 2 years), type II endoleak and iliac limb occlusion emerged as the primary complications. The TIGRE update reported 16 total complications (10.88%), including 8 type II endoleaks and 6 iliac limb occlusions, with a 2-year reintervention rate of 4.76%. In the single-center series, 1 type IIIa endoleak (1.6%) and 3 clinically significant type II endoleaks requiring embolization were observed. Favorable mid-term sac behavior was noted in the registry, with 72.11% of patients demonstrating >10-mm aneurysm sac shrinkage. Predefined anatomical hostility did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with adverse outcomes or reinterventions in the registry data. CONCLUSIONS: Early and mid-term evidence for the E-tegra stent graft demonstrates high procedural success and acceptable clinical outcomes with competitive mid-term complication and reintervention rates. However, the current literature is strictly limited to single-arm observational data with short-to-medium horizons (18-24 months). Long-term durability and structural performance relative to well-established companion platforms remain unestablished, highlighting the critical need for continued prospective surveillance and comparative, long-term multicenter trials.

METHODS: Conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 framework, systematic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane databases. Observational studies and registry reports reporting clinical outcomes of adults undergoing EVAR with the E-tegra system were included.

title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR. METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed. RESULTS: Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low < 128, medium 128 - 200, high > 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions. CONCLUSION: The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane. REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I= 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I= 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I= 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I= 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I= 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I= 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I= 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I= 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes. CONCLUSION: Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.

title: Endothelial Contributions to Venous Thrombus Resolution.
abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is an obstructive vascular condition with an incidence of ~1 in 1000 adults per year. Complications of DVT include post-thrombotic syndrome, which is debilitating and painful, and pulmonary embolism, which is life-threatening. Current treatments for DVT are associated with increased risks of bleeding, infection, or re-thrombosis, and fail to accelerate natural venous thrombus resolution. Venous thrombus resolution occurs through a process of organization that involves thrombus retraction away from the vein, fibrinolysis of the thrombus, and the formation of vascular channels within and around the thrombus. Endothelial cell (EC)-lined vascular channels are present in rodent and human resolving thrombi. Rodent models of DVT show that thrombus neovascularization occurs as early as 3-4 days after thrombus induction and increases progressively thereafter throughout thrombus resolution. The extent to which thrombus neovascularization contributes to its resolution, as well as the source of the ECs that vascularize the resolving thrombus, are unclear. Circumstantial evidence suggests that neovascularization is driven by resident ECs that ingress into the resolving thrombus, while circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) promote neovascularization in a paracrine manner. Resident ECs and EPCs also contribute to thrombus fibrinolysis. The aim of this review is to describe the role of ECs and EPCs in DVT resolution, and the potential of promoting thrombus endothelialization and vascularization for the treatment of DVT. We will also outline knowledge gaps in the understanding of EC/EPC-mediated contributions to DVT resolution. The promotion of EC-mediated thrombus resolution represents a novel therapeutic strategy for DVT.

title: Pantothenate metabolic alterations in PROS1 mutation carriers and the antithrombotic effects of pantethine.
abstract: Background Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear. Objectives This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1‑mutation patients through integrated multi‑omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models. Methods Serum metabolomics, siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed. Results Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM‑1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF‑κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL‑1β‑induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM‑1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine‑conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co‑incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation‑driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet mode of interaction. Conclusions This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet association in Protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1‑deficient in vivo models.

title: Incidence and predictors of suboptimal functional outcomes despite successful reperfusion in paediatric stroke: a cohort study from the Save ChildS Pro registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Successful vessel reperfusion with persistent clinical deficit occurs in 40-60% of adults undergoing mechanical thrombectomy but has never been characterised in childhood stroke. We aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of so-called futile recanalisation, in which the occluded artery is reopened but the patient does not recover good function, in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Save ChildS Pro registry, an international, multicentre, observational registry that included children aged 28 days to 18 years presenting with acute ischaemic stroke across 45 centres in 12 countries between Jan 1, 2020, and Aug 31, 2023. Patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy and had successful recanalisation (expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [eTICI] grade ≥2b) were included. The primary outcome was suboptimal functional outcome despite successful recanalisation, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score greater than 2 at 90 days, on a scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death) on which 0-2 denotes functional independence; three additional thresholds (mRS score >1, Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure [PSOM] >1·0, and PSOM >0·5) were analysed as sensitivity analyses. Adjusted associations between candidate predictors (age, baseline Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [PedNIHSS] score, baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score [ASPECTS], and final eTICI grade) and each outcome were estimated using Firth-penalised multivariable logistic regression. Save ChildS Pro is registered with the German Clinical Trials Registry (DRKS00018960). FINDINGS: 101 patients (54 [53%] males and 47 [47%] females; median age 11·0 years [IQR 6·0-15·0]) had successful recanalisation with 90-day follow-up and comprised the analytical cohort. A suboptimal outcome (mRS score >2) occurred in 18 (18%) of 101 patients. On Firth-adjusted multivariable analysis, lower final eTICI grade was significantly associated with suboptimal outcome (adjusted OR 0·44 [95% CI 0·23-0·84], p=0·012), and younger age was associated in the same direction (0·87 [0·78-0·97] per year, p=0·0098); baseline PedNIHSS score and baseline ASPECTS were not independently associated with a suboptimal outcome. Findings were directionally consistent across the three sensitivity thresholds. INTERPRETATION: In this analysis, 18% of children with successful recanalisation had a suboptimal functional outcome at 90 days, markedly lower than the proportion reported in adults (40-60%). Lower recanalisation quality and younger age were independently associated with suboptimal outcome, whereas baseline PedNIHSS score and ASPECTS had limited prognostic value. These findings highlight the need for longer-term studies and challenge the direct translation of adult prognostic frameworks to paediatric stroke, supporting age-specific approaches. Given the limited event count, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation. FUNDING: None.
