title: Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease.
abstract: ABSTRACT: Severely calcified lesions of the femoropopliteal segment have always presented very complex conditions for endovascular therapy of peripheral arterial disease (PAD). In particular, the rigidity and instability of the heavily calcified vessel wall result in a limited initial lumen gain after angioplasty, frequent recoil, early restenosis, and an increased rate of reinterventions. In this context, intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is increasingly becoming the focus of interest. By using low-energy shock waves, both superficial and deep intimal and medial calcifications are selectively micro-fractured. This leads to improved vessel compliance and enables effective angioplasty. At low inflation pressures of 4-6 atm, the barotrauma acting on the vessel wall during IVL is overall reduced. Randomized clinical studies demonstrate a higher technical success rate of IVL compared to PTA plus DCB-PTA, with a lower complication rate and significantly better 1- and 2-year patency. IVL can be used both as a stand-alone therapy and for vessel preparation in combination with DCBPTA, and also presents an alternative therapy to atherectomy, cutting, scoring, and high-pressure balloon angioplasty. This review focuses on the methodological description of the IVL with the Shockwave system in the femoropopliteal segment, considering both technical and clinical success data. KEY POINTS: · IVL enables effective vessel preparation in severe calcified femoropopliteal lesions.. · IVL works with low inflation pressures thereby reducing barotrauma, dissections, and bail-out stenting.. · Patency rates of IVL plus DCB are superior to conventional angioplasty plus DCB.. CITATION FORMAT: · Hölting MS, Bekker I, Stehr A et al. Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2907-7766.

title: Image quality assessment of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CT angiography.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lower-extremity CT angiography (CTA) is widely used for the assessment of peripheral arterial disease. Reducing iodinated contrast medium is desirable, particularly in patients with impaired renal function. This study evaluated the impact of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) on image quality in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 60 patients who underwent lower-extremity spectral CTA with 40 mL of iodinated contrast medium were included. Conventional reconstructions and 40-keV VMI were compared regarding vascular attenuation, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), iodine concentration, and subjective image quality across predefined arterial segments. Qualitative image quality was independently assessed by two readers using a 5-point Likert scale. RESULTS: Compared with conventional reconstructions, 40-keV VMI significantly increased vascular attenuation, SNR, and CNR across all arterial segments (all p < 0.001). Subjective ratings for vessel contrast, vessel sharpness, overall image quality, and diagnostic confidence were significantly higher with VMI for both readers across all evaluated arterial segments (all p < 0.05). Iodine concentration decreased progressively from proximal to distal arterial segments, whereas the CNR advantage of VMI remained preserved throughout the arterial tree. CONCLUSION: Forty-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction significantly improves quantitative and qualitative image-quality parameters in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA compared with conventional reconstructions. These findings suggest that low-keV VMI may improve image-quality characteristics in reduced-contrast CTA protocols, particularly in distal arterial segments. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Low-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction may support reduced-contrast lower-extremity CTA protocols by improving image quality without increasing contrast medium volume. This approach may be particularly valuable for patients in whom minimizing iodinated contrast medium exposure is desirable.

title: Evaluating the Quality and Accessibility of Integrated Vascular Surgery Residency Program Websites for Prospective Applicants.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted a shift to virtual residency interviews, although approximately half of integrated vascular surgery residency (VSR) programs have since returned to an in-person format. Amidst this evolving landscape, program websites have remained an invaluable resource for candidates to learn about VSR programs. In this study, we examined whether VSR program websites provide adequate and current information for residency candidates. METHODS: A list of all active VSR programs was obtained from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS) website. Each program's website was reviewed in November 2025, and data were collected regarding program structure, faculty and current resident rosters, application requirements, and publicly available formal policies. RESULTS: Of the 81 active programs, 80 (98.8%) had a formal residency program website. Information on residency program structure was reported in the majority of websites, including mission statement (91.4%), rotation and curriculum data (65.4%), rotating sites (61.7%), educational conferences (64.2%), and resident research experience (56.8%). Only ten programs (12.3%) reported resident operative volumes. Information regarding the residency program director (PD; 91.4%), program coordinator (PC; 92.6%), teaching faculty (92.6%), and current residents (81.5%) was available in most websites. However, with the exception of the PC (91.4%), contact information for the PD (40.7%), faculty (29.6%), and residents (13.6%) was not easily accessible. The majority of websites had a "how to apply" section (86.4%), but relatively few reported their interview dates (30.9%). Resident experience videos were available in less than half of websites (39.5%). Data on salary (53.1%), resident benefits (53.1%), vacation policies (27.2%), and academic conference policies (28.4%) were also inconsistently reported. CONCLUSIONS: Residency program websites remain a central resource for applicants, particularly in the current era of virtual and hybrid interview formats. In this study, we found substantial variability in the information presented across VSR program websites, with a notable lack of accessible contact information for program leadership, faculty, and residents. Enhancing website content and transparency may better support applicants as they evaluate programs and prepare for the residency application process.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.
englishSummary: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age.

title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point. CONCLUSIONS: High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE. METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model. RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups. CONCLUSION: Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for people with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease: reducing uncertainty in clinical practice.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) may be the most frequent first manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents. The ADA recommends both GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) as the first-line therapy to reduce the cardio-renal risk in people with T2D, including those with PAD. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show that semaglutide is better than placebo in reducing by 30% PAD events in people with T2D (with or without PAD at baseline), although no RCT was designed to investigate PAD-related hard outcomes as a primary endpoint; however, both liraglutide and semaglutide may increase walking distance by approximately 25-30 m at six months in people with T2D and PAD. Cohort studies also confirm that GLP-1RA use is better than non-use in reducing by 28% the risk of MALE in individuals with T2D and PAD, although their retrospective design might introduce residual confounding and under-ascertainment of outcomes. Dedicated RCTs will obtain more direct evidence for the promising lower limb benefits of GLP-1RAs, but the scientific outlook of specific RCTs on hard limb events is empty. In the meantime, clinicians should choose a GLP-1RA of proven efficacy in subjects with T2D and PAD to improve their cardio-nephro-metabolic outlook, as well as their walking capacity, limited at present to liraglutide and semaglutide.

title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism After Lumbar Spine Interbody Fusion: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a feared complication after spine surgery, with limited data comparing approach-specific risk factors after lumbar interbody fusion. This study compared the rate of VTE complications after transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) and anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF). METHODS: A multi-institutional electronic medical record database was queried for patients aged older than 18 years undergoing single-level or multilevel TLIF and ALIF between 2004 and 2024. Patients were evenly divided into single-level (n = 9,618) and multilevel (n = 1,774) TLIF and ALIF cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was conducted using demographics, comorbidities, and anticoagulation use. Odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) of VTE and postoperative bleeding complications were calculated at 30, 60, and 90 days. RESULTS: Compared with single-level TLIF, single-level ALIF was associated with higher odds of VTE events at 30 days (OR: 2.0, 95% CI, 1.4 to 2.9; P < 0.001), 60 days (OR: 1.8, 95% CI, 1.3 to 2.5; P < 0.001), and 90 days (OR: 1.7, 95% CI, 1.3 to 2.4; P < 0.001). Multilevel ALIF was also associated with higher odds of VTE events at 30 days (OR: 2.7, 95% CI: 1.2 to 5.1; P = 0.015), 60 days (OR: 2.0, 95% CI, 1.2 to 3.4; P = 0.010), and 90 days (OR: 1.9, 95% CI, 1.1 to 3.2; P = 0.015) when compared with multilevel TLIF. No significant differences were observed in postoperative bleeding complications between single-level and multilevel TLIF and ALIF cohorts at all study intervals (P > 0.05). DISCUSSION: ALIF was associated with increased VTE complications, with no differences in postoperative bleeding complications when compared with TLIF. These findings suggest that surgical approach should be considered in perioperative VTE risk stratification and patient counseling after lumbar interbody fusion surgery, highlighting the need for future prospective studies evaluating approach-specific VTE prevention strategies.

This study compared the rate of VTE complications after transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) and anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF). METHODS: A multi-institutional electronic medical record database was queried for patients aged older than 18 years undergoing single-level or multilevel TLIF and ALIF between 2004 and 2024.

title: Endovascular Treatment for Ruptured Internal Carotid Artery Pseudoaneurysms Secondary to Radiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of endovascular intervention in treating ruptured internal carotid artery (ICA) pseudoaneurysms secondary to radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with NPC and angiographically confirmed ruptured ICA pseudoaneurysms who underwent endovascular treatment at Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, between September 2016 and September 2023. After CTA or emergency DSA, the bleeding site and collateral circulation were assessed. Balloon test occlusion (BTO) was performed selectively when parent artery occlusion (PAO) was considered feasible. Treatment was individualized using covered stent implantation, coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, or PAO. Outcomes included final angiographic hemostasis, recurrent bleeding, complications (analyzed as events when patients had more than one event), and the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at last follow-up. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were analyzed: 15 underwent coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, 12 covered stent implantation, and 5 PAO. BTO was performed in 8 patients (25.0%): 5 tolerated BTO and underwent PAO, whereas 3 had inadequate collateral reserve and received reconstructive treatment. Final angiographic hemostasis was achieved in all 32 patients (100%; 95% exact CI 89.1-100%). At last follow-up, 28 patients (87.5%; 95% CI 71.0%-96.5%) had mRS 0-1. Six complication events were recorded across 32 procedures (18.8 events per 100 procedures): 4 recurrent bleeding events and 2 transient limb weakness events, graded as Medical Research Council muscle-power grade 3. One patient contributed both recurrent bleeding and transient weakness; therefore event rates should not be interpreted as unique-patient incidence. No severe complications were observed. CONCLUSION: Endovascular treatment achieved immediate hemostasis in this small, retrospective series of ruptured radiation-related ICA pseudoaneurysms. Treatment should be individualized according to collateral reserve, vascular anatomy, and the feasibility of BTO. Covered stents and coil-based reconstruction can preserve the parent artery but require close surveillance for endoleak, residual pseudoaneurysm, and new lesions. PAO may be considered only when collateral circulation is adequate; the zero-event estimate in five patients has a wide confidence interval. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with NPC and angiographically confirmed ruptured ICA pseudoaneurysms who underwent endovascular treatment at Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, between September 2016 and September 2023. After CTA or emergency DSA, the bleeding site and collateral circulation were assessed.

title: Local complications of peripheral intravenous vasopressor use with phentolamine as an antidote: a retrospective review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prior studies have indicated that peripheral administration of vasopressors, particularly norepinephrine, can be considered safe, with local complications occurring in 0% to 1.8% of patients. Our study further explored the local skin complications from peripheral vasopressor administration treated with phentolamine in a large health care system. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who received phentolamine for effects of local infiltration of pressors. Data were collected for demographics, vasopressor dose and duration of use, phentolamine dose and time after extravasation until administration, peripheral intravenous characteristics, as well as outcomes such as length of stay and mortality. Data on patients who did and did not require central venous catheter placement postextravasation were compared. RESULTS: 2 Of 92 patients with infiltrated vasopressor intravenous access who required phentolamine, the mean age was 69, with 65% being female and a mean body mass index of 28 kg/m. The most common sites of intravenous access were the antecubital fossa (33%) and forearm (27%). Mean number of hours prior to extravasation of peripheral vasopressors requiring phentolamine administration was 21 hours. Mean number of minutes prior to phentolamine administration after extravasation was 131 minutes. Seventy-six percent of patients did not any have significant ischemic tissue injury with extravasation, and 24% of patients had only minor bruising and erythema. Two significant reactions occurred, including deep vein thrombosis and local skin necrosis. Fifty-two percent of patients required a subsequent central venous line placement. The mean length of stay was 5.4 days in the intensive care unit and 11.8 days in the hospital, and in-patient mortality was 17%. CONCLUSION: In our large cohort of patients with extravasation from peripheral vasopressors managed with local phentolamine administration, severe tissue skin or soft tissue injury was rare.

Our study further explored the local skin complications from peripheral vasopressor administration treated with phentolamine in a large health care system. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who received phentolamine for effects of local infiltration of pressors.

title: Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing. METHODS: A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The final seven-variable ARC included age >60 years, abrupt onset pain, severe pain, hypotension/shock, neurological deficit, pulse deficit, and known aortic disease. Patients were classified as positive if any ARC variable was present and negative only if all variables were absent. In the derivation cohort, ARC achieved a sensitivity of 99.2% (95% CI 99.1-99.3). In the ADvISED/PROFUNDUS cohort (4598 patients, 10.2% AAS prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100) with specificity 23.7% (95% CI 22.4-25.0). In the DAShED cohort (5346 patients, 0.3% prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 76.8-100) and specificity 36.4% (95% CI 35.1-37.7), ruling out 36.3% of patients without missing any AAS cases. CONCLUSIONS: ARC is an externally validated, pragmatic clinical rule demonstrating high diagnostic sensitivity in a large external validation cohort. When incorporated into existing diagnostic pathways, ARC has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing while maintaining diagnostic performance. Further prospective validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing.

title: Development and application of evaluation criteria for venous thromboembolism prevention in patients with gynecologic malignancies during the perioperative period.
abstract: i C i C BackgroundPatients with gynecologic malignancies face a high perioperative VTE risk and suboptimal prevention adherence, yet lack systematic, evidence-based evaluation standards.ObjectiveTo develop and preliminarily validate evidence-based, comprehensive evaluation criteria for perioperative VTE prevention in this population.MethodsThe Delphi method was employed to formulate the evaluation criteria for VTE prevention in this population. The Attribute Hierarchical Model (AHM) was used to assign a weight to each indicator, and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was applied to evaluate adherence to perioperative VTE prevention standards among patients undergoing gynecologic surgery at our hospital.ResultsThe final criteria included 12 indicators covering quantitative and dynamic VTE risk assessment, bleeding risk evaluation, implementation of basic prophylaxis, assessment of indications and contraindications for mechanical and pharmacologic prophylaxis, timing, dosing, and duration of anticoagulant prophylaxis, and monitoring of efficacy and safety. The indicator weight coefficients ranged from 0.0234 to 0.1357. Among the 107 patients, 62 (57.94%) had ≥ 0.6, and 45 (42.06%) had < 0.6. Indicator-level analysis showed 100% compliance for basic prophylaxis, mechanical prophylaxis indications, and absence of contraindications to pharmacologic prophylaxis. The lowest compliance rates were observed for quantitative VTE risk assessment (25.23%, 27/107), dynamic VTE risk assessment (32.71%, 35/107), initiation timing (24.30%, 26/107), prophylaxis duration (24.30%, 26/107), and efficacy and safety monitoring (14.95%, 16/107).ConclusionThis study developed scientifically grounded and clinically feasible evaluation criteria for perioperative VTE prevention in patients with gynecologic malignancies. They provide a practical basis for quality improvement and ongoing refinement of institutional VTE prevention strategies.

title: Multidisciplinary forensic evaluation of fatal non-traumatic rectus sheath hematoma associated with acute pulmonary thromboembolism and salicylate exposure: A case report.
abstract: Rectus sheath hematoma is an uncommon cause of severe hemorrhage and may present a diagnostic challenge in forensic practice, particularly when the hemorrhage extends from the abdominal wall into the pelvic extraperitoneal space. We report the case of a 71-year-old woman who was found dead at home. Postmortem computed tomography demonstrated a hyperdense lesion extending from the lower abdominal wall into the pelvic cavity. Autopsy revealed a massive hematoma extending from the rectus sheath through the extraperitoneal space into the lesser pelvis, without external evidence of trunk trauma. The total hemorrhage volume was estimated to approach 1000 mL. Additional findings included deep vein thrombosis extending from the inferior vena cava to the left common iliac vein and fresh pulmonary thromboemboli in the lobar branches of both lungs. Histopathological examination demonstrated partial organization of the deep vein thrombosis, whereas the pulmonary thromboemboli were relatively fresh, consistent with an acute terminal event. Toxicological analysis detected salicylic acid at a therapeutic level, and an over-the-counter medication containing acetylsalicylic acid was found at the scene. Taken together, the findings were considered most consistent with fatal non-traumatic rectus sheath hematoma, likely triggered by severe cough in the setting of acute pulmonary thromboembolism and possibly exacerbated by impaired hemostasis associated with salicylate exposure. This case highlights the importance of integrating postmortem computed tomography, conventional autopsy, histopathology, and toxicology in the evaluation of extensive truncal hemorrhage and in the differentiation of non-traumatic from traumatic bleeding in forensic casework.

We report the case of a 71-year-old woman who was found dead at home. Postmortem computed tomography demonstrated a hyperdense lesion extending from the lower abdominal wall into the pelvic cavity.

title: Non-invasive assessment of postoperative revascularization using slab MIP images in 3D TOF MRA in pediatric moyamoya disease.
abstract: PURPOSE: Repeated assessment of postoperative revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease is clinically important, but digital subtraction angiography (DSA) is invasive. We aimed to develop a novel, non-invasive scoring method (moya-ASPECTS) that applies the six cortical MCA regions of ASPECTS to slab maximum intensity projection (MIP) images from three-dimensional time-of-flight (3D TOF) magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), and to examine its correlation with DSA findings and cerebral blood flow (CBF) changes after surgery. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 45 treated hemispheres in 28 pediatric patients who underwent revascularization between 2010 and 2023. Eight hemispheres underwent indirect revascularization alone and 37 underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization. We evaluated postoperative cortical revascularization using the moya-ASPECTS score based on slab MIP images derived from 3D TOF MRA, and examined its associations with Matsushima grade, resting cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebrovascular reserve (CVR), and regression of basal moyamoya vessels. RESULTS: The moya-ASPECTS score showed a strong correlation with Matsushima grade (p < 0.001). Postoperative resting CBF increased by 2.27 ml/100 g/min for each point increase in moya-ASPECTS (95% CI 0.87-3.67, p = 0.003). While moya-ASPECTS was not associated with CVR change, it correlated significantly with regression of moyamoya vessels (RR 1.33, 95% CI 1.12-1.58, p < 0.001). Higher moya-ASPECTS scores were inversely associated with postoperative asymptomatic infarction, although the number of events was small. CONCLUSION: The moya-ASPECTS score derived from slab MIP images provides a non-invasive, repeatable, and semi-quantitative method for evaluating postoperative cortical revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease. This method correlates well with DSA-based Matsushima grade and postoperative CBF improvement, supporting its potential use as a practical non-invasive adjunct for serial outpatient follow-up.

title: CTA-defined calcified nodules as a predictor of adverse outcomes following carotid revascularization.
abstract: Carotid calcification can complicate carotid artery stenting (CAS), but the clinical impact may depend on calcification morphology rather than calcification burden alone. We retrospectively evaluated 92 patients who underwent carotid revascularization with either carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or CAS and classified preoperative CTA findings as no/spotty calcification (Group 1), outer calcification (Group 2), or a calcified nodule (CN) pattern directly abutting the contrast-enhanced lumen (Group 3). The primary composite endpoint comprised procedural failure, ischemic complications, or restenosis. The endpoint occurred in 4 of 83 patients (4.8%) in Groups 1/2 and in 5 of 9 patients (55.6%) in Group 3 (unadjusted OR, 24.69; 95% CI, 4.72-129.14; p < 0.001). In a parsimonious multivariable model including treatment modality and calcification pattern, Group 3 remained associated with the composite endpoint (adjusted OR, 49.05; 95% CI, 4.82-498.94; p = 0.001), whereas CEA was associated with lower risk (adjusted OR, 0.045; 95% CI, 0.003-0.664; p = 0.024). Among patients undergoing CAS, the endpoint occurred in 3 of 38 patients (7.9%) in Groups 1/2 and all 5 patients (100%) in Group 3 (p < 0.001). A CTA-defined CN pattern may identify lesions at particularly high risk for CAS-related technical failure or restenosis and may support consideration of CEA when surgically feasible.

The primary composite endpoint comprised procedural failure, ischemic complications, or restenosis.

title: Cardiac Complications following Creation of Arteriovenous Access in Medicare Beneficiaries with ESKD.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs) are the preferred long-term hemodialysis access for the majority of patients, but produce hemodynamic changes that contribute to cardiac complications including heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia. This cohort study leverages nationwide claims data to examine adverse cardiac events associated with AVGs and AVFs among patients with ESKD. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using 100% Medicare fee-for-service claims to identify adults with ESKD undergoing AVF or AVG creation from 2017-2024. The primary outcome was hospitalization for a composite adverse cardiac event (heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or atrial fibrillation or flutter) within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included the composite outcome through 5 years, its individual components, all-cause hospitalization, and flow-reduction procedures. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models. Independent variable analyses were conducted for the primary outcome. RESULTS: We identified 210,002 accesses (mean age 66.3 years; 43% female) including 147,709 (70%) AVFs and 62,293 (30%) AVGs. AVG recipients had a greater burden of baseline comorbidity and cardiovascular disease. Through 1 year, the cumulative incidence of hospitalization for an adverse cardiac event was 40% (AVF 39%, AVG 44%, P < .001), constituting 61% of all-cause hospitalizations. Heart failure predominated (AVF 33%, AVG 37%, P < .001), followed by atrial fibrillation or flutter (AVF 19%, AVG 21%, P < .001), and pulmonary hypertension (AVF 8%, AVG 9%, P < .001). Older age (≥ 50 years), AVG creation, pre-existing pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia were independently associated with a higher hazard of the primary outcome (P < .05). CONCLUSIONS: The high rate of hospitalization for adverse cardiac events in the first year after arteriovenous access creation supports consideration of strategies (e.g., lower-flow forearm access, flow-volume surveillance) to mitigate the hemodynamic consequences of long-term arteriovenous access.

title: The complexity of provoked venous thromboembolism: one treatment plan does not fit all.
abstract: The decision of whether to continue patients diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) on anticoagulation after the initial treatment period is often nuanced. Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE. In addition, major transient risk factors generally carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE than minor transient risk factors. However, many patients will also have ≥1 persistent VTE risk factor, which further increase the risk for recurrence. Some persistent risk factors, such as inflammatory bowel disease, are associated with a sufficiently high risk of recurrent VTE, for which guidelines recommend indefinite anticoagulation. There are multiple other persistent risk factors that carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE, such as chronic renal insufficiency and obesity. The HI-PRO (High-Risk Patients with Provoked Venous Thromboembolism) trial sought to assess the efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis for the prevention of recurrent VTE in patients with an initial provoked VTE and at least 1 persistent risk factor. The study found a lower risk of recurrent VTE in the thromboprophylaxis cohort, challenging the traditional time-limited treatment for provoked VTE, but heterogeneity of the study population and small sample size preclude identification of which subsets of patients could safely discontinue anticoagulation. We consider the conundrum of provoked VTE in this review.

Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE.

title: Late Type IIIa Endoleak Despite Adequate Component Overlap after AFX2 EVAR: A Report of Two Cases.
abstract: Late type IIIa endoleak is a recognized complication of AFX2 (Endologix, Irvine, CA, USA) endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). We report 2 cases occurring 6 and 7 years after EVAR despite adequate initial overlap. In Case 1, computed tomography angiography (CTA) did not clearly demonstrate component uncoupling, whereas duplex ultrasonography showed bidirectional ("to-and-fro") flow and angiography confirmed a type IIIa endoleak. In Case 2, serial computed tomography (CT) retrospectively demonstrated progressive sideways displacement before complete uncoupling. Focal cuff relining and complete endograft relining were performed, respectively. These cases emphasize the need for lifelong surveillance for sac enlargement and changes in endograft configuration after AFX2 EVAR.

title: Native Aorta Non-Touch Total Arch Hybrid Repair for Residual Aortic Dissection after Hemiarch Replacement.
abstract: Reintervention for residual aortic arch dissection after hemiarch replacement for acute type A aortic dissection remains technically challenging. A 70-year-old man presented with progressive dissecting arch aneurysmal dilatation 6 years after hemiarch replacement. Native aorta non-touch total arch hybrid repair was performed using the previously implanted hemiarch graft as the inflow source for total supra-aortic debranching and as the site for short elephant trunk placement. Staged thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed the following day. Postoperative computed tomography showed no endoleak, and the patient remained free from aortic events at 5-year follow-up.

title: Retrograde Open Mesenteric Stenting Failure Requiring Aorto-Mesenteric Bypass in Acute-on-Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is a rare pathology, most commonly associated with multivessel atherosclerosis, whose diagnosis is often delayed due to nonspecific symptoms. Endovascular treatment is the first-line treatment option, although its results may be limited by restenosis or intrastent thrombosis. Open surgery remains an important option in cases where endoluminal treatment has failed. The aim of this paper is to illustrate, through a clinical case, the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges associated with severe CMI. CASE PRESENTATION: A 69-year-old female patient, a long-term smoker being treated for peripheral arterial disease, presented with postprandial abdominal pain that had been present for 6 months, accompanied by severe malnutrition. The CT angiogram revealed occlusion of the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery, with the development of extensive collateral circulation. Initial endovascular revascularization via stenting was performed in a patient presenting with gastrointestinal distress that had required segmental resection of necrotic ileojejunal loops. The course of the disease was characterized by a recurrence of symptoms and stent thrombosis, leading to surgical revascularization via an aorto-mesenteric bypass. The postoperative course was favorable, with the mesenteric angina gradually subsiding, significant weight gain, and lasting functional improvement. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the limitations of endovascular treatment alone in severe multivessel disease and confirms the value of a personalized treatment strategy incorporating open surgery to optimize long-term outcomes.

Endovascular treatment is the first-line treatment option, although its results may be limited by restenosis or intrastent thrombosis. Open surgery remains an important option in cases where endoluminal treatment has failed.

title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear. METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS). RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory. DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT. TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Sensors Placed Frontally and Parietally to Detect Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We aimed to determine whether two-channelled near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) was feasible for recognising anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO) with a device suitable for prehospital use and whether probe placement (frontal vs. parietal) made a difference. METHODS: We analysed NIRS readings of six computed tomography angiography (CTA)-confirmed LVO-stroke patients at Tampere University Hospital during the six-month study period. We placed four sensors on patients' heads: two frontally and two parietally. We provided a detailed description and analysis of these recordings and their correlation with imaging-confirmed changes in perfusion. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 In the frontally placed sensors, the rSOwas 1-8 percentage points higher on the affected side before and 0-9 percentage points higher on the affected side after endovascular treatment (EVT). rSO2 values did not change significantly. One patient showed higher rSOon the healthy side (5 percentage points) before and after EVT. We could not recover frontal values from one patient. In parietally placed censors, all patients had 3-9 percentage points higher rSOon the healthy side before EVT. After EVT, 3 patients had 3-7 percentage points higher rSOon the healthy side. In two cases, after EVT, the difference in rSOchanged to 1-2 percentage points higher on the affected side. We could not record parietal readings in one patient. CONCLUSIONS: 2 Neither NIRS sensor placement detected differences in rSOin LVO; therefore, NIRS appears unsuitable as a diagnostic tool for LVO. Future research should focus on other technologies.

title: When the Filter Becomes the Source: POCUS Detection of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Thrombosis Extending Into the Right Atrium.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are used to prevent pulmonary embolism in patients with venous thromboembolism when anticoagulation is contraindicated. Although uncommon, filter thrombosis can result in thrombus propagation and potentially life-threatening embolic complications. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides a rapid bedside assessment of the heart, lungs, and may facilitate the prompt recognition of unexpected thromboembolic complications. CASE PRESENTATION: A 43-year-old man with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage was admitted to the intensive care unit requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. Six days after admission, he developed sudden severe hypoxemia, tachycardia, and hypotension requiring reinitiation of norepinephrine. POCUS demonstrated bilateral anterior A-lines, left femoral and popliteal deep vein thrombosis, and preserved right ventricular (RV) function without echocardiographic evidence of RV strain. Catheter-based pulmonary angiography confirmed subocclusive thrombosis involving segmental branches of the right middle and lower lobes, which was treated with mechanical thromboaspiration, followed by IVC filter placement because anticoagulation was initially contraindicated. Four days later, he developed a new episode of acute hypoxemia despite remaining hemodynamically stable. Repeat POCUS demonstrated a large mobile thrombus in transit within the right atrium. Subcostal longitudinal imaging of the IVC demonstrated a large elongated thrombus attached to the IVC filter, with a freely mobile portion extending into the right atrium. Urgent mechanical thrombectomy and IVC filter replacement were performed. The new filter was positioned approximately 2 cm below the confluence of the hepatic veins with the inferior vena cava. Approximately 24 h later, follow-up POCUS showed no evidence of new thrombus formation. More than 2 weeks after admission, following a follow-up brain CT showing no significant progression of the intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation with enoxaparin was initiated and progressively increased to a full therapeutic dose. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the value of POCUS for the prompt bedside recognition of an established and potentially life-threatening complication of IVC filter placement. Systematic bedside cardiac and venous ultrasound may identify thrombus propagation into the right atrium even in the absence of RV dilation or echocardiographic evidence of RV strain, facilitating timely endovascular intervention.

Although uncommon, filter thrombosis can result in thrombus propagation and potentially life-threatening embolic complications. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides a rapid bedside assessment of the heart, lungs, and may facilitate the prompt recognition of unexpected thromboembolic complications.

title: Noninvasive assessments for identifying peripheral artery disease described within guidelines, consensus, and best practice statements: A rapid systematic review.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects approximately 4% of adults and is associated with lower-limb pain, reduced function, ulceration, amputation, and an increased likelihood of cardiovascular events. Noninvasive vascular testing methods are essential for accurate diagnosis to enable clinicians to deliver appropriate management. Clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and best practice documents are commonly used to guide practice. The quality of these documents, how well they specify the populations requiring screening, assessment, and the most appropriate noninvasive tests to use when diagnosing PAD is currently unclear. This rapid systematic review identified 37 national and international guidelines, consensus statements, or best practice documents that included information on noninvasive assessments for PAD diagnosis published up to 2025. The quality of these documents was assessed using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation Instrument 2 or Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) appraisal checklist for textual evidence (policy/consensus guidelines), and scores varied substantially, with contemporary documents generally yielding higher scores. Common reasons for lower scores were a lack of systematic methods used to derive recommendations and inadequate engagement with key stakeholders, such as end-users. Within the documents, signs and symptoms of PAD consistently listed as indicators for further vascular assessment were intermittent claudication, rest pain, gangrene, and nonhealing wounds. Other prompts for vascular assessments were traditional cardiovascular risk factors, with some newer guidelines highlighting additional risk factors such as end-stage renal disease, First Nations ancestry, and lack of physical activity. There was varying guidance on the use and interpretation of the tests. Many documents did not consider the changes in diagnostic performance that occur in noninvasive tests in people with diabetes or renal disease. Some newer documents included clinical assessment pathways, which were considered beneficial in simplifying the assessment and interpretation process for clinicians. Although some high-quality documents with strong evidence-based recommendations were identified, there was a gap in comprehensive guidance that could be applied in a variety of settings and patient cohorts. Therefore, the development of an evidence-based, co-designed comprehensive guidance document for noninvasive vascular assessment is warranted.
englishSummary: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects approximately 4% of adults and is associated with lower-limb pain, reduced function, ulceration, amputation, and an increased likelihood of cardiovascular events. Noninvasive vascular testing methods are essential for accurate diagnosis to enable clinicians to deliver appropriate management. Clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and best practice documents are commonly used to guide practice.

title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups. RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR. METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs). RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies. CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses. METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes. CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.

title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial. METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed. RESULTS: interaction Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; P= 0.96). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications. title: Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline). RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121). CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

title: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension. METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality. CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

title: Can Outpatient Total Knee Arthroplasty Be Performed at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
abstract: BACKGROUND: Outpatient (same-day discharge) primary total knee arthroplasties (TKAs) have been recently popularized, but results from academic medical centers remain limited. Outpatient surgery shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. Meanwhile, surgeon reimbursements continue to decrease. We retrospectively evaluated 90-day rates of emergency room (ER) visits, reoperations, revisions, and incoming/outgoing postoperative patient touches associated with outpatient TKAs at our complex, academic, quaternary referral center. METHODS: At our institution, 1,787 outpatient primary TKAs were performed between 2019 and 2024 in 1,552 unique patients. The mean age was 65 years, 51% were women, the mean body mass index (BMI) was 33, the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2.4, and the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 1.5 (range, 0 to 10). Medical comorbidities, ER visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches within 90 days after TKA were collected. Univariate logistic regression analyses were completed. RESULTS: The rates of ER visits, reoperations, and revisions within 90 days of surgery were 8.5, 3.1, and 0.7%, respectively. Knees averaged nine postoperative touches, and total touches increased from 61 in 2019 to greater than 5,800 in 2024. The most common first-time ER visit reason was a medical issue unrelated to surgery (35%), followed by evaluation for venous thromboembolism (VTE; 29%). The actual VTE incidence was 0.6%. The most common reoperation was manipulation under anesthesia (MUA; incidence 1.5%). The 90-day periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) incidence was 0.7%, and all cases required reoperation or revision. Older age and increasing ASA score were significantly associated with risk of ER visits (odds ratio [OR] 1.2; P = 0.01 and OR 1.8; P < 0.001, respectively). Increasing CCI was significantly associated with risk of ER visits (OR 1.2; P = 0.001), revisions (OR 1.5; P = 0.001), and PJI (OR 1.3; P = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: We found a high rate of ER visits within 90 days after outpatient TKAs, with nearly 40% unattributable to surgery. Increasing age and comorbidities were associated with increased ER visit risk, and comorbidities also increased revision and PJI risk. Knees averaged nine non-clinic postoperative touches.

Outpatient surgery shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. Meanwhile, surgeon reimbursements continue to decrease.

title: Prognosis of Patients with Delayed Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Rupture after Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Multicentre Retrospective Study in France.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The majority of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) undergo endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture. METHODS: A multicentre retrospective study of patients who presented with ruptured AAA after successful EVAR between 2007 and 2022 at 22 academic hospitals was conducted. The index EVAR procedures were performed between 2002 and 2020. Data were extracted from electronic hospital records and computed tomography scans. Death during follow up was ascertained using the French register of deceased persons. Survival probabilities at 30, 90, and 365 days were estimated with Kaplan-Meier estimators. Cox proportional hazards survival regression was used to identify determinants associated with increased risk of death. RESULTS: One hundred and nine patients (96 men) were included, with a mean age of 79.1 ± 9 years at the time of rupture. The median time from index EVAR to rupture was 50 months (range 0 - 179 months). Sixty-seven patients had open surgery (of which 37% underwent suprarenal cross clamping), 39 received endovascular treatment, and three underwent hybrid repair. Overall mortality was 26.6% at thirty days, increasing to 33.9% at ninety days, and 41.3% at 1 year. Neither the type of endoleak nor the type of repair was significantly associated with risk of death during follow up. Post-operative complications were frequent, including renal complications (44.0%), major haemorrhage (22.9%), respiratory distress (19.3%), and mesenteric ischaemia (6%). CONCLUSION: This study presented a large multicentre series of patients treated for ruptured AAA after EVAR. Despite considerable progress in stent graft technology, EVAR offers little protection in the event of late rupture, even among patients with type II endoleak only. The mortality rate in this study is within the range of those published based on de novo AAA rupture.

Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture.

title: Leadership, Teamwork, and Healthcare Economics Training in Vascular Surgery Residency Programs: A National Cross-Specialty FREIDA Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare reported training in leadership, interprofessional teamwork, and healthcare economics among vascular surgery residency programs and 10 other surgical and procedural specialties. METHODS: We reviewed FREIDA educational-benefits data for 11 specialties on June 20, 2025, excluding programs without these data. Vascular surgery residency programs were compared with the highest-reporting specialty in each category and with the remaining 10 specialties combined using two-sided Fisher exact tests. RESULTS: Of 1,717 programs, 810 (47.2%) reported educational-benefits data, including 36 of 78 (46.2%) vascular surgery residency programs. Among these 36 programs, 13 (36.1%) reported leadership training, 20 (55.6%) formal interprofessional teamwork programs, 19 (52.8%) healthcare economics instruction, and 6 (16.7%) reported all three. Compared with the highest-reporting specialty, vascular surgery residency programs had lower reporting rates for leadership (36.1% vs 56.3% in obstetrics and gynecology; P = .030), teamwork (55.6% vs 80.2% in obstetrics and gynecology; P = .003), economics (52.8% vs 80.8% in interventional radiology; P = .009), and all three (16.7% vs 35.5% in obstetrics and gynecology; P = .033). Comparisons with the remaining 10 specialties combined were not statistically significant for leadership (36.1% vs 51.0%; P = .089), teamwork (55.6% vs 67.7%; P = .147), or economics (52.8% vs 59.7%; P = .488). CONCLUSION: Vascular surgery residency programs ranked among the lowest specialties in reported SBP-aligned training, with only 16.7% reporting all three domains. Although pooled comparisons were not statistically significant, these findings highlight an opportunity for specialty-wide standardization of SBP education.

title: PROphylactic use of closed incision negative Pressure wound thERapy for VASCular surgery groin incisions: recommendations from an international expert-based consensus (PROPER-VASC).
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to obtain experts' consensus and define recommendations regarding best clinical practices on the use of prophylactic close incision negative wound pressure therapy (ciNPWT) in patients undergoing groin incisions in vascular surgery METHODS: A modified Delphi consensus methodology was employed over three rounds, involving a panel of 20 experts, by using a four point likert scale. Statements that reached consensus at the first round were submitted to a second round, unmodified. Statements that failed the first round were adapted and proposed to the second and third rounds of judgment. Agreement and consistency derived from the three rounds were used to develop recommendations on the prophylactic use of ciNPWT on groin incisions after vascular operations. RESULTS: After three rounds, 3 statements were rejected, and 20 recommendations were made. Six received a Grade B consensus, and fourteen statements reached a Grade A consensus. Experts agree on the potential of ciNPWT in reducing superficial groin SSI in patients with high-risk features, which should consequently be treated with such technology routinely, contrary to standard-risk patients who would not benefit as much from ciNPWT dressings. Practical recommendations that reached consensus included the use of ciNPWT as soon as possible after surgery, possibly already in the operating theater, and devices should stay in place for 5-7 days. CONCLUSIONS: Inguinal ciNPWT should be used in patients at increased risk of SSI and wound dehiscence after vascular interventions to prevent superficial infections. Individualized risk assessment should be performed for each patient to guide decision-making and practical instructions for device management should be provided.
