title: Real-world safety of intrasaccular flow disruption for unruptured cerebral aneurysms: a multicenter analysis of on-label versus off-label aneurysm location treatment in the NeuroVascular Quality Initiative-Quality Outcomes Database registry.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Intrasaccular flow disruption (IFD) has been shown to be safe and efficacious in the treatment of unruptured cerebral aneurysms. However, previous studies were typically performed at large-volume centers, were carefully curated, and devices were used in on-label locations. The purpose of this study was to examine IFD safety using real-world data, in both on-label and off-label aneurysm locations. METHODS: The NeuroVascular Quality Initiative-Quality Outcomes Database registry was analyzed for all unruptured aneurysms treated with IFD. On-label versus off-label treatment locations were compared. The primary outcome was the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score at discharge. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative complications, mRS score at last follow-up, and aneurysm occlusion status. Direct comparisons between groups were performed first, and results were confirmed with propensity score matching. RESULTS: There were 329 (82%) on-label aneurysm location treatments and 72 (18%) off-label treatments. The mean patient age was 64.6 years (range 27-86 years). On-label aneurysms were slightly larger than off-label aneurysms, with a mean maximum dimension of 6.9 mm versus 6.2 mm (p = 0.041). Otherwise, there were no significant differences in group characteristics. The mean follow-up was 512 days. There was no significant difference for the primary outcome of mRS score at discharge (mRS score ≤ 2: 94.1% on-label vs 97.5% off-label, p = 0.615). There were no significant differences for secondary outcomes including any intraoperative complication (3.6% vs 2.8%, p > 0.999), mRS score at last follow-up, and aneurysm occlusion status at discharge (Raymond-Roy class 1: 54.1% vs 56%, p = 0.929). There were significant missing data for occlusion status at the last follow-up, precluding analysis. Propensity score matching yielded 68 patients in each group and confirmed no significant differences for primary and secondary outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: This largest-to-date prospective registry study supports the overall safety of IFD treatment for unruptured cerebral aneurysms in both on-label and off-label aneurysm locations. Questions remain regarding long-term efficacy due to current follow-up data limitations in the registry.

title: Pediatric cerebral arteriovenous malformation: an institutional experience from 25 years of treatment.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: In pediatric cerebral arteriovenous malformation (AVM), the long-term outcome data are scarce. The aim of this study was to analyze the clinical and radiological long-term outcomes from an institutional experience of children and adolescents treated for AVM over 25 years. METHODS: The authors reviewed clinical and radiological data from a consecutive series of patients (age ≤ 18 years) treated for AVM at a single institution from 2000 to 2024, with at least 1 year of follow-up. RESULTS: Overall, 96 patients were treated for AVM (48 males and 48 females, mean age 12.8 ± 4.8 years). Spetzler-Martin grades were I in 18 patients (19.4%), II in 33 (35.5%), and III in 30 (32.3%), and 14.6% of patients had an infratentorial location. Overall, 8.3% of patients were asymptomatic and 54.2% presented with hemorrhage. Moreover, 11.5% of patients experienced new or repeated hemorrhage during the initial observation or ongoing treatment. The stand-alone treatment was microsurgery in 38.5% of patients, radiosurgery in 28.1%, and embolization in 2.1%, while 9.4% of patients were treated conservatively. The treatment was multimodal in 21.9% and repeated in 49.4% of patients. The obliteration rate in patients with completed treatment (n = 75) was 80% (higher in those presenting with hemorrhage: 91.1% vs 63.3%, p = 0.003). The obliteration rate was 88.6% after microsurgery and 57.9% after radiosurgery (higher in the hemorrhagic group: 87.5% vs 36.4%, p = 0.026). Recurrence occurred in 8.3% of patients at a median of 60 months (range 36-68 months), and following microsurgery in all cases. A favorable clinical outcome (modified Rankin Scale scores 0-2) was achieved in 83.2% of patients, nonsignificantly less in those with hemorrhagic presentation (76.5% vs 90.9%, p = 0.061). The overall mortality rate was 5.3%, without a significant difference between the hemorrhagic and nonhemorrhagic groups. Hydrocephalus, hemorrhage volume, nidus size, infratentorial location, and Spetzler-Martin, supplementary, and combined grades were negative predictors of a good outcome in the univariate analysis, with the combined grade being the strongest predictor. Hemorrhage was a strong predictor of obliteration in the multivariate model, whereas radiosurgery and the number of treatments were predictors of nonobliteration. CONCLUSIONS: Although more than half of children and adolescents with AVM presented with hemorrhage, most patients had a favorable clinical outcome. In our experience, microsurgery and radiosurgery resulted in the highest obliteration rates, particularly in hemorrhagic cases, while the role of endovascular treatment was only supplementary.

The aim of this study was to analyze the clinical and radiological long-term outcomes from an institutional experience of children and adolescents treated for AVM over 25 years. METHODS: The authors reviewed clinical and radiological data from a consecutive series of patients (age ≤ 18 years) treated for AVM at a single institution from 2000 to 2024, with at least 1 year of follow-up.

title: Association Between Intradialytic Foot Temperature Gradients and Severe Peripheral Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis: Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD. METHODS: In this prospective observational study, we recruited 109 patients undergoing chronic maintenance HD. Skin temperatures were monitored continuously at the instep and sole during HD sessions using wearable sensors (Temp Pal, iWEECARE Co, Ltd), which are wireless, nanochip-based mHealth thermometers with ±0.05 °C accuracy. The diagnostic performance of temperature parameters, specifically the temperature difference between the wrist and foot at the end of HD, was evaluated against vascular duplex ultrasound (DUS). Severe PAD was defined as abnormal (monophasic or absent) flow in the distal posterior tibial artery (PTA) or anterior tibial artery (ATA). RESULTS: Patients with abnormal tibial flow on DUS exhibited significantly different temperature gradients between the wrist and foot at the end of dialysis compared to those with normal flow. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that the wrist-foot temperature difference at the sole effectively discriminated abnormal ATA flow (area under the curve [AUC] 64.5%, 95% CI 57.8%-70.9%) and abnormal PTA flow (AUC 62.0%, 95% CI 55.2%-68.5%). Notably, an instep wrist-foot temperature difference cutoff of -2.2 °C or less yielded a specificity of 97.6% (95% CI 94.0%-99.3%) for detecting abnormal PTA flow. CONCLUSIONS: Intradialytic foot temperature monitoring, particularly the temperature gradient between the wrist and foot, significantly correlates with severe tibial artery flow abnormalities. This method offers an accessible, noninvasive screening adjunct to the ABI for detecting severe PAD in the HD population. These findings indicate an association rather than a standalone diagnostic test; given the modest discriminative ability, external validation is warranted.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD.

title: Evaluating the Performance of Large Language Models in Vascular Surgery Cases: Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are increasingly used by clinicians, yet their accuracy, safety, and consistency in clinical cases remain poorly defined. Most studies assess LLMs using multiple-choice questions rather than free-response reasoning. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the performance and safety of 3 widely used LLMs in realistic vascular surgery scenarios in key domains such as diagnosis, investigation, and multidisciplinary and multimodal management. The secondary objective of this study was to evaluate the safety of the models' outputs. METHODS: t A total of 42 fictitious vascular cases across 5 major pathologies (acute limb ischemia [ALI], aortopathy, chronic limb ischemia, diabetic foot infection, and extracranial cerebrovascular disease) were independently entered into GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 using standardized prompts. Each model answered structured questions covering diagnosis, investigation, and management (both operative and nonoperative). Responses were scored out of 20 by a panel using a predefined rubric. Each plan's overall safety was separately assessed. Comparative analyses used 2-tailedtests, ANOVA, and multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: P P P P Mean composite scores by model were 86.5% for ChatGPT, 83.5% for Gemini, and 88.0% for Claude, whereas scores by disease were 82.7% for ALI, 83.8% for aortopathy, 85.9% for chronic limb ischemia, 86.1% for diabetic foot infection, and 80.7% for extracranial cerebrovascular disease (>.05 in each case). Unsafe plans were generated in 11.9%, 23.8%, and 7.1% of cases by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, respectively. On multivariable analysis, independent predictors of unsafe outputs were lower composite score (odds ratio [OR] 0.471, 95% CI 0.306-0.722;=.001), higher word count (OR 1.003, 95% CI 1.001-1.005;=.001), and ALI (OR 20.9, 95% CI 3.79-61.8;<.001). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate LLMs' promise in managing routine vascular surgery cases. However, their inconsistent safety profiles and ethical limitations preclude unsupervised clinical use. Rigorous specialty-specific validation is essential before they may be integrated into routine practice.

title: Effects of angiotensin receptor blockers on aortic growth and clinical events in Marfan syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is a major cause of aortic dissection and premature mortality in Marfan syndrome. Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome. We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, and Web of Science through February 1, 2025. Acute aortic dissection and all-cause mortality were the primary outcomes. Binary outcomes were analyzed using both Mantel-Haenszel common-effect (MH-CE) and inverse-variance random-effects (IV-RE) models. For outcomes with an event incidence below 10% in every contributing study, the MH-CE estimate was emphasized and the IV-RE estimate was treated as a sensitivity analysis. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using IV-RE models. All analyses were conducted with the meta package in R (v4.3.2). Seven randomized controlled trials involving 1522 patients with Marfan syndrome were included in the main analysis. For acute aortic dissection, the MH-CE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·24-1·59) and the IV-RE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·20-1·92). For all-cause mortality, the corresponding estimates were RR 0·53 (95% CI 0·17-1·64) and RR 0·58 (95% CI 0·16-2·07). Confidence intervals were wide and crossed unity. ARBs were associated with less aortic-root growth measured by MRI (MD - 0·48 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·89 to - 0·08) and by echocardiography over 3 years (MD - 0·51 mm/3 years, 95% CI - 0·85 to - 0·17), whereas annual echocardiographic measurement showed no significant difference (MD - 0·06 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·22 to 0·10). No significant effect was observed on ascending-aortic diameter, aortic Z-score at 3 years, aortic surgery, or serious adverse events. No statistically significant effect modification was detected in exploratory subgroup analyses. In patients with Marfan syndrome, ARB therapy was associated with small reductions in aortic-root growth in selected imaging analyses but did not significantly reduce acute aortic dissection or all-cause mortality. Sparse events, wide confidence intervals, and limited follow-up preclude firm conclusions regarding clinical benefit. Adequately powered, long-term trials with standardized imaging and clinical outcomes are required.

Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome.

title: Percutaneous Transmural Arterial Bypass for Recurrent Superficial Femoral Artery Chronic Total Occlusion.
abstract: IMAGE: Fluoroscopic angiography and duplex ultrasound. CASE SUMMARY: A 73-year-old man with Rutherford class IV chronic limb-threatening ischemia had a recurrent, heavily calcified superficial femoral artery chronic total occlusion despite multiple prior endovascular interventions. After declining surgical bypass, he underwent percutaneous transmural arterial bypass using covered stent grafts routed through the femoral venous pathway. Inline flow was restored without immediate complications. At 3 months, duplex ultrasound demonstrated bypass patency, and rest pain had resolved. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Percutaneous transmural arterial bypass may offer an alternative for carefully selected patients with complex femoropopliteal disease when conventional endovascular treatment has failed, and surgical bypass is declined.

title: Micrococcus luteus Streptococcus mitis Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated Withandin a 77-year-Old Man.
abstract: Micrococcus luteus Streptococcus mitis BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identifiedand, rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

title: Untargeted Plasma Metabolomics Reveals Molecular Subtypes Associated with Reintervention Risk in Peripheral Artery Disease after Revascularization.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity after revascularization that is incompletely explained by conventional severity indicators. We performed untargeted plasma LC-MS metabolomics in 175 PAD patients undergoing revascularization and applied variability-based feature selection, unsupervised clustering, pathway and chemical-class analyses, survival modeling, and metabolite prioritization. Three metabolically defined molecular subtypes were identified: redox protective (n = 93), metabolic burden (n = 72), and renal dysfunction (n = 10). Compared to the redox-protective subtype, the metabolic-burden subtype showed higher risks of composite adverse outcomes, reintervention, and major adverse cardiovascular events, accompanied by acylcarnitine accumulation, fatty-acyl enrichment, and COX-prostaglandin-related inflammatory signaling. Secondary clustering of high-risk patients identified a subgroup with increased reintervention risk, despite no corresponding increase in Rutherford classification or ankle-brachial index severity, characterized by sphingomyelin, diglyceride, and thromboxane/leukotriene-related lipid mediator signatures. A five-metabolite score was associated with reintervention risk and showed numerically higher apparent discrimination than the original and expanded clinical models. These findings establish an untargeted metabolomics framework for molecular subtyping of PAD after revascularization and nominate metabolic phenotypes for future validation.

title: Saddle pulmonary embolism and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in acute pancreatitis: a case report.
abstract: Acute pancreatitis causes severe inflammation, predisposing patients to thromboembolism, which can be further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (HITT). A 47-year-old diabetic male patient with severe acute pancreatitis developed a massive saddle pulmonary embolism. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) treatment triggered a deep vein thrombosis, and a severe platelet drop (28 × 109/l), confirming HITT. Due to a refractory response to fondaparinux, the patient was successfully switched to direct oral anticoagulation with dabigatran etexilate (150 mg twice daily). This led to rapid platelet normalization and clinical stability. When standard parenteral treatments fail in HITT, direct oral anticoagulants like dabigatran offer an effective alternative strategy.

title: Personalized anticoagulation and drug monitoring for pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism in hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency.
abstract: Pregnant women with hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency (ATD) are at significantly increased thrombotic risk. We present the case of a woman with four consecutive pregnancy losses due to venous thromboembolism (VTE), subsequently diagnosed with type IIa hereditary ATD. Type IIa ATD is exceptionally rare. The principal therapeutic challenge lies in the absence of established guidelines regarding optimal anticoagulant selection, dosing strategies, and monitoring approaches for such patients, contributing to treatment failure in her first four pregnancies. The patient was referred to our institution before her fifth conception. Preconception intervention began, and we instituted low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) therapy, with dose titration guided by thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT) and anti-Xa activity levels. This regimen demonstrated safety and efficacy, achieving a maximum nadroparin dose of 10 250 IU twice daily. Under close pharmacotherapeutic monitoring by a clinical pharmacist using this individualized protocol, the patient achieved a successful term delivery and was discharged.

title: Perioperative combined intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid does not increase venous thromboembolism risk after total knee arthroplasty in plateau areas: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: After total knee arthroplasty (TKA), rivaroxaban is often used to prevent venous thromboembolism (VTE), while tranexamic acid (TXA) is used to reduce perioperative bleeding. However, plateau hypoxia may affect coagulation. We assessed whether combined intravenous and intra-articular TXA increases VTE risk in plateau TKA patients. This single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, pilot controlled trial was conducted at altitude greater than 3500 m. Fifty unilateral TKA patients were randomized to experimental (intravenous + intra-articular TXA) or control (intravenous TXA alone). All received rivaroxaban for 14 days. Primary outcome was new-onset DVT (deep vein thrombosis) or PE (Pulmonary Embolism) at day 3; secondary outcomes included thromboelastography (TEG) and coagulation parameters at 6 h, 1, 2, and 3 days. No VTE occurred in either group. Nonthrombotic ultrasound findings (intermuscular vein dilation with blood stasis) were observed in 9/25 (36%) of the experimental group and 13/25 (52%) of the control group, with no between-group difference (P = 0.254). TEG parameters showed no significant differences, except for a transiently lower D-dimer in the experimental group on day 1 (P < 0.001), though clinical relevance is unclear. Hb and Hct declined less in the experimental group at all time points (P < 0.05), suggesting reduced blood loss. In plateau TKA patients, adding intra-articular TXA to intravenous TXA did not increase short-term VTE risk. These preliminary findings suggest combined TXA with rivaroxaban may be well tolerated in this population.

title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes. OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment. RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N  = 10, sham: N  = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P  = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P  = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P  = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication ( N  = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P  = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P  = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P  < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN. CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.

title: Dynamic infrared thermography for quantitative assessment of peripheral microcirculation: models, metrics, and clinical translation.
abstract: Peripheral microcirculation assessment is critical for understanding tissue oxygenation, thermoregulation and metabolic function, but conventional techniques such as laser Doppler perfusion imaging and indocyanine green angiography are constrained by contact requirements, invasiveness or limited field of view. Dynamic infrared thermography (DIRT) provides a non-contact method that quantifies microvascular function by analyzing skin temperature recovery following a controlled thermal challenge, thereby offering functional insights into perfusion dynamics beyond static anatomical imaging. This narrative review synthesizes the bioheat models, quantitative metrics and clinical evidence supporting DIRT for peripheral microcirculation assessment. Following PRISMA-adapted searches, 71 studies and key modeling papers with dynamic protocols and perfusion-related quantitative endpoints were included. Bioheat transfer models, from the Pennes formulation to non-Fourier dual-phase-lag extensions, enable inverse estimation of perfusion parameters from temperature time-series. Validated metrics include rewarming rate, thermal time constant, area under the temperature vs time curve, maximum recovery percentage and spatial hotspot detection for perforator mapping. These parameters correlate strongly with laser Doppler and laser speckle contrast imaging, particularly in Raynaud's phenomenon (RP), and achieve high diagnostic performance for preoperative perforator mapping and postoperative flap monitoring in reconstructive microsurgery. Evidence is most mature in surgical applications, supporting DIRT as a repeatable adjunct for planning and surveillance. In RP, peripheral arterial disease and diabetic foot disease, DIRT metrics detect microvascular impairment and show promise for early ulceration risk prediction, although heterogeneity in protocols and scarcity of large-scale outcome data hinder broader adoption. As a conclusion, DIRT offers practical advantages of portability, negligible consumable cost and absence of contrast or ionizing radiation. Its transition to routine quantitative clinical use requires standardized acquisition protocols, integration of advanced signal processing and machine learning, and adequately powered multicenter trials linking metrics to patient-centered outcomes across populations.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Two-Stage Machine Learning Multivariable Model to Support Clinical Decision-Making in Thrombophilia Management.
abstract: Thrombophilia is a disease characterized by an increased risk of venous thromboembolism. Diagnosing and treating thrombophilic patients requires the nuanced interpretation of a great number of medical data. In this single-center, retrospective study, we evaluated the use of a two-stage machine learning (ML) model to predict the thrombophilia risk category and subsequent anticoagulation recommendation.The model was trained and tested using clinical and laboratory data obtained from 496 patients who underwent a complete thrombophilia work-up at the University Hospital Bonn between 2019 and 2024. The hybrid nature of the diagnostic categories, which combine ordinal classes including thrombophilia diagnosis, severity, and treatment recommendations and categorical classes (e.g., antiphospholipid syndrome), necessitated a two-stage approach. First, XGBClassifier was used to distinguish between the two classes, and then an ordinal-specific XGBOrdinalV2 model was used. Performance was assessed across 100 random 80/20 train-test splits.For exact class prediction (primary analysis), mean macro-averaged sensitivity, specificity, and precision were 58, 91, and 56.2% for diagnosis and 54.4, 91.3, and 58.5% for treatment. Performance was highest for frequent classes and poor for rare high-risk classes. When predictions within one adjacent class were accepted (secondary analysis), macro-averaged sensitivity was 91.9 and 86.2%, respectively. Antiphospholipid antibody status, age at first thrombosis, and unprovoked thrombosis were the most influential features for diagnosis. Model predictions and physician decisions were concordant in 395 of 496 patients (79.6%).This study demonstrates that ML models can support standardized thrombophilia management and improve diagnostic accuracy. However, external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

Diagnosing and treating thrombophilic patients requires the nuanced interpretation of a great number of medical data. title: Discontinuation of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors before non-cardiac surgery: a meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The best management approach for renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitor use before surgery is controversial. Some studies have suggested that continuation could increase the risk of clinically significant peri-operative hypotension and, thus, organ injury. By contrast, others believe that withholding them significantly increases the risk of severe hypertension and heart failure. To determine the most effective strategy, this systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials compared discontinuation vs continuation of RAS inhibitors in patients undergoing non-cardiac and non-vascular surgeries. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) databases were searched for randomized controlled trials that compared discontinuation vs continuation of RAS inhibitors in patients undergoing non-cardiac and non-vascular surgery. RESULTS: Five randomized controlled trials (n = 10 773 patients; 5388 randomized to discontinuation) were included. Discontinuation of an RAS inhibitor probaby reduced peri-operative hypotension (27.66% vs 34.06%; risk ratio [RR] 0.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.73-0.89; moderate certainty). The evidence is very uncertain about effects on peri-operative hypertension (9.46% vs 8.05%; RR 1.38, 95% CI 0.66-2.89; very low certainty). For major clinical outcomes, discontinuation suggested little to no difference in acute kidney injury (10.45% vs 10.69%; RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.66-1.45; low certainty), acute heart failure (5.38% vs 5.32%; RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.76-1.31; low certainty), myocardial infarction (1.22% vs 1.00%; RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.60-2.39; low certainty), stroke (0.42% vs 0.40%; RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.56-1.93; low certainty), and arrhythmias (1.80% vs 1.40%; RR 1.28, 95% CI 0.69-2.38; low certainty). CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that discontinuation of RAS inhibitors is likely to reduce peri-operative hypotension in patients undergoing non-cardiac, non-vascular surgery, but the evidence is very uncertain about effects on peri-operative hypertension and major clinical outcomes.

title: Safety and efficacy of cerebral embolic protection devices during TAVI: a meta-analysis and sequence analysis of trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral embolic protection (CEP) devices have been developed to reduce postoperative neurological outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI); however, their effectiveness remains controversial. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of CEP use during TAVI on the occurrence in clinical outcomes. METHODS: Databases were used to search for randomized clinical trials. The occurrence of all strokes, of disabling strokes specifically, transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), all-cause mortality, and vascular complications were analyzed. Conventional meta-analysis was conducted using fixed-effects modeling and trial sequential analysis (TSA: type I error of 5%, power of 90%). The systematic review protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420251081075). RESULTS: p p p In total, eight clinical trials were included, gathering 11,589 patients randomized between those who used the devices (5,943) and those who did not (5,646). The meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between CEP use and reduced odds of all-cause stroke (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.73-1.15, = 0.46) and disabling stroke (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.57-1.13, = 0.20). The sequential analysis identified a lack of evidence for all strokes (required sample size [rSS] = 38,626; 10.53%), disabling strokes (rSS = 59,732; 17.05%). In terms of mortality, there was no significance in the use of devices (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.71-1.69, = 0.69), reaching evidence for support (rSS = 7,053; 42.25%). CONCLUSION: The data on the use of CEP is insufficient to support meta-analytic conclusions regarding cerebrovascular outcomes. Nevertheless, TSA demonstrated evidence supporting futility regarding mortality reduction.

title: Efficacy of tranexamic acid in reducing perioperative blood loss and transfusion requirements following limb-salvage surgery for bone tumors: A randomized controlled trial.
abstract: BackgroundLimb salvage surgery with endoprosthetic reconstruction for malignant bone tumors is frequently associated with substantial perioperative blood loss and high transfusion requirements. Although tranexamic acid (TXA) has demonstrated efficacy in reducing blood loss in total joint arthroplasty, high-level evidence supporting its use in orthopaedic oncology remains limited.MethodsWe conducted a prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial between April 2023 and September 2025. Thirty-six patients undergoing tumor resection and endoprosthetic reconstruction of the femur(Proximal/distal/total), proximal tibia, or proximal humerus were randomized to receive either intravenous TXA (15 mg/kg at induction; n = 18) or placebo (n = 18). The primary outcome was calculated total blood loss at 72 hours using the hemoglobin balance method. Secondary outcomes included transfusion requirements, postoperative hemoglobin concentration, drain output, hospital stay, wound complications, and thromboembolic events. All patients completed a minimum follow-up of six weeks.ResultsMean calculated blood loss at 72 hours was lower in the TXA group than in the control group (995 ± 324 mL versus 1708 ± 508 mL; mean difference 713 mL; p < 0.001). Patients receiving TXA required fewer packed red blood cell transfusions (1.1 ± 0.7 versus 1.7 ± 0.7 units; mean difference 0.6 units; p = 0.01). Postoperative hemoglobin concentration was higher in the TXA group (9.3 ± 1.1 versus 8.7 ± 0.9 g/dL), although this difference was not significant (p = 0.073). No differences were observed in drain output, wound complications, or hospital stay. No symptomatic deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism occurred in either group.ConclusionIn this single-center randomized controlled trial, tranexamic acid was associated with reduced calculated total blood loss at 72 hours. However, the relatively small sample size limits conclusions regarding uncommon adverse events. Larger multicenter randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these findings and further evaluate safety across diverse orthopaedic oncology settings.

title: Urgent Reno-Hepatic Artery Bypass for Acute on Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia Following Robotic Low Anterior Resection for Rectal Cancer in a Patient with Severe Stenosis of the Hepatosplenomesenteric Trunk.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute mesenteric ischemia, including acute exacerbation of chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI), is a life-threatening condition associated with a 50% in-hospital mortality risk and requires immediate diagnosis, revascularization, and resection of necrotic organs. In colorectal surgery, mesenteric artery stenosis can lead to anastomotic leakage which increases morbidity and mortality. Here, we describe a case of acute exacerbation of CMI caused by severe stenosis of the hepatosplenomesenteric trunk (HSMT) and ligation of the left colic and inferior mesenteric arteries in an earlier rectal surgery that was successfully treated with urgent reno-hepatic artery bypass. CASE PRESENTATION: An 80-year-old woman was referred to our department with acute exacerbation of CMI after multiple procedures for rectal cancer. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed severe stenosis with calcification at the origin of the HSMT and hypoenhancement of the right hepatic lobe, spleen, and small intestine. Percutaneous antegrade endovascular stenting failed because the lesion was severely calcified. We opted to perform urgent open surgery, including revascularization and resection of the necrotic organs. A bypass from the right renal artery to the proper hepatic artery was selected because of the high risk of failure associated with retrograde open mesenteric stenting, the limited length of available saphenous vein, the risk of anastomotic failure secondary to infection, the patient's poor general condition, and the degree of calcification precluding aortoiliac clamping. Postoperatively, the patient developed Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and disseminated intravascular coagulation, both of which were successfully managed and resolved in the ICU. On POD 24, the patient underwent duodeno-jejunal anastomosis, ileostomy closure, and colostomy. The patient tolerated oral intake well 80 days after arterial bypass surgery and was discharged on POD 147 on single antiplatelet therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Although hepato-renal artery bypass is typically used for renal revascularization, reno-hepatic bypass can be useful for mesenteric revascularization in patients with anatomical variations, peritonitis, or severe aortoiliac calcification.

title: Combined antegrade-retrograde technique in urgent carotid stenting for true lumen compression after total arch replacement.
abstract: Type A aortic dissection extending into the carotid arteries with true lumen compression poses a significant risk of cerebral hypoperfusion and neurological sequelae. This case report describes an elderly patient who developed an extension of the right common carotid artery dissection with associated true lumen compression immediately following total arch replacement for acute Type A aortic dissection. Urgent carotid stenting was performed using a combined antegrade-retrograde approach (trans carotid and trans radial approach) to restore blood flow. Postprocedural imaging confirmed patency without major complications. This technique highlights a viable salvage strategy for managing complex aortic dissections when traditional methods fail. A literature review discusses the combined antegrade-retrograde approach used in urgent carotid stenting, as well as the advantages of ultrasound in selecting the true lumen and its minimally invasive nature.

title: Hybrid Occipital Artery-AICA Bypass Followed by Endovascular Embolization for a Radiation-Induced Dissecting AICA Aneurysm in a Pediatric Patient.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE: Pediatric anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) aneurysms are rare; radiation-associated dissecting lesions require exclusion without compromising brainstem or cerebellar perforators. CLINICAL PRESENTATION: A 13-year-old boy developed a progressively enlarging right AICA a2 dissecting aneurysm after cranial irradiation for pineal nongerminomatous germ cell tumor. Because direct clipping or isolated parent vessel occlusion was considered high risk, he underwent occipital artery-AICA a3 bypass followed by endovascular coil embolization in a single hybrid session. Dual arterial access enabled transradial vertebral artery treatment and transfemoral angiographic bypass assessment. Postoperative MRI showed a small transient cerebellar ischemic lesion that resolved within 2 weeks. At 2 months, the patient was neurologically intact with patent bypass and no aneurysm recurrence. CONCLUSION: Hybrid occipital artery-AICA bypass followed by endovascular embolization is a feasible flow-preserving option for selected pediatric AICA aneurysms requiring distal perfusion preservation.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Rivaroxaban versus LMWH Thromboprophylaxis Following Gynecologic Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Comparison Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of rivaroxaban vs low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic cancer surgery. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality. A multivariable logistic regression model was used to adjust for potential confounding factors. RESULTS: A total of 250 women were included, 134 received rivaroxaban and 116 received LMWH for postoperative thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic malignancy-related surgery. After adjusting for potential confounding factors using multivariable logistic regression, the 30-day VTE and bleeding events showed no significant differences between the rivaroxaban group and the LMWH groups. There were no cases of 30-day readmission related to surgery, no 30-day mortality, and no all-cause mortality during the 1-year follow-up. Notably, all distal DVT events in both groups were calf muscular vein thromboses. During the 1-year follow-up, no patients were rehospitalized or died due to VTE. CONCLUSION: We observed no significant differences in short- and long-term outcomes between rivaroxaban and LMWH after gynecologic malignancy surgery. Given the retrospective design and limited number of events, these results should be interpreted with caution, and prospective randomized studies are warranted.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality.

title: Pulmonary Artery Interventional Thrombectomy Stent System: Combined Application of Stent and Negative Pressure Aspiration.
abstract: This protocol describes a pulmonary artery thrombectomy technique that combines stent deployment and negative pressure aspiration to achieve rapid thrombus removal and restore pulmonary arterial perfusion. Prolonged obstruction may lead to right heart dysfunction and hemodynamic instability. The pulmonary artery thrombectomy stent system provides a rapid approach to thrombus removal and restoration of pulmonary perfusion, thereby alleviating respiratory distress and hypoxemia while reducing pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular strain. This technique is applicable for patients with intermediate- to high-risk pulmonary embolism, particularly those with contraindications to thrombolysis. Preoperative computed tomography imaging revealed pulmonary artery emboli involving both the left and right pulmonary arteries and their branches. Following thrombectomy using the pulmonary artery interventional thrombectomy stent system, postoperative imaging confirmed complete clearance of the thrombi and full restoration of pulmonary artery blood flow.

title: Development and Temporal Validation of a Thromboelastography-Based Nomogram for Queensland-Defined High Thrombotic Risk in Postpartum Women.
abstract: This study developed and temporally validated a nomogram that integrates thromboelastography (TEG) and maternal clinical factors to identify women classified as having high thrombotic risk according to the 2020 Queensland Clinical Guideline at postpartum reassessment after 24 h. The derivation cohort included 447 women who delivered at Foshan Women and Children Hospital between January 1, 2021, and December 27, 2022; 346 had Queensland scores of 0-2 and 101 had scores of ≥3. A same-center temporal validation cohort included 207 women who delivered between December 28, 2022, and February 14, 2025. Candidate clinical and TEG variables were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, and model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, and decision curve analysis. The final model retained hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, maternal age, current body mass index, native-cup TEG reaction time (R), and 24-h postpartum blood loss. Discrimination was acceptable in the derivation cohort (area under the curve [AUC], 0.791; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.737-0.845; sensitivity, 70.3%; specificity, 77.2%) and good in the temporal validation cohort (AUC, 0.847; 95% CI, 0.771-0.923; sensitivity, 75.8%; specificity, 85.6%). The model estimates Queensland-defined high thrombotic risk rather than objectively confirmed venous thromboembolism. It may support simplified postpartum reassessment after the first 24 h, but multicenter validation against objectively confirmed thrombotic outcomes is required before claims regarding event prediction or clinical implementation can be made.

title: Kidney Allograft Salvage by Autotransplantation for a Suspected Infectious Arterial Pseudoaneurysm in a Pediatric Recipient.
abstract: 2 Transplant renal artery pseudoaneurysm is a rare complication following kidney transplantation. Noninfected pseudoaneurysms are increasingly managed with endovascular intervention; however, infected pseudoaneurysms often require surgical resection or transplant nephrectomy for definitive management. We report the case of a 14-year-old female kidney transplant recipient with a neurogenic bladder who developed recurrent UTIs and bacteremia. The patient was diagnosed with a 3.0 × 2.8 cm renal artery pseudoaneurysm. After a course of antibiotics, she underwent resection of the pseudoaneurysm and an involved segment of the right external iliac artery, followed by kidney autotransplantation to a deceased donor iliac artery interposition graft. Final cultures were negative for bacterial or fungal growth. Six years later, the patient remains off dialysis with a serum creatinine of 2.08 mg/dL (eGFR 34 mL/min/1.73m). A review of the literature suggests that, in carefully selected recipients, excision of renal transplant pseudoaneurysms with renal autotransplantation can allow for allograft salvage.

Noninfected pseudoaneurysms are increasingly managed with endovascular intervention; however, infected pseudoaneurysms often require surgical resection or transplant nephrectomy for definitive management. We report the case of a 14-year-old female kidney transplant recipient with a neurogenic bladder who developed recurrent UTIs and bacteremia.

title: In Vitro Passive Sealing Stent-Grafts for Chimney Endovascular Repair:Examination and a Japanese Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (JAAAs) present with a short infrarenal neck that does not permit standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). The AFX VELA cuff extension with its endoskeletal architecture may reduce type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) through passive sealing. We examined this hypothesis using a double-chimney benchtop model and a clinical cohort treated with VELA-based chimney EVAR (ChEVAR). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A benchtop model compared gutter leakage volumes among VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3 (5 trials per device). A retrospective single-centre cohort (January 2018-April 2024) included consecutive JAAA patients undergoing VELA-based ChEVAR with ≥12-month follow-up. Postoperative computed tomographic (CT) morphometry compared seal-zone geometry across the 3 platforms. RESULTS: In the benchtop model, VELA showed a median gutter leakage of 5.0 mL/min (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-11.0), whereas both comparators exceeded 500 mL/min and were right-censored. In the clinical cohort, 20 patients (55% male; median age 80.0 years) underwent ChEVAR for JAAAs with a median diameter of 53.5 mm and infrarenal neck length of 5.0 mm. Clinically successful sac exclusion was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95%). Intraoperative TIaEL occurred in 5 patients: 1 major endoleak was sealed with adjunctive gutter coil embolisation, and 4 minor endoleaks resolved spontaneously on the 1-month CT angiogram. Over a median follow-up of 36.5 months, no persistent TIaEL was detected on follow-up imaging, and no chimney stent-graft (SG) occlusion occurred. One patient (5%) required an aortic-related reintervention for a type Ib endoleak. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decreased by ≥20% in 9 patients (45%), and 1 started dialysis at 4 years. On postoperative CT morphometry, relative gutter area was lowest with VELA, intermediate with Endurant II and highest with Excluder C3; circumferential apposition followed the inverse pattern. CONCLUSION: In the benchtop model, VELA produced consistently lower leakage than both comparators, with concordant CT morphometric evidence consistent with a passive sealing mechanism. In this cohort, VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%) with no persistent TIaEL and no chimney SG occlusion. These findings support the feasibility of VELA-based ChEVAR when FEVAR is unavailable; multicentre prospective validation is required. CLINICAL IMPACT: Persistent type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) is a principal limitation of chimney EVAR (ChEVAR) compared with fenestrated EVAR (FEVAR). We report short-to mid-term outcomes of ChEVAR using the AFX VELA cuff extension, whose endoskeletal architecture is designed to promote passive sealing. Postoperative CT morphometry comparing the 3 devices (VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3) showed a smaller relative gutter area and higher circumferential apposition with VELA, paralleling the benchtop pattern. VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%), without persistent TIaEL detected on follow-up imaging. VELA-based ChEVAR appears feasible when FEVAR is unavailable; however, multicentre validation is required.

The AFX VELA cuff extension with its endoskeletal architecture may reduce type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) through passive sealing. We examined this hypothesis using a double-chimney benchtop model and a clinical cohort treated with VELA-based chimney EVAR (ChEVAR).

title: Technical Feasibility and Outcomes of t-Branch Proximal Shortening in Urgent Complex Aortic Repair.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Branched endovascular repair has shown consistently good outcomes, being sometimes the only available endovascular solution for aortic emergencies. However, in cases of limited proximal extension of the disease, such as juxtarenal or pararenal aneurysms, branched endografts usually cover a greater extent of the aorta than needed to establish a seal zone, thus increasing the risk for spinal cord ischemia (SCI) by unnecessarily covering segmental arteries.Our objective is to analyze a series of patients who underwent proximal shortening of an off-the-shelf (OTS) branched endograft to limit aortic coverage and preserve segmental arteries. METHODS: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) with a shortened t-Branch, through the removal of the first stent row, from April 2020 to March 2026.Perioperative technical success and complications were evaluated. Primary endpoints were technical success. Secondary endpoints were 30-day mortality, SCI, assessment of number of saved segmental arteries, and endograft migration at follow-up. RESULTS: Fifteen patients underwent BEVAR with a shortened t-Branch endograft. All were urgencies, 60% being ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs). Thirteen (86%) cases were juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysms, and 3 (20%) had a previous endovascular aortic repair. In all cases, the proximal sealing stent of the t-Branch was removed, whereas in 2 cases, an additional large posterior fenestration at the second sealing stent was created. Technical success was 93%, with 1 severely stenotic renal artery not able to be catheterized and left unbridged. No endograft deployment complication (migration or malrotation) were experienced. There was 1 postoperative mortality in a patient with a ruptured AAA. Major complication rate was 27%, including 2 patients having SCI (one grade 2, one grade 3). A median of 2 segmental arteries were saved through the endograft modification.At a median follow-up of 1 year no endograft migration was observed. CONCLUSIONS: In urgent complex aortic repair for circumscribed anatomies such as juxta/pararenal aneurysms, the use of a modified OTS branched endograft proved to be a reproducible and safe technique, allowing the preservation of segmental arteries and possibly affecting favorably the spinal cord ischemic rates.Clinical ImpactOn-table shortening of the t-Branch endograft, optionally creating a big fenestration at the second sealing stent, is a feasible and reproducible option for urgent juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysm repair when custom-made devices are not available. The modification allowed sparing a median of two segmental arteries otherwise covered with a standard t-Branch, which might help mitigating the risk of spinal cord ischemia.

title: Pharmacogenomics guided clopidogrel utilization in veterans undergoing peripheral arterial intervention with vascular surgery compared to usual care.
abstract: After revascularization, patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) are at risk for ischemia. CYP2C19 variants may impact outcomes in those receiving clopidogrel but data is limited in PAD. This pilot study evaluated pharmacogenomic (PGx) guided care in 146 adult patients who underwent revascularization and were prescribed P2Y12 inhibitors. PGx testing was compared to no testing, with 61 patients in the PGx group vs 85 in control (clopidogrel only group). Clopidogrel was used in 97% of patients at baseline. Use of aspirin (64.7% vs 85.2%; p < 0.01) as well as stent interventions (44.7% vs 80%; p < 0.01) were less frequent in the control group, but P2Y12 inhibitor therapy duration was longer (10.2 ± 3.4 vs 8.0 ± 4.0 months; p < 0.04). Roughly one-third of patients were switched from clopidogrel based on PGx. Overall, in the control group, the composite of major adverse limb and cardiovascular events (45.9% vs 32.8%; p = 0.11), as well as bleeding events (14.1% vs 9.8%; p = 0.43) were non-significantly higher. At 7-12 months after revascularization, ischemic events were significantly lower in the PGx group (21.3% vs 4.7%; p = 0.01). A majority of ischemic events in the PGx group occurred within 90 days, and timely PGx testing was found to be delayed.

CYP2C19 variants may impact outcomes in those receiving clopidogrel but data is limited in PAD. This pilot study evaluated pharmacogenomic (PGx) guided care in 146 adult patients who underwent revascularization and were prescribed P2Y12 inhibitors.

title: Modelling medial degenerative features by enzymatic digestion to evaluate disease-relevant structure-function relationships in the thoracic aorta.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To clarify aortic microstructure-function relationships, we used improved, disease-motivated enzymatic digestion models of medial degeneration to evaluate individual extracellular matrix (ECM) components (i.e., elastin, collagen, and proteoglycans) and their influence on biomechanical properties of ascending aortic tissue. METHODS: Thin, 200 µm medial porcine ascending aortic sections were progressively digested with elastase or collagenase for selective degradation of these ECM components. Full thickness human aortic tissues were treated with chondroitinase, hyaluronidase, and heparinase to completely remove proteoglycans. Low- and high-strain modulus, transition-zone behavior, strain-energy density, and energy loss were derived from planar biaxial tensile testing. Degradation of elastin was captured with two photon excitation fluorescence imaging. Degradation of collagen was captured with picrosirius red staining and polarized light microscopy. Proteoglycan content and organization was confirmed by Alcian blue staining. RESULTS: Degradation of elastin fibers reduced low-strain modulus, strain-energy density, transition zone stress, and energy loss. Collagen degradation similarly reduced strain-energy density and decreased strain at the onset of transition, with reductions in high strain modulus and energy loss with increased degradation. Proteoglycan removal decreased energy loss and reduced strain-energy density and strain at onset of transition, and increased high strain modulus. CONCLUSIONS: Through targeted modeling of ECM degenerative features, we have delineated the overlapping effects of major matrix constituents, underscoring the complex, multifactorial nature of structure-function relationships in aortic disease. We also identified multiple microstructural pathways to increasing energy loss and the vulnerability of aortic tissue to failure. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Thoracic aortic dissection results from the progressive degeneration of the aortic wall extracellular matrix, yet the contributions of individual matrix constituents to this mechanical failure remain understudied. To address this gap, we developed a disease-motivated enzymatic model that enables controlled, graded modification of key extracellular matrix constituents in aortic tissue, better replicating the partial degeneration observed in vivo than existing approaches. Using this framework, we systematically evaluated the biomechanical consequences of elastin, collagen, and proteoglycan degeneration. Here, we revealed multiple microstructural pathways to altered viscoelastic behavior, which is associated with increased susceptibility to aortic failure. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into structure-function relationships in aortic disease and help explain how matrix degeneration contributes to tissue vulnerability and dissection risk.

METHODS: Thin, 200 µm medial porcine ascending aortic sections were progressively digested with elastase or collagenase for selective degradation of these ECM components. Full thickness human aortic tissues were treated with chondroitinase, hyaluronidase, and heparinase to completely remove proteoglycans.

title: Comparative outcomes of endovascular versus synthetic bypass for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions: A 3-year single-center cohort study.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) ranges from intermittent claudication to critical limb‑threatening ischemia (CLTI), with <3% of intermittent claudication cases progressing to CLTI. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stenting (PTAS) and synthetic graft femoropopliteal bypass (FPB) in a homogeneous PAD cohort. A subgroup analysis of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) B and C lesions, which lack standardized treatment algorithms, was also performed. We retrospectively analyzed 88 patients with no prior history of vascular interventions in the same limb who were treated for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions between 2016 and 2020 (29 underwent PTAS and 59 underwent FPB). Primary outcomes were reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, and vessel patency (primary, assisted primary, and secondary) over a 3‑year follow‑up. Subgroup analysis was performed to assess differences in treatment outcomes. No statistically significant differences were detected in reintervention, limb amputation, mortality, or patency between the two treatments. For loss of primary patency, the hazard ratio (HR) for FPB versus PTAS was 1.89 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76-4.69; log-rank p = 0.146) and 1.23 (95% CI, 0.45-3.38) after adjustment for lesion length and TASC grade. In the TASC B and C subgroup, no significant differences were observed in primary, assisted primary, or secondary patency (log-rank p = 0.809, 0.302, and 0.135, respectively). The study was underpowered to detect modest effects (post-hoc power for primary patency, 34.4%). In this small single-center cohort, no statistically significant difference in 3-year outcomes was detected between PTAS and FPB for isolated superficial femoral artery lesions; clinically meaningful differences cannot be excluded, and the findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

This study aimed to compare the outcomes of percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stenting (PTAS) and synthetic graft femoropopliteal bypass (FPB) in a homogeneous PAD cohort. A subgroup analysis of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) B and C lesions, which lack standardized treatment algorithms, was also performed.

title: Surgical management of fibrous dysplasia: recurrence and functional outcomes based on MSTS and TESS evaluation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Fibrous dysplasia (FD) is a benign bone disorder with variable clinical presentation and controversial management strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, surgical outcomes, recurrence rates, and functional results of patients with FD using Musculoskeletal Tumor Society (MSTS) and Toronto Extremity Salvage Score (TESS) systems. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 62 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FD between 2000 and 2022 at a tertiary referral center. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, presenting complaints, surgical methods, graft use, and recurrence were evaluated. Functional outcomes were assessed using MSTS and TESS scores. Statistical analyses were performed to determine factors affecting recurrence and functional outcomes. RESULTS: The mean age was 28.77 ± 14.72 years. Pain was the most common presenting complaint (50.0%). The proximal femur was the most frequently affected site (33.9%), and most lesions involved the lower extremity (82.3%). Recurrence occurred in 13 of 62 cases (21.0%) and was associated with presenting complaint (p = 0.001), being more common in patients presenting with pain. No significant association was found between recurrence and surgical method or graft use (p > 0.05). Mean MSTS and TESS scores were 90.56 ± 11.55 and 88.49 ± 9.86, respectively. Exploratory comparisons did not identify significant differences by surgical method or graft use. CONCLUSION: Surgical treatment of FD provides favorable functional outcomes with low complication rates. Clinical presentation and disease type significantly influence functional results and recurrence, whereas surgical technique and grafting do not appear to affect outcomes.

This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, surgical outcomes, recurrence rates, and functional results of patients with FD using Musculoskeletal Tumor Society (MSTS) and Toronto Extremity Salvage Score (TESS) systems. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 62 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FD between 2000 and 2022 at a tertiary referral center.

title: Descending aortic replacement after frozen elephant trunk: graft clamping and true-lumen anastomosis.
abstract: Second-stage descending aortic replacement after arch replacement with a frozen elephant trunk requires proximal control at a site that is often hostile to cross-clamping. The conventional elephant trunk technique was introduced to avoid cross-clamping the vulnerable proximal aorta; the previously implanted graft, left hanging in the descending aorta, is grasped and clamped directly, and the new graft is sutured to it. This video tutorial demonstrates the manoeuvre in the current era of the frozen, stented elephant trunk. In a patient with a frozen elephant trunk, computed tomography confirmed complete circumferential thrombosis of the false lumen around the stented graft. Through a left thoracotomy the distal aorta was clamped, and the completely thrombosed false lumen was opened without a proximal cross-clamp. The previously implanted stented graft was exposed and clamped directly, providing proximal control without dissecting or cross-clamping the densely adherent native aorta and without damaging the stent. The new graft was anastomosed proximally to the unstented distal cuff, and distally to the true lumen only, avoiding leak into the false lumen and limiting late aortic enlargement. The imaging that makes the approach safe, the step-by-step conduct, and the pitfall of identifying the graft within the walled-off true lumen are described.

The conventional elephant trunk technique was introduced to avoid cross-clamping the vulnerable proximal aorta; the previously implanted graft, left hanging in the descending aorta, is grasped and clamped directly, and the new graft is sutured to it. title: Carotid artery bypass and supraclavicular subclavian artery cannulation for cerebral malperfusion in aortic dissection.
abstract: Cerebral malperfusion complicating acute aortic dissection type A is a serious complication associated with markedly increased morbidity, permanent neurological deficit, and mortality. Early cannulation and extended replacement of occluded or dissected carotid arteries is an effective yet underused strategy for improving outcomes in such patients. We present a case of acute aortic dissection type A extending from the aortic root to the right common femoral artery, complicated by an occluded right common carotid artery and a dissected left common carotid artery. The patient was successfully treated with an extensive repair comprising David's procedure, arch repair, frozen elephant trunk implantation, bilateral extended carotid artery bypass and extended left subclavian artery bypass.

Early cannulation and extended replacement of occluded or dissected carotid arteries is an effective yet underused strategy for improving outcomes in such patients. We present a case of acute aortic dissection type A extending from the aortic root to the right common femoral artery, complicated by an occluded right common carotid artery and a dissected left common carotid artery.

title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke - New Directions.
abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

title: Popliteal Venous Aneurysm with Recurrent Pulmonary Embolism Treated by Ligation without Venous Reconstruction: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Popliteal venous aneurysm (PVA) is rare but may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE). CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old man presented with recurrent, transient loss of consciousness. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated bilateral PE and a saccular aneurysm of the right popliteal vein. Anticoagulation therapy improved his respiratory status, but surgical treatment was performed in view of the risk of recurrent embolism. The postoperative course was uneventful. CONCLUSIONS: At the 1-year follow-up, the patient remained free of clinically apparent lower-leg edema, and venous duplex ultrasonography demonstrated no deep vein thrombosis and the development of collateral venous channels. Although ligation is not a standard procedure for PVA, it may be an effective option in patients in whom reconstruction is difficult or in those at high operative risk.

title: Multifocal Cutaneous Angiosarcoma of the Lower Limbs Presenting With Severe Tumour-Related Haemorrhage: A Case Report.
abstract: Cutaneous angiosarcoma (CAS) is a rare and highly aggressive vascular tumour of endothelial origin with a poor prognosis. It can present with atypical skin lesions, making early diagnosis challenging. We present a case of a man in his late 80s who presented with a two-year history of weight loss, fatigue, iron-deficiency anaemia, and persistently elevated inflammatory markers. He subsequently developed rapidly progressive, multifocal violaceous nodules affecting both lower limbs. Initial differential diagnoses included melanocytic and nodular vasculitis. Skin biopsy confirmed high-grade CAS. The lesions progressed to fungation with recurrent bleeding, resulting in severe symptomatic anaemia requiring repeated blood transfusions. Management was complicated by his background of a persistent endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) of a large abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). This case highlights the importance of considering CAS in rapidly evolving, atypically located skin lesions. Early diagnosis and patient-centred multidisciplinary management are essential, particularly when advanced disease and significant comorbidities limit therapeutic options.

title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with acetabular fractures are at significant risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet the optimal chemoprophylactic agent remains undefined. Emerging evidence from elective arthroplasty and general orthopaedic trauma populations suggests that aspirin (ASA) may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery. METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a global, web-based health research network that provides on-demand access to de-identified, real-world data from electronic health records and claims. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025 and received VTE prophylaxis within 14 days of surgery were identified. Patients were stratified into ASA (n = 1189) and other anticoagulant (n = 5478) cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, yielding 1174 patients per cohort. Rates and odds of DVT, emergency department (ED) visits, deep infection, stroke, and readmission were assessed at 14-, 30-, and 90-day postoperative intervals. Temporal trends in VTE prophylaxis utilization were also analyzed. RESULTS: Compared to other anticoagulants, ASA was associated with significantly lower odds of DVT at 14 days (1.11% vs. 2.22%; odds ratio [OR]: 0.494; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.253-0.967; P = 0.036), 30 days (1.45% vs. 2.73%; OR: 0.524; 95% CI: 0.290-0.950; P = 0.030), and 90 days (2.56% vs. 4.34%; OR: 0.577; 95% CI: 0.365-0.913; P = 0.018). ASA was also associated with significantly lower odds of ED visits at 90 days (OR: 0.741; 95% CI: 0.570-0.963; P = 0.024). There were no significant differences in deep infection, stroke, or readmission rates. ASA utilization increased from 7.2% in 2014-39.5% in 2025. CONCLUSIONS: ASA is safe and effective for DVT prevention following acetabular fracture surgery and is associated with fewer ED visits compared to other anticoagulants. These findings support the growing adoption of ASA as a VTE prophylactic agent in the acetabular fracture population.

The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery.

title: Prediction models for venous thromboembolism in pediatric patients: A protocol for systematic review and critical appraisal.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) in children is a severe disease with high mortality rates. It is also gradually recognized as a major source of morbidity in hospitalized children, leading to increased length of hospital stay, higher mortality, and increased costs. The majority of pediatric subjects with VTE present inherited or acquired risk factors,such as the use of a central venous catheter (CVC), which accounts for more than more than 90% of neonatal VTE and 50% of pediatric VTE. Clinical studies on predictive models for VTE in children have shown inconsistent results. This systematic review aims to evaluate published prediction models for pediatric VTE, analyzing their characteristics, predictors, efficacy, and the methodological quality and applicability. The protocol has been prepared using the Preferred Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The systematic review protocol for VTE prediction in pediatric patients has been registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO 2025CRD420251231316. Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/vi-ew/CRD420251231316.) A comprehensive search across five major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang) will be conducted for studies on prediction models of VTE among pediatric patients. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and evaluate the bias risk and applicability of included studies using prediction modelling study tools. This systematic review will provide critical insights into the efficacy and quality of reporting of the VTE model in pediatric patients. This will guide clinical physicians in selecting the most appropriate VTE prediction model and inform future research endeavors in pediatric VTE prediction.

title: SEQuential tUnneled Catheters and Infective Events in haemodiaLysis: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study (SEQUEL Study).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tunnelled-cuffed catheters (TCCs) are widely used for haemodialysis access when permanent vascular access is unavailable. Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear. This study evaluated these two competing determinants of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI). METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included all TCC insertions at a tertiary nephrology unit between January 2016 and December 2021. The primary analysis examined CRBSI incidence per 1000 catheter-days stratified by catheter sequence number (first, second, third+ insertion per patient). Secondary analyses compared femoral versus internal jugular TCCs overall and within sequence strata. A registry-index cohort (patients with no documented prior TCC before January 2016, n = 135) was used to reduce, though not eliminate, sequence-related confounding in the site comparison; given only 24 CRBSI events, this analysis is exploratory and a clinically meaningful site difference cannot be excluded. Kaplan-Meier methods with log-rank testing were used for time-to-event outcomes. A cluster-robust marginal Cox model was used to account for repeated catheter insertions within patients, adjusting for sequence number, insertion site, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter. RESULTS: Among 626 TCC insertions in 339 patients (389 FV, 237 IJV), contributing 98,727 catheter-days, CRBSI incidence escalated with catheter sequence: 1.17 per 1000 catheter-days for first insertions, rising to 1.98 for second and 2.49 for third-or-more insertions. Notably, by the second insertion, CRBSI rates were similar between FV and IJV access (31.7% each). In the index cohort (n = 135; FV = 95, IJV = 40), CRBSI-free survival did not differ significantly between sites (log-rank p = 0.340), nor did catheter survival (p = 0.950) or patient survival (p = 0.487). In the all-TCC cohort, after adjustment for catheter sequence number, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter using a cluster-robust marginal Cox model, femoral access remained associated with a higher, though attenuated, CRBSI hazard after adjustment for the measured covariates (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.02-2.01; p = 0.039), indicating a modest residual site hazard beyond the sequence effect. CONCLUSIONS: Repeated catheterization was independently associated with increasing CRBSI risk, and catheter sequence number was the strongest predictor in the fully adjusted model. The femoral site effect was substantially attenuated after adjustment for sequence and was not statistically significant in the registry-index cohort analysis, though the wide confidence intervals preclude an equivalence interpretation. IJV access remains preferred; when IJV is unavailable, femoral TCC placement may be an acceptable alternative from an infection-risk perspective, but this must be weighed against thrombotic and limb complications, including deep vein thrombosis, which were not systematically ascertained in this study. Residual confounding cannot be excluded in this single-center retrospective study.

Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear.

title: Two chromosome-scale genomes of wild Aedes aegypti aegypti mosquitoes from North America and South-East Asia.
abstract: The yellow fever mosquito (Aedes aegypti) is the primary vector for diseases such as chikungunya, dengue fever, yellow fever, and Zika fever. These mosquitoes have been designated as two subspecies: Ae. aegypti formosus (Aaf) and Ae. aegypti aegypti (Aaa)-the former being a darker form limited to sub-Saharan Africa and the latter referring to lighter colored individuals found circumglobally in the tropics and sub-tropics. In addition to morphology and distribution, these two sub-species differ in their behavior and ecology-Aaf females generally feed on nonhuman mammals and live in rural and sylvatic areas, whereas Aaa females preferentially feed on humans and are found in human dwellings in urban areas. These characteristics and differences make them species of great medical importance, and the development of resources for understanding their biology has high priority. We recently published a chromosome-scale wild Aaf genome assembly and here we add to this body of resources by presenting two de novo chromosome-scale genome assemblies of wild-caught Aaa from North America and Southeast Asia. Using the Pacific Biosciences HiFi sequencing platform combined with HiC sequencing, we achieved high continuity (N50: >400 Mb; L50: 2) and completeness (BUSCO single-copy: ~97%; diptera set). These assemblies will contribute to further elucidate the global genetic diversity of this major disease vector and uncover the genetic basis of phenotypic differences between the sub-species.
