title: ClpB-mediated modulation of GroEL-bound luciferase and subsequent refolding by DnaK chaperone system.
abstract: In prokaryotes, DnaK-DnaJ-GrpE (KJE), GroEL-GroES (ELS) and the AAA+ disaggregase ClpB constitute the major ATP-dependent chaperone systems involved in protein quality control machinery. Although the individual functions and interplay of KJE and ClpB systems have been extensively studied, the role of ClpB with ELS during KJE-mediated substrate refolding is still elusive. Here, we investigated the role of ClpB in KJE- and ELS-mediated refolding of chemically and heat-denatured luciferase. Simultaneous presence of KJE, ELS and ClpB significantly enhanced the refolding of chemically denatured luciferase, whereas the combination of KJE and ClpB resulted in a higher refolding yield of heat-denatured luciferase. The inhibitory effect of ELS on KJE-mediated refolding of luciferase was significantly reduced when KJE, ELS and ClpB were present simultaneously. Sequential chaperone addition experiments showed that ELS-bound heat-denatured luciferase was refolded to 24% and 36% of its native activity by KJE and ClpB respectively, whereas the KJE-ClpB chaperone system further enhanced refolding to 43%. ClpB alone did not enhanced the refolding of ELS-bound chemically denatured luciferase, while subsequent addition of KJE or KJE-ClpB restored 36% and 44% of the native activity, respectively. Turbidity assay showed that the KJE system effectively suppressed heat-induced luciferase aggregation, whereas ClpB alone exhibited no anti-aggregation activity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ClpB cooperates with the KJE chaperone system to enhance substrate refolding and rescue ELS-stalled substrate proteins, thus providing insights into the coordinated action of ATP-dependent chaperone systems in the maintenance of cellular protein homeostasis.

title: Perioperative Management of the Orthopedic Patient Taking Antipsychotics: A Narrative Review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Antipsychotic prescribing continues to rise among older adults, the group most likely to present for orthopedic surgery, and orthopedic surgeons now operate regularly on patients taking these agents. Guidance for managing them around an operation sits largely in the psychiatric, anesthesiology and pharmacologic literature rather than the surgical one. This narrative review gathers the orthopedic-specific evidence and organizes it by whether a finding reflects the medication or the psychiatric illness for which it was prescribed. FINDINGS: Antipsychotic exposure is associated with higher all-cause revision and periprosthetic fracture after total knee arthroplasty, and second-generation exposure raises all-cause and aseptic revision after shoulder arthroplasty independent of psychiatric diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism roughly doubles after primary total knee arthroplasty. Among geriatric hip fracture patients antipsychotics are the only medication class independently linked to in-hospital falls, and preoperative use independently predicts postoperative delirium that prophylaxis does not prevent. Spine, sports medicine and trauma surgery all show worse outcomes in patients carrying a psychiatric diagnosis, yet none of those literatures disentangles the drug from the disorder. Thromboembolism and the shoulder revision signal are the clearest drug-attributable exceptions. Hyperprolactinemia-mediated hypogonadism, metabolic derangement and impaired fracture healing remain plausible but unproven. Nearly all available evidence is retrospective. CONCLUSION: Antipsychotic therapy should continue through the perioperative period unless a specific reason exists to stop it. Abrupt discontinuation risks psychiatric relapse, which is harder to manage than the perioperative risks the drugs themselves carry. Low bone mineral density, poor glycemic control and thromboembolic risk are all worth addressing before surgery, drawing on psychiatry and internal medicine. Antipsychotics are not recommended for delirium prophylaxis. Whether altering therapy improves orthopedic outcomes has not been studied prospectively.

title: Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes in patients with severe pelvic ring injury requiring REBOA: A two-center matched cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) is used for life-threatening hemorrhage, but evidence has largely focused on acute outcomes. Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes among survivors treated with REBOA remain poorly characterized. METHODS: This retrospective two-center matched cohort included 98 adults with severe, hemodynamically unstable pelvic ring injuries who survived at least 24 h; hospital survivors required at least 12 months of follow-up. Forty-nine REBOA-treated patients were matched 1:1 to 49 non-REBOA patients by major Young-Burgess category, Injury Severity Score, and age. The primary outcome was functional status among hospital survivors, categorized as good/fair/poor. Deep surgical site infection (SSI) after definitive pelvic fixation was the key secondary outcome, and nonunion was exploratory. Main models used a propensity-score linear predictor based on age, Injury Severity Score, initial systolic blood pressure, and lactate. RESULTS: Seventy-five patients survived hospitalization (30 REBOA; 45 non-REBOA); median follow-up was 19 months. Good/fair/poor outcomes were 16.7%/46.7%/36.7% in REBOA survivors and 51.1%/37.8%/11.1% in non-REBOA survivors. REBOA exposure was associated with worse functional status after adjustment (common odds ratio [cOR], 3.14; 95% CI, 1.11-8.92; P = 0.032). Among 68 definitive-fixation survivors, deep SSI occurred in 44.0% versus 9.3% (adjusted OR, 7.01; 95% CI, 1.88-31.07; P = 0.003); all observed events occurred within 60 days. Nonunion occurred in 26.7% versus 6.7% (adjusted OR, 9.09; 95% CI, 2.00-53.71; P = 0.004). Sensitivity analyses for deep SSI were directionally consistent. CONCLUSIONS: Among hospital survivors, REBOA exposure was associated with poorer long-term functional recovery and a higher burden of deep SSI. Nonunion was more frequent but remained exploratory. These findings characterize a high-risk orthopaedic survivor phenotype but do not establish a direct causal effect of REBOA.

title: Dysphagia as the Initial Manifestation of Anti-HMGCR Antibody-Positive Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-positive immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels. Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are also at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), though data specific to IMNM remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: An 83-year-old man with brief, remote statin exposure presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and a three-year history of oropharyngeal dysphagia preceding limb involvement. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated creatine kinase and transaminases. Anti-HMGCR antibodies were positive, and muscle biopsy confirmed necrotizing myopathy. During evaluation for occult malignancy, bilateral pulmonary emboli were incidentally identified. The patient required high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, and intravenous immunoglobulin for refractory disease. With aggressive immunosuppressive therapy and rehabilitation, he demonstrated substantial clinical recovery at 6 months. CONCLUSION: This case highlights oropharyngeal dysphagia as an early and, for a prolonged period, isolated manifestation of anti-HMGCR antibody-positive IMNM; here, it preceded the onset of limb weakness by approximately 3 years. It underscores the importance of comprehensive diagnostic evaluation in patients with unexplained oropharyngeal dysfunction, in whom an inflammatory myopathy may otherwise be overlooked for years. Clinicians should maintain awareness of thrombotic risk in inflammatory myopathies, particularly during active disease. Early recognition and prompt immunosuppressive therapy remain critical to optimize outcomes and prevent irreversible muscle damage.

Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. title: The law of surprise: temporal variation and seasonality of acute aortic syndromes: a single-centre epidemiologic cohort analysis spanning 20 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) represent life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies characterized by high mortality rates despite rapid intervention. Global epidemiological data indicate substantial variance in incidence. Longitudinal single-centre data over extended periods are limited but crucial for understanding diagnostic, demographic, and systemic factors influencing admission trends.(1). This study aimed to analyze annual and seasonal variation trends of AAS over a 20-year period in a single maximal care centre and explore potential chronological and environmental contributors to this variation. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated 403 patients admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of AAS between 2005 and 2025 at the University Hospital Erlangen, Germany. All diagnoses were established via computed tomography angiography (CTA) and confirmed intraoperatively. Annual, quarterly, and monthly surgical volumes were calculated, and temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Admission rates during public holidays and school vacations were also evaluated. RESULTS: Over the 20-year observation period, a steady increasing trend in the annual number of AAS cases was observed, peaking in 2017. Analysis of quarterly distributions revealed a statistically significant dominance of cases in the fourth quarter (Q4: October-December; p < 0.05) compared to the second (Q2) and third (Q3) quarters. Monthly analysis demonstrated a prominent peak in October (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.85 vs. June, p < 0.05). Conversely, fixed public holidays and school vacations were associated with statistically significant reductions in daily admission counts (p < 0.05), with the lowest relative case counts observed during the Christmas vacation period (IRR: 0.40-0.50). CONCLUSION: The case counts of acute aortic syndromes exhibits significant temporal and seasonal variation, characterized by a distinct late-autumn and early-winter peak, alongside significant declines during institutional vacation periods. These findings suggest that acute cardiovascular events are heavily modulated by cyclical environmental and socio-systemic factors.

title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques. RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts. CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention. KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

title: "Fatal venous thromboembolism and divergent phenotypes in DOCK8 deficiency: a three-sibling case series".
abstract: Dedicator of Cytokinesis 8 (DOCK8) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive combined immunodeficiency characterized by early-onset eczema, recurrent bacterial, viral, and fungal infections, and an increased risk of malignancy. The disease arises from impaired actin cytoskeletal regulation, leading to defective immune cell migration and T-cell activation, together with the development of a Th2-skewed immune response. In this case report, we present three siblings with genetically confirmed DOCK8 deficiency and multisystem involvement. All patients presented with early-onset atopic dermatitis, recurrent respiratory tract infections, and failure to thrive. Bronchiectasis and severe viral infections were observed in all three patients. Ocular involvement developed in two patients: one experienced Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis resulting in persistent visual impairment, while the other developed corneal perforation secondary to herpesvirus infection. One patient developed iatrogenic Cushing syndrome due to prolonged topical corticosteroid use. In the same patient, catheter-related superficial thrombophlebitis progressed to deep vein thrombosis and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, with a fatal outcome complicated by probable pulmonary thromboembolism. This case series highlights the severe multisystem involvement and risk of irreversible organ damage associated with DOCK8 deficiency, and underscores the critical importance of early diagnosis and timely planning of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) as the only curative therapeutic approach.

In this case report, we present three siblings with genetically confirmed DOCK8 deficiency and multisystem involvement.

title: Role of Microcatheter Tip Position and Microguidewire Stiffness in Safe Neuroendovascular Navigation of Distal Vessels.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Advancements in neuroendovascular devices have enabled greater access to distal, tortuous vasculature. However, this expanded capability also increases the risk of serious hemorrhagic complications during device navigation. The aim of the study is to quantify how microcatheter position and microguidewire stiffness affect tip contact force at a distal MCA segment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A moderate-tortuosity silicone model of the MCA was used to evaluate three 0.014-inch Synchro SELECT microguidewires (Soft, Standard, and Support) with a TrevoTrak microcatheter positioned proximally in the M1 or distally in the M2 segment. Tip contact forces at the distal end of the M2 segment were recorded with a digital force gauge serving as a standardized surrogate for the distal vessel wall during motorized controlled wire advancement. From the force-distance curves, tip contact force slopes (mN/mm) and maximum tip contact forces (mN) were calculated and statistically compared across wire types and catheter positions. RESULTS: P P With distal microcatheter support, the average tip contact force slopes were 10.64 mN/mm (Soft), 10.85 mN/mm (Standard), and 15.28 mN/mm (Support) (< .0001). With proximal support, the average slopes were significantly lower: 1.61 mN/mm (Soft), 3.15 mN/mm (Standard), and 3.87 mN/mm (Support) (< .01). Distal microcatheter positioning consistently produced approximately 3- to 6-fold higher tip contact force slopes and higher maximum tip contact forces than proximal positioning. CONCLUSIONS: Microcatheter tip position and microguidewire stiffness were the primary determinants of the tip contact force transmitted to distal vessel segments during neuroendovascular navigation in this model. Stiffer microguidewires exert significantly greater tip contact force, particularly when the microcatheter is positioned near the distal segment. Maintaining the microcatheter tip proximally attenuates these forces and offers a simple strategy to reduce mechanic loading of fragile distal branches during distal access procedures.

The aim of the study is to quantify how microcatheter position and microguidewire stiffness affect tip contact force at a distal MCA segment.

title: Histologically Validated Ex Vivo Characterization of Intraplaque Hemorrhage and Lipid Components Using Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Accurate characterization of carotid plaque components is essential for stroke risk assessment. Intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is a well-established marker of plaque vulnerability, whereas lipid-rich necrotic cores (LRNCs) often show overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-four carotid plaque specimens obtained by en bloc excision during carotid endarterectomy between October 2017 and August 2021 were examined. All specimens underwent ex vivo MRI at 3T, including T1WI, T2WI, and TOF-equivalent FLASH, as well as QSM reconstructed from multiecho FLASH phase data. After MRI, specimens were serially sectioned and stained using H&E and immunohistochemical techniques. ROIs corresponding to histologically confirmed IPH and lipid components were delineated on MRI by consensus of 2 radiologists. On conventional MRI, signal intensities were measured in corresponding histologic regions, and contrast-to-noise ratios (CNRs) were calculated relative to surrounding agarose gel. On QSM, absolute magnetic susceptibility values were measured in the same regions. The difference between plaque tissue and the surrounding agarose gel was defined as the relative susceptibility value (rSV), which was used for statistical analysis. CNRs and rSVs among plaque components were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by the Steel-Dwass test for pair-wise comparisons. RESULTS: P P P Seventy-nine matched cross-sectional slices were analyzed, yielding 24 IPH, 61 LRNCs, and 13 foam-cell aggregates (FAs). No significant difference in CNR was observed between IPH and LRNC on T1WI or FLASH. Histopathologic analysis demonstrated that many LRNCs exhibited erythrocyte-derived remnants consistent with prior hemorrhagic events. FAs showed lower CNRs than IPH on T1WI and FLASH (< .05). On T2WI, IPH showed lower CNRs than LRNCs or FAs (< .05). On QSM, IPH demonstrated higher rSVs than LRNCs or FAs (< .01). CONCLUSIONS: Histologic validation demonstrates that many LRNCs contain erythrocyte remnants, which may contribute to their overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. QSM captures erythrocyte-derived susceptibility effects within plaques and provides complementary susceptibility-based information not available from conventional MRI.

Intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is a well-established marker of plaque vulnerability, whereas lipid-rich necrotic cores (LRNCs) often show overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation.

title: Characterization of Perfusion Scotoma in Acute Ischemic Stroke after Endovascular Treatment.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: CTP may underestimate the size of the ischemic core, a phenomenon known as perfusion scotoma. We aimed to investigate the prevalence of perfusion scotoma, characterize its baseline predictors, and explore its association with functional outcomes in a real-world population of patients with stroke treated with endovascular treatment (EVT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: P Data were obtained from a prospective EVT registry, selecting patients with successful recanaliztion (final modified TICI ≥2b), a good-quality baseline CTP, and an available 24-hour noncontrast CT. Ischemic core underestimated volume (ICuV) was calculated as the difference between follow-up infarct volume and CTP-estimated ischemic core. The primary outcome was the presence of perfusion scotoma, defined as ICuV ≥10 mL. Baseline characteristics withvalue <.20 in univariable comparisons were entered in a backward stepwise, multivariable logistic regression analysis to identify factors independently associated with perfusion scotoma. RESULTS: P P P P A total of 464 patients of 672 (69%) were included in the analysis. The median age was 74 years (interquartile range = 68-83), 215 (46.3%) were men, and 116 (25%) had a perfusion scotoma. Perfusion scotoma was independently associated with male sex (adjusted OR 1.62 [95% CI, 1.01-2.51];= .04), more distal site of occlusion (adjusted OR 1.60 [95% CI, 1.10-2.34];= .01; per each 1-point increase: terminal ICA to M1 to M2), lower ASPECTS at admission (adjusted OR 0.64 [95% CI, 0.54-0.76];< .001; per each 1-point increase), and longer onset-to-CT time (adjusted OR 1.05, [95% CI, 1.01-1.10];= .03; per each 1-hour increase). The optimal onset-to-CT time cutoff to distinguish between patients without and with perfusion scotoma was 420 minutes. Perfusion scotoma was associated with 90-day ordinal mRS (adjusted common OR 3.16 [95% CI, 2.12-4.76]). CONCLUSIONS: Perfusion scotoma occurred in 1 of every 4 patients. Baseline predictors included male sex, lower ASPECTS, more distal vessel occlusion, and longer onset-to-CT time. Perfusion scotoma was associated with poorer functional outcomes.

title: Tranexamic Acid Administration is Associated With Lower Transfusion Rates and Wound Complications Following Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used in total joint arthroplasty, but data on its efficacy in periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) of the knee are scarce. We assessed TXA efficacy in revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for PJI. METHODS: A national database was queried for patients ≥18 years undergoing stage-one revision TKA for PJI from 2016 to 2023. Patients with and without TXA exposure were propensity matched. Multivariable logistic regression assessed primary outcomes (postoperative transfusion, bleeding complications, and wound complications) and secondary outcomes (thromboembolic complications). RESULTS: P P P P P P Overall, 13,247 TXA patients were matched 1:1 to 13,247 non-TXA patients on comorbidities, Charlson Comorbidity Index, demographics, hospital characteristics, and preoperative transfusion rates, all with standardized mean differences <0.10. Mean age was 67.4 years in both cohorts, with similar use of venous thromboembolic chemoprophylaxis. TXA was associated with decreased adjusted odds of postoperative transfusion (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 0.77, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.69-0.85,< .001) and aggregate wound complications (aOR: 0.65, 95% CI: 0.60-0.70,< .001), with similar odds of aggregate bleeding complications (aOR: 1.02, 95% CI: 0.95-1.09,= .563). Odds of aggregate venous thromboembolism (aOR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.82-1.13,= .874), deep vein thrombosis (aOR: 1.00, 95% CI: 1.00-1.01,= .309), and pulmonary embolism (aOR: 1.06, 95% CI: 0.83-1.34,= .639) were similar. CONCLUSIONS: TXA was associated with lower rates of transfusion and aggregate wound complications, without increased venous thromboembolism risk, during revision TKA for PJI.

We assessed TXA efficacy in revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for PJI. METHODS: A national database was queried for patients ≥18 years undergoing stage-one revision TKA for PJI from 2016 to 2023.

title: Acute ischemic stroke in a young adult with persistently reduced protein S levels: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Protein S deficiency is a rare thrombophilic disorder whose contribution to arterial ischemic stroke in young adults remains uncertain. While its association with venous thromboembolism is well established, evidence supporting a causal association with arterial ischemic stroke is limited. PRESENTATION OF THE CASE: A 34-year-old woman with no vascular risk factors presented with acute right-sided hemiparesis and dysarthria of 6 hours' duration. Examination showed right upper motor neuron facial palsy, right-sided hemiparesis (power 3/5), and a positive Babinski sign on the right side. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed an acute infarct in the left paramedian pons. Thrombophilia workup at 2 weeks showed a low free Protein S antigen level of 42% (reference range, 50-134%) by immunoturbidimetric assay. Recognized acquired causes of low Protein S were excluded. Antiplatelet therapy was discontinued, and rivaroxaban, 20 mg daily, was initiated as an individualized decision. The patient recovered fully with no recurrent thrombotic events at 3 months. Due to financial constraints, only the Protein S antigen level was reassessed at 3 months, which showed a persistently low free Protein S antigen level (40%). Without genetic testing, family screening, and total Protein S antigen measurement, the findings were considered suggestive of, but not diagnostic of, inherited Protein S deficiency. CONCLUSION: This case report highlights persistently reduced protein S antigen levels as a possible but unconfirmed contributor to an otherwise cryptogenic arterial stroke in a young adult. It emphasizes that thrombophilia testing should be considered selectively in young stroke patients, after excluding more common etiologies, rather than performed routinely.

While its association with venous thromboembolism is well established, evidence supporting a causal association with arterial ischemic stroke is limited. title: Age-specific associations of endovascular therapy and reperfusion delay with outcomes after large vessel occlusion: a regional registry study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The benefit of endovascular therapy (EVT) in very elderly patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain, and sensitivity to reperfusion delay may differ by age. We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed 1,280 patients with acute LVO in an emergency medical service-based registry, divided into groups aged 85 years or older and younger than 85 years. The primary outcome was an ordinal shift towards a better 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score. Secondary outcomes were dichotomized functional measures incorporating prestroke status. RESULTS: Among 837 patients younger than 85 years, EVT was associated with a favourable mRS shift (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.01). Among 443 patients aged 85 years or older, the estimate was favourable but not statistically significant (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.87-1.92). No significant age-by-treatment interaction was observed for functional outcomes. Among patients treated with successful reperfusion by EVT, favourable outcomes declined more steeply with increasing onset-to-reperfusion time in those aged 85 years or older. DISCUSSION: The association of EVT with functional outcomes was not significantly modified by age but estimates in very elderly patients were less precise. Very elderly patients appeared more vulnerable to reperfusion delay. CONCLUSION: Treatment selection should integrate prestroke function, stroke severity, imaging findings, procedural feasibility, and the likelihood of rapid reperfusion rather than age alone.

We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes. title: The Latest Progress in the Application of Tofacitinib in Rheumatic Diseases--A Narrative Review.
abstract: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After screening and eligibility assessment, 89 clinical publications were included in the disease-specific evidence synthesis, and the strength of clinical evidence across disease indications was evaluated qualitatively. The most robust evidence is available for rheumatoid arthritis, with randomized trials, long-term extension studies, and real-world investigations demonstrating improvements in disease activity and physical function and inhibition of radiographic progression. Clinical evidence also supports therapeutic benefit in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whereas evidence for Takayasu arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, systemic lupus erythematosus, and anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease remains limited or exploratory. Long-term integrated safety analyses in RA have reported incidence rates of serious adverse events of approximately 9.0-9.4 per 100 patient-years and serious infections of approximately 2.5-2.7 per 100 patient-years, while herpes zoster, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and malignancy remain clinically important safety considerations. Potential drug-drug interactions and dose adjustment in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and other special populations further require individualized assessment. Overall, tofacitinib has a well-established role in RA treatment and potential therapeutic value in several other rheumatic diseases; however, its use should be guided by disease-specific evidence, previous treatment exposure, comorbidities, concomitant medications, and individual safety risks. Further prospective and long-term studies are needed to better define its role in less well-established indications and special populations.

title: Sex-associated territory-specific vascular phenotypes in genetically confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: COL3A1 To characterise territory-specific sex-associated vascular phenotypes in genetically confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and assess whether associations persisted after accounting formolecular mechanism. METHODS: In this retrospective multicentre cohort, clinical-genomics review identified 95 eligible patients from 110 source records. 18 prespecified vascular outcomes were evaluated using Firth bias-reduced logistic regression adjusted for completed age per 10-year increment. Sensitivity analyses among 75 patients with classifiable dominant-negative or haploinsufficient mechanisms additionally adjusted for molecular mechanism. RESULTS: The cohort included 34 male and 61 female patients. Male sex was associated with ascending aortic dilation or aneurysm (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.68 to 15.41), iliac/femoral aneurysm (4.61, 95% CI 1.79 to 12.52), extra-aortic dissection (3.93, 95% CI 1.61 to 10.24), renal dissection (10.08, 95% CI 3.08 to 42.11) and splanchnic dissection (5.84, 95% CI 2.27 to 15.90). Aortic dissection and cervical aneurysm or dissection were not associated with male sex. In the imaging-restricted unadjusted comparison, head and neck tortuosity, ectasia or dilation was present in 23/44 (52.3%) female and 7/29 (24.1%) male patients (p=0.028). In genotype sensitivity analyses, associations remained for iliac/femoral, renal and splanchnic aneurysms and for extra-aortic, renal, splanchnic and iliac dissections, whereas several broader aneurysm and intervention estimates became less precise. CONCLUSIONS: Male sex was associated with a territory-specific vascular phenotype, with the most consistent genotype-adjusted associations involving renal, splanchnic, iliac/femoral and broader extra-aortic dissection territories. Surveillance should remain comprehensive rather than sex restricted.

title: Electrosurgical Septotomy Across the Full Spectrum of Aortic Dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. METHODS: A retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair, and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < .001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia, or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital, and overall mortality were 10%, 14%, and 19%, respectively, with 1 fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion.

title: Superficial venous procedures improve clinical and hemodynamic outcomes in patients with concomitant deep venous reflux: a prospective observational study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Concurrent deep venous reflux (DVR) is frequently observed in patients with superficial venous reflux (SVR). However, the effect of SVR treatment on symptom relief and hemodynamic changes in patients with concomitant DVR remains unclear. METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients evaluated between January 2010 and December 2019 who were found to have both DVR and SVR. Patients were categorized into the treatment group, which underwent superficial venous procedures, and the observation group, which received no intervention. RESULTS: A total of 31 patients were enrolled, including 9 in the observation group and 22 in the treatment group. The median age was 58 years, and 25.8% were male. Baseline characteristics were not significantly different between the groups, although the treatment group tended to have a higher proportion of male patients, higher venous clinical severity score (VCSS), and higher clinical, etiological, anatomical, and pathophysiologic classifications. Among 38 limbs, 47.4% had deep axial reflux. At a median follow-up of 6.4 years, the treatment group showed significant improvement, with median VCSS and Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire improvements of 2.0 and 5.4, respectively, whereas both scores worsened in the observation group. Complete DVR resolution occurred in 9.1% of limbs in the observation group and 29.6% of limbs in the treatment group. Popliteal vein reflux duration significantly decreased from 5.1 to 3.0 seconds after treatment. CONCLUSION: In patients with concomitant DVR and SVR, superficial venous procedures were associated with long-term symptomatic improvement and favorable hemodynamic changes in DVR. DVR should not be considered a barrier to superficial venous intervention.

However, the effect of SVR treatment on symptom relief and hemodynamic changes in patients with concomitant DVR remains unclear. METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients evaluated between January 2010 and December 2019 who were found to have both DVR and SVR.

title: Long-term outcomes of laparoscopic aortobifemoral bypass: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Laparoscopic aortobifemoral bypass (LABF) is a minimally invasive option for extensive aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD), but data on its long-term durability are limited. We aimed to evaluate the 10-year outcomes of LABF for patients with TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) II C and D lesions. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of 20 patients who underwent LABF for TASC II C or D AIOD at a single tertiary center between January 2004 and December 2012. Primary endpoints were primary and secondary patency rates, survival, and postoperative complications. RESULTS: The median patient age was 65 years, and 18 (90.0%) were male. TASC II D lesions were present in 18 patients (90.0%). There was one perioperative death (5.0%). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed primary patency rates of 94.7%, 88.8%, 82.0%, and 82.0% at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years, respectively. The 10-year secondary patency rate was 88.0%. Reintervention was required in 2 patients (10.0%) during follow-up. CONCLUSION: LABF provides excellent long-term patency rates comparable to open repair for complex AIOD. With careful patient selection, LABF represents a safe, feasible, and durable minimally invasive alternative, particularly for patients unsuitable for endovascular therapy.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of 20 patients who underwent LABF for TASC II C or D AIOD at a single tertiary center between January 2004 and December 2012.

title: Frailty as a Modifier of Revascularization-Associated Outcomes in Diabetic Foot Ulcer: A Nationwide Inpatient Study.
abstract: We examined whether frailty modifies the association between revascularization and major amputation among hospitalizations for diabetic foot ulcer. We identified adult hospitalizations in the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 through 2022 and classified frailty using the 109-code Hospital Frailty Risk Score. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed major amputation and in-hospital mortality across four frailty strata, adjusting for demographic and clinical characteristics. Among 2 588 159 diabetic foot ulcer hospitalizations, frailty burden exceeded that of diabetes hospitalizations without foot ulcers. The association between revascularization and major amputation weakened with increasing frailty: adjusted odds ratios were 0.30 (95% confidence interval, 0.26-0.35) for low frailty, 0.68 for intermediate frailty and 0.82 for intermediate-high frailty. No statistically significant association was observed for high frailty (adjusted odds ratio, 1.05; 95% confidence interval, 0.86-1.29; interaction p < 0.001). Revascularization was associated with lower in-hospital mortality across frailty strata without significant interaction (p = 0.413). Frailty modified the observed association with major amputation, whereas mortality associations showed limited heterogeneity. Treatment selection and unmeasured clinical differences preclude causal interpretation.

title: Inferior Vena Cava Cement Migration with Pulmonary Cement Embolism: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Vertebral augmentation procedures, including vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty, can result in cement extravasation, which is often clinically silent. Less commonly, cement may migrate intravascularly into the inferior vena cava (IVC) and pulmonary arterial circulation, resulting in pulmonary cement embolism, a potentially life-threatening complication. Early recognition in the emergency department (ED) is essential to guide appropriate imaging, specialty consultation, and timely management. CASE REPORT: A 76-year-old woman with recent third lumbar vertebral augmentation presented to the ED with acute worsening low back pain and burning bilateral radicular symptoms approximately one week after the procedure. Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast demonstrated linear hyperdense material extending from the treated vertebral body into the IVC, concerning for intravascular cement migration. Additional CT of the chest demonstrated multiple bilateral subsegmental pulmonary cement emboli. Interventional radiology was consulted emergently, and the patient was transferred for endovascular retrieval of the IVC cement fragment, which was successfully removed. The pulmonary cement emboli were small, peripheral, and asymptomatic and were managed conservatively. The patient remained hemodynamically stable and was discharged after monitored hospitalization. CONCLUSION: Inferior vena cava cement migration with pulmonary cement embolism is a potentially life-threatening complication of vertebral augmentation. Emergency physicians should maintain suspicion for this diagnosis in patients with acute pain or new cardiopulmonary symptoms following recent spinal procedures. Early imaging, multidisciplinary consultation, monitored admission, and endovascular retrieval when indicated may reduce morbidity.

Less commonly, cement may migrate intravascularly into the inferior vena cava (IVC) and pulmonary arterial circulation, resulting in pulmonary cement embolism, a potentially life-threatening complication. Early recognition in the emergency department (ED) is essential to guide appropriate imaging, specialty consultation, and timely management.

title: Atypical Presentation of Extensive Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection Initially Misattributed to Aspiration Pneumonia: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute aortic dissection is a life-threatening emergency that may present with nonspecific symptoms, particularly in older adults, leading clinicians to anchor on more common diagnoses. CASE REPORT: An 85-year-old man presented with four days of cough, weakness, and constipation after a recent emergency department (ED) visit due to food impaction after he choked on a carrot. A chest radiograph obtained the day before admission showed left basal consolidation, prompting referral for suspected aspiration pneumonia. In the ED, he appeared comfortable with no complaints of chest pain. Physical examination noted mild tachycardia and wheezes bilaterally and treatment was initiated with antibiotics and bronchodilators. A low-voltage electrocardiogram led to immediate point-of-care echocardiography, which demonstrated a large circumferential pericardial effusion, a markedly dilated aortic root, and right ventricular collapse. Computed tomography angiography confirmed an extensive Stanford Type A aortic dissection. CONCLUSION: This case highlights how deceptively calm presentations can mask catastrophic disease and why clinicians must be ready to abandon their first diagnosis when the data demands it.

title: Trends and Disparities in Peripheral Artery Disease and Dementia-Related Mortality in the United States, 1999-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular risk factors are common among individuals with both peripheral artery disease (PAD) and dementia, and these co-existing conditions are a major public health problem. Our goal is to assess nationwide mortality trends and disparities associated with concomitant PAD and dementia in the United States between 1999 and 2024. METHODS: This is a population-based analysis using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to assess adults aged 65 years and older. Death certificates that mentioned both PAD and dementia were included. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were calculated to study the national trends by demographic and geographic subgroups. RESULTS: There were 317,390 deaths among patients who had both PAD and dementia. The overall AAMR was fairly stable over the study period, rising marginally from 23.97 in 1999 to 24.22 in 2024. AAMRs were higher in non-Hispanic African Americans across racial and ethnic groups and peaked in non-metropolitan regions. The sensitivity analyses showed that mortality rates that were driven by PAD significantly declined (AAPC: -4.77) and rates driven by dementia (AAPC: 3.77) increased significantly over the 25-year period. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the age-standardized mortality for concomitant PAD and dementia was largely stable, but there are still important geographical and demographic differences. The mortality curves when divided by underlying cause of death show that deaths due to PAD have decreased, while deaths due to dementia have risen in the United States among older adults over the study period.

Our goal is to assess nationwide mortality trends and disparities associated with concomitant PAD and dementia in the United States between 1999 and 2024. METHODS: This is a population-based analysis using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to assess adults aged 65 years and older.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Self-Reported Practices of Emergency and Intensive Care Nurses in Managing Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, with a growing burden in low- and middle-income countries. Nurses in emergency and intensive care units (ICUs) play a critical role in TBI management, yet little is known about their competencies in Palestine. AIMS: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes and self-reported practices of emergency and intensive care unit nurses regarding traumatic brain injury management and to identify factors associated with these outcomes. STUDY DESIGN: A descriptive cross-sectional survey using stratified random sampling was conducted in governmental and private hospitals in the northern West Bank, Palestine. Data were collected in January 2025 using a validated Arabic questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation coefficients and multiple linear regression analyses were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: A total of 151 nurses participated, yielding a response rate of 61.4% (151/246). Nurses demonstrated generally good foundational knowledge, particularly in Glasgow Coma Scale interpretation and recognition of neurological responses, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring. Attitudes were predominantly positive, with strong support for specialised training. Self-reported practices included maintaining adequate blood pressure and initiating deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis. Knowledge correlated significantly with attitude and self-reported practice, and attitude correlated strongly with self-reported practice. Previous TBI training, higher educational level and longer clinical experience were associated with better outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Emergency and intensive care unit nurses demonstrated adequate foundational knowledge and positive attitudes towards traumatic brain injury management, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring and selected self-reported practices. Structured continuing professional development, standardised protocols and organisational support are needed to strengthen neurotrauma nursing care. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The findings support context-sensitive continuing education, simulation, standardised protocols and organisational measures that enable nurses to translate knowledge into consistent neurotrauma care in resource-constrained settings.

title: Mortality, Morbidity, and Treatment-Related Outcomes Following Pathological Hip Fractures: An 8-Year Single-Center Experience.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, type of treatment, and factors associated with mortality and morbidity, including the length of hospital stay, among patients with pathological hip fractures in a tertiary center in Saudi Arabia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted, which included all adult patients diagnosed with pathological hip fractures from 2016 to 2024. Demographics, fracture type, type of treatment, complications, and outcomes data were evaluated. A univariate analysis was performed to identify associations between clinical variables and patient outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 47 patients were included, with a mean age of 60.6 ± 17.12 years. Most patients were female (61.7%) and had femoral neck fractures (63.8%). Surgical treatment was performed in 78.7% of cases. The overall mortality rate was 6.4%, and 17.0% of patients experienced complications, including gait disturbances, bleeding, and deep vein thrombosis. Mortality was significantly associated with conservative treatment (P = 0.007). All deaths occurred in the conservatively treated group. Longer hospital stays were linked to pre-operative anticoagulant use (P = 0.011) and osteoporosis (P = 0.03). CONCLUSION: Surgical management of pathological hip fractures was associated with improved survival and should be prioritized when clinically feasible. Awareness of pre-operative anticoagulant use and osteoporosis is essential for perioperative planning and may help reduce prolonged hospitalization in this high-risk population.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted, which included all adult patients diagnosed with pathological hip fractures from 2016 to 2024. Demographics, fracture type, type of treatment, complications, and outcomes data were evaluated.

title: Limb Salvage in Limb-Threatening Necrotizing Fasciitis of the Diabetic Foot: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Necrotizing fasciitis (NF) is a rapidly progressive soft tissue infection with high morbidity and mortality, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus. Early diagnosis is challenging because initial clinical signs may be subtle, yet timely intervention is critical to prevent limb loss and death. CASE REPORT: We report a 68-year-old male with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus and multiple comorbidities who presented with a 1-week history of rapidly progressive left foot pain and swelling extending to the mid-calf. Laboratory investigations revealed marked inflammation, and imaging indicated fascial involvement. The patient underwent multiple surgical debridements, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, strict glycemic control, limb off-loading, tibial angioplasty to optimize perfusion, and advanced wound care including negative pressure wound therapy and reconstructive procedures. Progressive healing was achieved without major amputation. CONCLUSION: Limb salvage remains feasible in selected diabetic patients with limb-threatening NF when early recognition, aggressive surgical management, vascular optimization, metabolic control, and coordinated multidisciplinary care are implemented.

title: Nomogram for Postoperative Permanent Neurologic Dysfunction Following Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Multicentral Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Permanent neurologic dysfunction (PND) often complicates following surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and is strongly correlated with unfavorable outcomes. Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance. METHODS: This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set. We used logistic regression to identify predictors and developed a nomogram, which was assessed using the area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision curve analysis. External validation was conducted using the validation set. RESULTS: In this study, 169 cases were finally collected (117 in the training set and 52 in the validation set), of whom 64 patients developed postoperative PND. Four risk factors were identified: brachiocephalic trunk dissection at the bifurcation plane, chronic kidney disease, age over 50, and cross-clamp duration over 168 min. The AUC was 0.809 for the training set and 0.736 for the validation set. The nomogram model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, and decision curve analysis potential clinical utility for predicting postoperative PND risk for thresholds of 1%-90% in the training set and 3%-75% in the validation set. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and validated a predictive model for assessing the risk of postoperative PND in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery, which may assist clinicians in individualized risk assessment.

Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance. title: Ethnic Differences in Clinical Manifestations of Behçet's Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Turkic and Non-Turkic Patients.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis with clinical heterogeneity that may vary across ethnic groups within the same country. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the clinical manifestations, immunogenic laboratory findings and disease course of BD by comparing Turkic and non-Turkic patients in a large Iranian referral cohort. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 2697 patients with BD followed at the BD clinic of Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2019 were included. RESULTS: Patients were stratified by ethnicity into Turkic (N = 1037; 38.5%) and non-Turkic (N = 1660; 61.5% [with Persian/Fars, N = 980 subgrouping]) groups, and demographic, clinical manifestations, and immunogenic laboratory findings were extracted from medical records. Mean age at BD onset was 25.72 ± 10.02 years in Turkic patients and 24.69 ± 10.23 years in non-Turkic patients, and males comprised 61.3% and 57.1% of the two groups, respectively. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-B5 positivity was 55.1% in Turkic versus 53.1% in non-Turkic patients, and HLA-B51 positivity was 48.7% versus 46.5%, respectively. Most clinical manifestations showed similar prevalence across groups, including oral aphthous ulcers (98.7% vs. 99.0%), genital aphthous ulcers (60.5% vs. 62.0%), uveitis (50.1% vs. 53.2%), and deep vein thrombosis (5.3% vs. 5.1%). Superficial phlebitis was more frequent in Turkic patients (p = 0.02), and oral aphthous ulcers occurred earlier in Turkic patients (p = 0.023). A three-class latent class model demonstrated the best fit (BIC = 14,986.58). In multinomial logistic regression analysis, Turkic patients had slightly higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 0.91-1.33; p = 0.320) and slightly lower odds ratio of the multisystem phenotype (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.68-1.30; p = 0.692); however, neither association was statistically significant. Female gender was associated with higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype than the mucocutaneous-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.14-1.67; p = 0.001). CONCLUSION: In this large Iranian BD cohort, Turkic and non-Turkic patients exhibited broadly similar disease phenotypes and comparable HLA-B51 frequencies, with small but potentially relevant ethnic differences in the timing of oral ulcers and the frequency of superficial phlebitis. These findings suggest that ethnicity may influence BD phenotype through mechanisms beyond HLA-B51, possibly involving other immune-related genetic variants such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1(ERAP1), Interleukin (IL)-10. Of note, the significant differences observed in Turkic versus non-Turkic comparisons were not present in the Turkic versus Persian (Fars) comparison, indicating that the findings are not driven by a single ethnic subgroup.

title: Development of Aortic Stents from Open Surgery to Endovascular Therapy: A Brazilian Contribution to the Treatment of Aortic Diseases.
abstract: The treatment of aortic diseases has undergone profound transformation over the last decades, with the progressive incorporation of endovascular techniques either replacing or complementing conventional open surgical repair. The development of aortic stents represents one of the most significant milestones in this transition. This article reviews the historical, experimental, and clinical evolution of aortic stents, with emphasis on pioneering Brazilian contributions, including the experimental phase in animal models, the first clinical applications in aortic dissection, and the role of the national industry in the development and dissemination of these technologies. The impact of these innovations on contemporary cardiovascular surgical practice and future perspectives are also discussed.

title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: [Efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt for acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: M t t CI CI HR CI P HR CI P HR CI P P vs. t P To evaluate the efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PMT-TIPS) in patients with acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis (NCPVT).This is a retrospective case series study. The clinical data of 61 patients with acute NCPVT who underwent PMT combined with TIPS at Department of Endovascular Surgery, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between June 2017 and June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. There were 39 males and 22 females, with an age ((IQR)) of 49.0 (24.5)years (range:21 to 73 years). Paired sample-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test were used to compare liver volume and biochemical parameters before treatment and at 1 year after treatment. Independent sample-test was used to compare changes in liver volume between patients with different stent patency statuses. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate stent patency and symptom recurrence. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the factors associated with stent occlusion.Among the 61 patients, 7 (11.5%) died during hospitalization and 5 (8.2%) died within 30 days after discharge, most commonly due to bowel necrosis. The remaining 49 patients were followed up for 43 (34) months (range:4 to 94 months). During follow-up, stent occlusion occurred in 35 patients (71.4%), with a median primary patency of 13.0 months (95%: 7.3 to 18.7 months). Among the 35 patients with primary stent occlusion, 21 developed symptom recurrence, whereas symptom recurrence occurred in 4 of the 14 patients with sustained patency. Ten patients with stent occlusion underwent stent recanalization, with a median secondary patency of 21.0 months (95%: 16.8 to 25.2 months). Univariate Cox regression analysis showed that myeloproliferative neoplasms (=3.08, 95%: 1.48 to 6.42,=0.003) and dual-stent implantation (=2.26, 95%: 1.09 to 4.70,=0.036) were associated with an increased risk of stent occlusion; multivariate Cox regression further revealed that only myeloproliferative neoplasms (=2.75, 95%: 1.31 to 5.78,=0.008) was an independent risk factor. At one year post-procedure, inflammatory and coagulation markers improved, total liver volume decreased compared with baseline (=0.005), and the reduction in liver volume was greater in patients with patent stents than in those with stent occlusion ((-215.6±205.5)cm³(-3.5±236.5) cm³,=-3.505,=0.001).In patients with acute NCPVT, the PMT-TIPS technique is feasible, but long-term stent patency is limited. This technique can be used as a rescue strategy rather than a definitive treatment.

title: [Dominant false lumen flow and abnormally high shear stress: a hemodynamic analysis of multichanneled aortic dissection].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: To explore the hemodynamic characteristics of multichanneled aortic dissection (MCAD).This is a retrospective cohort study. Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA). Centered on 4 MCAD cases with preprocedural death, 4 non-preprocedural-death MCAD patients and 4 non-preprocedural-death DCAD patients with balanced baseline characteristics, complete preoperative CTA datasets and well-defined outcomes were matched, yielding a total of 12 male patients. The ages of patients in preprocedural-death MCAD group, non-preprocedural-death MCAD group and non-preprocedural- death DCAD group were (62.0±5.7) years (range:54 to 66 years), (61.5±5.8) years (range:54 to 67 years) and (61.3±8.1) years (range:52 to 71 years), respectively. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and patient-specific aortic models, preoperative hemodynamic indices were quantitatively analyzed, including blood flow velocity, pressure distribution, flow distribution, wall shear stress (WSS) and time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS).Hemodynamic analyses revealed a stepwise decreasing trend of false lumen (FL) flow rate across the three groups. The preoperative death MCAD group exhibited a significantly higher FL flow ((62.81±7.59)ml/s (range: 56.29 to 73.78 ml/s)) than the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((24.84±9.25)ml/s (range: 17.23 to 36.84 ml/s)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((11.86±5.62)ml/s (range: 6.72 to 19.84 ml/s)). The intergroup variation patterns of FL flow ratio and maximum FL TAWSS were highly consistent. The preoperative death MCAD group yielded values of 0.77±0.16 (range: 0.56 to 0.93) and (34.44±6.50)Pa (range: 27.54 to 41.38 Pa),which were elevated compared with the non-preoperative death MCAD group (0.44±0.17(range: 0.33 to 0.70), (15.46±7.75)Pa (range: 6.69 to 25.01 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group (0.22±0.11(range: 0.14 to 0.37), (20.80±7.34)Pa (range: 15.23 to 31.60 Pa)),whereas no obvious disparities were observed between the latter two groups. In addition,the maximum FL WSS in the preoperative death MCAD group reached (125.76±26.57)Pa (range: 87.55 to 147.91 Pa),markedly exceeding that of the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((64.89±30.45)Pa (range: 28.62 to 102.40 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((91.15±28.16)Pa (range: 61.51 to 126.41 Pa)).Elevated FL flow and abnormally high shear stress may correlate with poor outcomes in patients with MCAD,and these parameters could serve as potential biomechanical biomarkers. CFD simulation can act as an auxiliary tool to identify high-risk aortic dissection patients,which helps refine clinical management and facilitate individualized precision treatment for MCAD.

Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: CI To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ.This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results.The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase.The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

title: [Is there still a role for manual deployment techniques in the era of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair? Normative boundaries and practical value in the management of hostile aortic landing zones].
abstract: Standard endovascular aortic repair has been widely used for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysms and selected complex aortic diseases because of its minimally invasive nature, rapid recovery, and favorable perioperative safety profile. However, in hostile aortic landing zones characterized by a short neck, severe angulation, conical neck configuration, mural thrombus, or circumferential calcification, standard endovascular repair remains associated with inadequate proximal apposition, type Ⅰ endoleak, endograft migration, and secondary intervention. Manual deployment techniques, including the push-up technique, reverse slider technique, Kabedon technique, and stepwise controlled deployment, may improve endograft axial alignment, proximal edge positioning, and local wall apposition to some extent; however, their role is mainly limited to optimization of the deployment process and cannot replace the principle of a durable sealing zone. This review summarizes the anatomical characteristics of hostile aortic landing zones, the mechanisms and clinical evidence of manual deployment techniques, the standardized value of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair and physician-modified endografts, adjunctive fixation and intraoperative bailout techniques, and application scenarios in emergency repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms. The aim is to provide a practical reference for rational selection between optimized deployment of standard endografts and complex sealing-zone reconstruction in complex endovascular aortic repair.

title: [Technical considerations and advances in distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia of the lower extremities].
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the end stage of lower extremity arterial disease and is associated with high rates of disability and mortality. With the rapid advancement of endovascular techniques, an "endovascular-first" strategy has become widely adopted. However, for patients with complex, long-segment, heavily calcified, diffuse, inflammatory lesions, or those with repeated endovascular failure, distal bypass surgery remains an indispensable option for limb salvage. The success of distal bypass depends not only on advanced surgical expertise but also on appropriate patient selection, accurate assessment of inflow and outflow tracts, optimal conduit choice, and meticulous perioperative management. Based on recent international guidelines and clinical evidence, this review focuses on key technical aspects of distal bypass, including inflow selection, target artery assessment, conduit selection, graft tunneling, distal anastomosis, intraoperative flow assessment, postoperative antithrombotic therapy and wound management. It also discusses the appropriate role of these techniques in the comprehensive treatment of CLTI based on recent evidence-based medical findings. In addition, emerging developments such as alternative conduits, and gene/cell therapy are discussed, aiming to provide insights into optimizing revascularization strategies for patients with CLTI.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.
