title: Update of a living network meta-analysis comparing noncompounded 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (Varithena) ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation in chronic venous insufficiency.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (PEM) and endovenous thermal ablation (ETA) for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when PEM was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026. No changes were made to selection criteria. Vein closure, deep venous thrombosis, and ulcer healing were summarized as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A composite outcome of disease-specific quality of life (QoL) or symptom improvement scales was summarized with Hedges' g standardized mean difference. RESULTS: The updated search yielded 507 new citations and 11 new eligible studies, for a total of 24 studies (235,413 patients). PEM was not statistically different from ETA for vein closure (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.42-1.21). A sensitivity analysis at longest follow-up (mean, 28 months; range, 12-72 months) showed similar results (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.45-1.11). There was no evidence of increased deep venous thrombosis risk with PEM vs ETA (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.29-2.43). Post-treatment improvement in disease-specific QoL or venous insufficiency symptoms showed no statistically significant difference between PEM and ETA (Hedges' g standardized mean difference, 0.04; 95% CI, -0.16 to 0.25), though the network was not fully connected. Finally, ulcer healing data was limited, but an exploratory analysis found no evidence of a statistically significant difference. CONCLUSIONS: This living network meta-analysis update reinforced the original findings that 1% PEM is not statistically different from ETA for venous closure or deep venous thrombosis in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency, and adds new preliminary information on outcomes relevant to the patient experience. There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference between PEM ablation and ETA for a composite of disease-specific QoL and symptom improvement, or for ulcer healing. The living approach maintains rigor and efficiently keeps evidence current as new studies emerge.

This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026.

title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression. RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

title: [Acute management of minor ischemic stroke].
abstract: This review summarizes acute-phase treatment for minor ischemic stroke, focusing on the latest evidence for reperfusion therapy and acute antithrombotic treatment. In patients with large vessel occlusion, the benefit of mechanical thrombectomy is not established and the risk of hemorrhage exists; therefore, indications should be judged carefully for each patient. Intravenous thrombolysis provides limited benefit in non-disabling cases, and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) can be an option. For minor non-cardioembolic stroke, early DAPT is recommended, and the possible role of adding argatroban is promising, especially for suspected branch atheromatous disease. For cardioembolic stroke, early initiation of a direct oral anticoagulant is desirable in mild cases without a large infarct.

title: Patient-specific finite element modeling of image-derived shell morphoelastic growth: A general framework and application to stented aortic dissection.
abstract: Vascular pathology often manifests in complex shape evolution visualized by longitudinal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing. While existing shell growth formulations can mitigate this burden, they require nontrivial FE implementation especially in commercial softwares (e.g., Abaqus) and their efficacy in patient-specific geometries under complex loading is unclear. In this work, we present a general computational framework to implement shell morphoelastic growth computed directly from registered patient-specific CT images. This shell implementation is validated against solid 3D formulations, allows thickness tunability, and increases compatibility with CT surfaces. We demonstrate the robustness of this formulation through modeling post-operative growth in a patient-specific aortic dissection under stent-based loading. Results first show that complex stent-based loading can deform the shell dissection flap to reproduce post-operative geometry. The outer aortic wall is then given a growth field calculated from registration of 1-month and 5-year post-operative CT images, which is implemented along with stent-based loading and pressurization. Results from this model capture the trends in total and lumen morphological evolution observed at intermediate timepoints. These findings establish a general framework, validated with a patient-specific case study of aortic dissection, with the potential to expand to other complex systems, scale to larger patient populations, and apply G&R to clinical translation.

Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes reveal hepatic regulatory mechanisms of residual feed intake during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize hepatic molecular features associated with residual feed intake (RFI) during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes. RFI was measured in 478 individually caged male Langya chickens from 96 to 133 days of age. After the feeding trial, the chickens were ranked in ascending order of RFI and classified into low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) subpopulations using the population mean RFI as the cutoff. Eight healthy chickens were then randomly selected from each subpopulation to form the LRFI and HRFI groups (n = 8 per group). Following slaughter and tissue collection at 133 days of age, hepatic transcriptomic and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomic analyzes were conducted. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) were subsequently subjected to enrichment and correlation analyzes. Compared with HRFI chickens, LRFI chickens had lower feed intake (FI) and higher eviscerated carcass yield and breast muscle yield. They also had lower abdominal fat percentage and muscle fat width, whereas BWG and metabolic body weight were similar between groups. Liver profiling identified 850 DEGs and 282 DAMs. Integrated KEGG analysis identified 15 pathways significantly enriched in both datasets. The amino acid metabolism-related pathways among these shared pathways collectively pointed to aromatic amino acid (AAA)-related metabolism, including biosynthesis of amino acids, phenylalanine metabolism, phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis, and tryptophan metabolism. A total of 16 DEGs and 29 DAMs were mapped to these pathways and showed widespread significant correlations. Among them, IL4I1, AFMID, ASS1, PHGDH, MAOB, IDO2, HAAO, and PAH were identified as candidate genes associated with RFI. These results characterized hepatic molecular features associated with RFI during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. These findings indicate that hepatic AAA-related metabolism may play a potential role in RFI divergence during the late growth stage in slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. The identified AAA metabolism-related pathways provide a focused set of candidate genes, metabolites, and pathways for further investigation of their roles in RFI and feed efficiency, and provide a theoretical basis for molecular breeding and breed conservation of slow-growing broilers.

After the feeding trial, the chickens were ranked in ascending order of RFI and classified into low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) subpopulations using the population mean RFI as the cutoff.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. title: Surgical management of splenic artery aneurysms: a case series of three patients with diverse presentations.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenic artery aneurysm (SAA) is the most common visceral artery aneurysm and includes true aneurysms and pseudoaneurysms, which have different etiologies and clinical behavior. Presentation ranges from incidental detection to life-threatening rupture with hemoperitoneum. Management depends on aneurysm size, symptoms, morphology, anatomical relationships, comorbidities, and rupture status. METHODS: We retrospectively described three consecutive patients with SAA or pseudoaneurysm treated surgically at a tertiary surgical center, Loghman Hakim Hospital, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran, between 2020 and 2025. Clinical records, imaging, operative findings, histopathology, postoperative course, and available follow-up were reviewed. The series was reported in accordance with the PROCESS 2025 reporting guideline. CASE PRESENTATIONS: Case 1 was a 66-year-old man with chronic liver disease and thrombocytopenia in whom a giant true SAA measuring approximately 72 × 68 × 76 mm was incidentally identified during trauma imaging. The aneurysm was adjacent to the pancreatic body without rupture. Elective open splenectomy with aneurysm resection and concurrent liver wedge biopsy was performed. Case 2 was a 63-year-old woman with a 7-month history of postprandial epigastric pain and a symptomatic true SAA of undocumented size. Elective open resection with splenectomy was performed; histopathology unexpectedly demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous splenitis. Case 3 was a 38-year-old woman with sickle cell disease who developed acute abdominal pain after a generalized seizure, with severe anemia and hemoperitoneum. A ruptured splenic artery pseudoaneurysm was identified at emergency laparotomy after a ruptured ectopic pregnancy had initially been suspected. RESULTS: All three patients underwent open splenectomy with aneurysm excision, which was elective in cases 1 and 2 and emergent in case 3. There were no intraoperative deaths or reoperations. All three patients had uneventful postoperative recoveries. 6-month follow-up was available for case 1; longer-term uniform follow-up was not available for all patients. CONCLUSION: SAAs encompass a broad clinical spectrum, from incidentally discovered giant aneurysms to symptomatic lesions and catastrophic rupture. These cases illustrate the importance of anatomy-directed treatment selection, early recognition of rupture, and consideration of vascular causes in patients with unexplained hemoperitoneum. Endovascular therapy is preferred for anatomically suitable elective lesions, whereas open surgery remains an important option for giant, complex, or ruptured aneurysms. The proposed algorithm is an educational synthesis of published evidence, current Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommendations, and the clinical experience represented by this institutional series rather than a prospectively validated decision tool.

title: Early functional outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy in patients with large vessel occlusion and active cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Evaluating mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large vessel occlusion stroke (LVOS) and active cancer (AC) is challenging because cancer-related mortality substantially affects conventional functional outcomes. This study aimed to assess the association between MT and early functional outcomes while minimizing the confounding impact of cancer-related death. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with LVOS and AC between January 2016 and December 2024. Patients were categorized into MT and non-MT groups. The primary outcome was the distribution of modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores at 2 weeks, analyzed using ordinal logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis excluding patients who died from cancer progression within 2 weeks of stroke onset was also performed. LVOS was defined as ischemic stroke with occlusion of the intra- or extracranial internal carotid artery, middle cerebral artery (M1 or M2 segments), or basilar artery. RESULTS: Among 72 patients with LVOS and AC (median age, 76 years; 36 women), 32 (44%) underwent MT (28 MT alone, and 4 MT procedures combined with intravenous thrombolysis), whereas 3 patients in the non-MT group received intravenous thrombolysis alone. At 2 weeks, MT was significantly associated with a favorable shift in mRS distribution (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-9.97; p = 0.020). In a sensitivity analysis excluding cancer-related deaths, this association remained significant, with a larger effect size (adjusted OR, 6.21, 95% CI, 1.89-20.47; p = 0.003). CONCLUSION: MT was associated with improved early functional outcomes in patients with LVOS and AC.

This study aimed to assess the association between MT and early functional outcomes while minimizing the confounding impact of cancer-related death. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with LVOS and AC between January 2016 and December 2024.

title: Cortical Destruction due to a Postoperative Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysm: A Case Report.
abstract: CASE: Periprosthetic cortical destruction due to vascular complications is exceptionally rare, with only a few cases reported. We present an 82-year-old man with progressive hip pain 2 years after γ-nail fixation. Imaging revealed a large cortical defect of the proximal medial femur. CT-angiography demonstrated a pseudoaneurysm of the profunda femoris artery. Endovascular stent grafting was performed. The patient's symptoms resolved, and cortical remodeling was observed at 4 months. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of considering vascular injury in the differential diagnosis of late postoperative hip pain and illustrates that timely recognition can guide adequate treatment and ensure favorable outcomes.

title: 6 The emerging role of mA in aortic dissection: from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic potential.
abstract: 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 Aortic dissection (AD) is an emergent medical condition with a hidden onset and sudden rupture, which usually results in a high mortality rate. N6-methyladenosine (mA) is the most abundant modification in eukaryotic RNA molecules and plays a critical role in regulating RNA metabolism. Dysregulation of mA modification has been linked to a variety of diseases. Interestingly, aberrant expression of mA-associated factors is observed in AD. The mA methylation can promote or inhibit the development of AD by modulating cell death, oxidative stress, macrophage polarization and VSMC phenotype switching, depending on mA-modified transcripts, readers and downstream pathways. In addition, mA exerts a significant effect on the major risk factors for AD, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, obesity and aortic aneurysm. Thus, modulating mA modification by small-molecule inhibitors, natural products or miRNAs may represent a promising approach for developing new therapeutic interventions for AD. In this review, we first give a brief perspective on mA modification and its regulators. Subsequently, we summarize the recent research progress on the role of mA in AD and related-risk factors, with an emphasis on its diagnostic value and therapeutic potential.

title: Early antithrombotic therapy improves 90-day functional outcomes in patients with postinterventional cerebral hyperdensity after mechanical thrombectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Postinterventional cerebral hyperdensity (PCHD) is a specific type of hyperdensity commonly observed on computed tomography (CT) scans of the head after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This study aimed to investigate the association between early antithrombotic therapy (EAT) and 90-day functional outcomes in anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (acAIS) patients with PCHD. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 141 consecutive acAIS patients with PCHD after MT. EAT was defined as antithrombotic therapy administered within 24 h post-MT. The primary outcome was a favorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2). The secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, ΔmRS (defined as the mRS score before MT minus the 90-day mRS score), enlargement of cerebral hyperdensity, and persistent hyperdensity on the 24-h follow-up CT graded by the European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study (ECASS III) morphology. Baseline and outcome data were compared between the EAT and non-EAT groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between EAT and favorable outcomes. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the robustness and internal consistency of the results. RESULTS: p p p p Of the 129 patients with complete 90-day mRS data, 59 (45.7%) received EAT. The EAT group had a higher proportion of favorable outcomes (59.3% vs. 37.1%,= 0.019). A multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that EAT remained significantly associated with favorable outcomes (Model 1: odds ratio (OR) 2.469, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.195-5.104,= 0.015; Model 2: OR 2.72, 95% CI 1.02-7.20,= 0.045; Model 3: OR 3.68, 95% CI 1.32-10.30,= 0.013), and the results were consistent after imputation based on discharge data and multiple imputation. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses showed consistent results, with no significant interaction effects observed. CONCLUSION: EAT is associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in acAIS patients with PCHD, warranting further investigation in larger prospective studies.

This study aimed to investigate the association between early antithrombotic therapy (EAT) and 90-day functional outcomes in anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (acAIS) patients with PCHD. title: Association of the triglyceride-glucose index with the severity of lower extremity arterial disease across glucose metabolic states: a single-center cross-sectional study of 656 patients with angiographically confirmed disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the cross-sectional association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the severity of lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) in hospitalized patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD, to test whether this association differs across Glucose Metabolic States, and to quantify the ability of the TyG index to discriminate prevalent ischemic tissue loss (Rutherford grades 5-6). METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 656 consecutive patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD who were hospitalized in the Department of Vascular Surgery at the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University from January 2023 through December 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed by digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Patients were classified into four groups according to their Glucose Metabolic States: normal glucose tolerance (NGT, n = 150), impaired glucose regulation (IGR, n = 148), diabetes with a duration of <10 years (DM<10y, n = 174), and diabetes with a duration of ≥10 years (DM≥10y, n = 184). Glucose and lipid parameters and LEAD severity (Rutherford classification) were assessed during the same hospitalization. Spearman correlation, multinomial logistic regression (with grade 1 mild claudication as the reference), ordinal logistic regression with a TyG × Glucose Metabolic States interaction term, proportional-odds assessment by cumulative binary splits, ROC analysis with bootstrap internal validation (1,000 resamples), and decision-curve analysis were performed. Sensitivity analyses used continuous glycemic measures instead of the categorical groups, excluded implausibly low fasting glucose values, and added liver enzymes to the adjustment set. The primary outcome was ischemic tissue loss, defined as Rutherford grades 5-6 (n = 205, 31.2%). RESULTS: The TyG index increased progressively across Glucose Metabolic States categories (8.79 ± 0.51, 9.15 ± 0.48, 9.57 ± 0.56, and 9.67 ± 0.52 for NGT, IGR, DM < 10 years, and DM ≥ 10 years, respectively; P < 0.001) and was strongly correlated with Rutherford grade (Spearman r = 0.677, P < 0.001). In a multinomial logistic regression model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, BMI, and fatty liver disease (all variance inflation factors < 1.5), the TyG index remained associated with each severity category above the reference, with adjusted odds ratios per 0.5-unit increment of 2.51 (grade 2), 2.83 (grade 3), 7.56 (grade 4), 9.62 (grade 5), and 20.45 (grade 6). The interaction between TyG and Glucose Metabolic States was statistically significant (likelihood-ratio χ² = 95.63, df = 3, P < 0.001); stratum-specific odds ratios per 0.5-unit increment were 1.51 (95% CI 1.07-2.13) in IGR, 2.50 (1.90-3.29) in DM < 10 years, and 8.14 (5.23-12.67) in DM ≥ 10 years, whereas the NGT-stratum estimate was unstable (quasi-complete separation) and could not be interpreted. When the categorical groups were replaced with a continuous glycemic measure, the interaction with fasting plasma glucose remained significant but was in the opposite direction (χ² = 9.36, df = 1, P = 0.002): the TyG-severity association was stronger at lower fasting glucose levels (OR per 0.5 unit 4.81 at 4.8 mmol/L) than at higher fasting glucose levels (3.46 at 8.3 mmol/L). For discriminating Rutherford grades 5-6, the AUC was 0.833 (95% CI 0.796-0.870); the Youden-optimal cutoff was 9.42 (sensitivity 85.9%, specificity 71.0%, positive predictive value 57.3%, negative predictive value 91.7%, LR + 2.96, LR- 0.199), and this cutoff was stable across bootstrap resamples. Decision-curve analysis showed a positive net benefit relative to treat-all or treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.09-0.57. CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD, the TyG index was independently associated with LEAD severity. The strength of this association appeared to vary across Glucose Metabolic States, but the apparent gradient from normal glucose tolerance to long-standing diabetes was not reproduced when glucose was modelled continuously, suggesting that part of the categorical pattern is attributable to the grouping itself (i.e., mathematical coupling and range restriction). The TyG index showed moderate ability to discriminate prevalent ischemic tissue loss. Because exposure and outcome were assessed during the same hospitalization, these findings represent a cross-sectional association rather than a predictive one; the proposed cutoff values were derived from the same sample in which they were evaluated and require external validation before they can be considered for clinical use.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 656 consecutive patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD who were hospitalized in the Department of Vascular Surgery at the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University from January 2023 through December 2024. title: Case Report: Fetal giant congenital hemangioma with arteriovenous malformation: to be or not to be.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study reports a rare and life-threatening case of a giant congenital hemangioma with arteriovenous fistula in a neonate and describes its clinical management and outcomes. METHOD: A female neonate with a giant right forearm hemangioma with arteriovenous fistula, detected prenatally at 23 weeks, was managed by a multidisciplinary team. Postnatally, the infant developed severe pulmonary hypertension and active bleeding from the mass. Diagnosis was confirmed via computed tomography angiography and arteriography. Emergency intervention with combined embolization coil and sclerotherapy was performed, followed by oral propranolol therapy. RESULTS: Following the combined intervention and pharmacotherapy, the condition of the infant improved significantly. The severe pulmonary hypertension resolved, and the tumor size progressively reduced. CONCLUSION: Congenital hemangioma combined with arteriovenous malformation can lead to severe, life-threatening complications. A prompt, multidisciplinary approach involving embolization, sclerotherapy, and pharmacotherapy can achieve favorable outcomes, underscoring the importance of early recognition and integrated perinatal management.

title: Added value of brain perfusion ultrasound to prehospital stroke scales-a secondary analysis of the SONAS trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Accurate prehospital identification of acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is critical to guide selection of an optimal target hospital for either intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) alone and/or mechanical thrombectomy (MT). The novel portable non-imaging brain perfusion ultrasound (BPU) device SONAS(TM) indicated similar sensitivity and specificity as prehospital stroke scales. In this study, we reanalyzed data from the original 20 patient cohort to evaluate whether combining BPU with prehospital stroke scales (ph-SS) can further improve LVO detection. METHODS: Clinical data and NIHSS scores of all patients suffering from acute ischemic stroke with and without proven LVO in the SONAS trial were collected and applied to 16 different phSS. As an exploratory analysis we also applied a prehospital score for intracerebral hemorrhage (ph-ICH) to this cohort. The positive and negative predictive values as well as sensitivity and specificity were analyzed retrospectively for both methods. RESULTS: The best performing phSS, CG-FAST, and RACE, showed comparable performances to BPU, but still misdiagnosed patients. However, in our specific cohort, the combination of both methods allowed for a reliable classification into three groups: (A) "highly probably LVO", (B) "highly probable non-LVO" and (C) "not assessable" (including all patients misdiagnosed by one method alone). The addition of BPU resulted in shifts towards higher sensitivity and NPV. When using the ph-ICH score three patients were classified as ICH (false positive), and all of them showed severe perfusion deficits in BPU indicating LVO. CONCLUSION: The combination of BPU with phSS may hold the potential to enhance prehospital triage of acute stroke patients selecting patients to (A) endovascular-capable centers, (B) the nearest stroke unit for, i.e., IVT or (C) either depending on other clinical factors and local circumstances. However, validation is critical in stroke-call patients in the prehospital setting including application by paramedics with/without emergency physicians or telemedical support, and compared to other prehospital point-of-care diagnostics both in respect to sensitivity/specificity, timeline and, ultimately, costs. In the future, the addition of serum biomarkers for ICH may open new opportunities for early ICH treatment or even enable prehospital IVT, and/or streamline direct to angio-suite approaches in confirmed LVO.

title: Spatial multi-omics implicates vascular adipocytes proximal to tertiary lymphoid structures in human aortic aneurysm and B-cell autoreactivity.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Perivascular Adipose Tissue (PVAT), tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS), and the B lymphocytes they harbor have been implicated in regulating vascular diseases, including abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Yet, the relationship of adipose tissue to TLS and B-cell responses is poorly understood. APPROACH AND RESULTS: Here, using multi-omics approaches, we characterized the potential interplay of vascular adipocytes and TLSs in shaping microenvironments conducive to pathogenic B-cell immunity in human AAA pathology. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing identified white adipocytes expressing transcripts for lipogenesis, lipolysis, and extracellular remodeling. Unexpectedly, these adipocytes expressed haptotactic and chemotactic factors such as thrombospondin 1 and autotaxin, and extracellular matrix proteins with potential to recruit CD44+ leukocytes within AAAs. Immunohistology revealed two anatomical compartments for the adipocytes within AAAs: PVAT and the medial-adventitial region. Medial-adventitial adipocytes were frequently associated with CD44+ TLSs and were largely absent from control non-aneurysmal abdominal aortas. Visium HD spatial transcriptomics revealed mature TLSs recapitulated the organization of functional secondary lymphoid structures, with multiple B-cell follicles clustered to form a nodular structure partly covered by a layer of smooth muscle cells. The TLSs harbored isotype-switched B cells expressing IgG1, IgG3, or IgA, with dominant kappa chain usage and IgG antibodies to the aortic wall. Myeloid cells in AAA were implicated in promoting B-cell effects, as they were the primary producers of B-cell activating factor (BAFF), a cytokine that promotes B-cell infiltration, survival, and function. CONCLUSION: Altogether, our results support a model in which new adipocytes in the medial-adventitial layer elicit inflammatory pathways that promote early TLS formation, and BAFF produced by myeloid cells promotes the survival and maturation of vascular wall-antigen-exposed B cells, leading to mature TLS formation, production of antibodies to AAA antigens, fueling inflammation and AAA growth. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Despite multiple drugs showing efficacy in preclinical animal models, no non-surgical treatments are available for AAAs. Therefore, we re-evaluated human aortic aneurysm pathology using new technologies to better understand human aneurysm pathogenesis. The results revealed formation of novel adipocytes in the medial-adventitial region of human AAAs. These vascular adipocytes exacerbate inflammation by attracting an arsenal of immune cells to the medial-adventitial region. B-cell activating factor (BAFF) further exacerbates the B-cell immune response by supporting the formation of mature tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) and production of antibodies against AAA tissue. While more studies are needed to confirm these findings, this work opens new avenues of investigation for potential therapeutics for treating small AAAs. Particularly, repurposing anti-adipogenesis drugs and anti-BAFF therapeutics may attenuate B-cell immune responses, inflammation, and AAA growth.

title: Percutaneous device closure of a massive pseudoaneurysm of the descending aorta in a paediatric patient with Takayasu arteritis.
abstract: TM Takayasu arteritis (TA) is commonly known as a disease of young women, highly prevalent in Asia and Central America, and associated with multiple vascular complications. Although it is well described in the paediatric population, severe complications are rarely seen. A 6-year-old girl was referred to our institution with features suggestive of a tuberculosis infection, along with a suspected intrathoracic mass on preliminary imaging. Further investigations confirmed the mass to be a massive pseudoaneurysm originating from the descending aorta and extending into the left hemithorax. A multidisciplinary discussion concluded that this pseudoaneurysm carried a high mortality risk with a direct surgical approach. This case report describes the use of an Amplatzerseptal occluder as a bridge to surgical excision of the massive pseudoaneurysm in a paediatric patient with confirmed TA.

title: Ascending and hemi arch replacement during bilateral orthotopic lung transplant: a case report.
abstract: Lung transplant candidates increasingly have concomitant cardiac disease. Prior studies have demonstrated the safety of lung transplant with concurrent cardiac surgery in small case series. Here, we describe a case of ascending aorta replacement at the same time as bilateral lung transplant utilizing a clamshell incision. The patient recovered well. With this case report, we aim to contribute to the growing literature showing the safety of concomitant heart and aortic surgery during lung transplant.

title: Factors associated with failures and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: to analyze factors associated with catheter progression failure and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters inserted by nurses in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. METHOD: observational cohort study was conducted with hospitalized COVID-19 patients, following the STROBE guidelines. Categorical variables were described as absolute and relative frequencies; quantitative variables were expressed as median and interquartile range. Non-parametric tests were applied due to non-normal distribution. Associations were analyzed using Pearson's chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression was performed for variables associated with outcomes. RESULTS: a total of 1061 Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters were analyzed. The main indications were for antibiotic therapy, and most catheters were removed after treatment completion. First-attempt failure and clinical patient profile were associated with catheter progression failure. Subcutaneous heparin was a protective factor. Among Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters successfully inserted, tip confirmation via chest X-ray and catheter-to-vessel ratio between 31%-40% were associated with thrombosis, whereas Sherlock™ confirmation was protective. CONCLUSION: catheter progression failure was associated with clinical conditions and first-attempt failure. Adverse outcomes were associated with X-ray tip confirmation and catheter-to-vessel ratio, whereas Sherlock™ use and subcutaneous heparin were protective factors.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of between-study variance (odds ratios [ORs]); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI). RESULTS: Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (eight studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%. CONCLUSION: In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.

title: Contact Aspiration Versus Combined Thrombectomy in Basilar Artery Occlusion: Clinical Severity and First-pass Recanalization Are Associated with Outcome.
abstract: PURPOSE: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) carries high rates of death and disability despite endovascular therapy, and the optimal technique remains unclear. We compared contact aspiration (CA) alone with combined CA plus stent retriever (CA + SR) and identified factors associated with first-pass reperfusion and 3‑month outcome. METHODS: In the prospective multicenter SARA-3 registry, the primary outcomes compared between CA and CA + SR were first-pass recanalization (modified Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b-3) and 3‑month functional independence. Secondary outcomes were final recanalization, procedural time, safety, 24‑h NIHSS, and mortality. Factors associated with unfavorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 3-6) were assessed by Firth penalized logistic regression, with first-line technique forced in as a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Among 68 patients (median admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] 11), 50 (73.5%) received CA and 18 (26.5%) CA + SR. The two techniques showed no statistically significant differences in reperfusion, safety, or 3‑month unfavorable outcome (48% vs. 53%; underpowered), but CA was faster (21 vs. 38 min; P = 0.007). Admission NIHSS (odds ratio [OR] 1.08 per point; P = 0.004) and first-pass mTICI 2b-3 (OR 0.06; P < 0.001) were independently associated with outcome; their combination discriminated well (area under the curve 0.83). Forcing technique into the model did not change these associations (CA + SR adjusted OR 1.19; P = 0.81). No baseline characteristic was independently associated with first-pass reperfusion. CONCLUSIONS: CA and CA + SR showed no statistically significant difference in 3‑month outcomes, but CA was faster. First-line technique was not associated with functional outcome; instead, outcome reflected baseline stroke severity and first-pass reperfusion, which defined prognostic groups that may aid risk stratification if externally validated.

title: Mechanical and Hemodynamic Effects of Balloon-Expandable and Self-Expanding Stents in a Saccular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Model: Fluid-Structure Interaction Analyses.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare the effects of balloon-expandable and self-expanding stents on vessel wall mechanics and hemodynamics in a patient-specific saccular abdominal aortic aneurysm model. METHODS: A patient-specific aneurysm model was constructed using computed tomography images, and balloon-expandable and self-expanding stent models were created. Aortic wall stress was evaluated by contact analysis. Fluid-structure interaction analyses were performed at 5 representative phases selected from the cardiac cycle. Mean intra-aneurysmal flow velocity, wall shear stress (WSS), pressure loss, and energy loss were compared. RESULTS: The balloon-expandable stent produced greater localized aortic wall stress than the self-expanding stent, whereas wall stress was more uniformly distributed with the self-expanding stent. Both stents reduced the mean intra-aneurysmal flow velocity, WSS, pressure loss, and energy loss compared with the no-stent model. However, greater reductions in WSS, pressure loss, and energy loss were noted with the balloon-expandable stent than with the self-expanding stent. CONCLUSIONS: Balloon-expandable and self-expanding stents exhibited different effects on vessel wall mechanics and hemodynamics. The findings indicate the importance of evaluating both hemodynamic and mechanical effects when assessing stent-vessel interactions.

METHODS: A patient-specific aneurysm model was constructed using computed tomography images, and balloon-expandable and self-expanding stent models were created. Aortic wall stress was evaluated by contact analysis.

title: Ortner's syndrome associated with a saccular aortic arch aneurysm presenting as isolated unilateral vocal cord paralysis: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ortner's syndrome, or cardiovocal syndrome, is an uncommon cause of recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy due to cardiovascular pathology. Thoracic aortic aneurysm is a rare but important etiology that may present only with hoarseness. CASE PRESENTATION: An 85-year-old man with hypertension and a history of chronic smoking presented with progressive hoarseness for 1 month. Flexible laryngoscopy showed paralysis of the left vocal cord without laryngeal pathology. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a 22 × 17 mm saccular aneurysm arising from the distal aortic arch at the aortopulmonary window, with mural thrombus and in close proximity to the left recurrent laryngeal nerve. No cervical, mediastinal, pulmonary, or laryngeal malignancy was detected. Echocardiography showed preserved systolic function without significant valvular disease or pulmonary hypertension. Ortner's syndrome associated with the distal aortic arch aneurysm was considered the most likely diagnosis based on the clinical and radiological findings and the exclusion of other identifiable causes. Surgical repair was advised, but the patient declined and was managed conservatively. At the 11-month clinical follow-up, he remained stable with persistent hoarseness; no follow-up CT was performed. CLINICAL DISCUSSION: Aortic arch aneurysm is a rare cause of Ortner's syndrome and may mimic more common causes of unilateral vocal cord paralysis, particularly malignancy. Imaging along the recurrent laryngeal nerve pathway, including the thorax, is essential when laryngoscopy does not reveal a local cause. CONCLUSION: Unexplained left vocal cord paralysis should prompt an evaluation for cardiovascular causes. Early cross-sectional imaging can identify a thoracic aortic aneurysm and guide timely multidisciplinary management.

title: A VPS4A Microtubule-Interacting and Trafficking Domain Variant in a Child With Hypomyelination and Developmental Regression: A Case Report With Features of CIMDAG Syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy in infancy has a broad differential diagnosis. Heterozygous variants in VPS4A, an endosomal sorting complexes required for transport-associated AAA-ATPase, have been reported in CIMDAG (cerebellar hypoplasia-cataracts-impaired intellectual development-congenital microcephaly- dystonia-dyserythropoietic anemia-growth retardation) syndrome, a multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder with variable systemic involvement. METHODS: A 14-month-old girl presented with inability to crawl or walk and delayed milestones. Examination showed a head circumference of 43.5 cm, a depressed nasal bridge, bilateral 4th-5th toe clinodactyly, motor delay, and hypotonia. Metabolic screening and targeted genetic tests were nondiagnostic. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed diffuse deficient myelination, a thin corpus callosum, optic nerve hypoplasia, and basal ganglia signal abnormalities. At 2 years 7 months, the child re-presented with loss of independent sitting and speech, tremor, and epileptiform electroencephalography abnormalities. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging showed persistent deficient myelination despite mild interval progression of myelination. Echocardiography showed moderate mitral regurgitation and a patent foramen ovale. RESULTS: Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous VPS4A variant, NM_013245.3:c.217T>G (p.Tyr73Asp), reported as absent from population databases and previously unreported at the time of testing. Maternal testing was negative; paternal testing was unavailable. The laboratory classified the variant as a variant of uncertain significance. CONCLUSIONS: The clinical and imaging findings overlap with the VPS4A-associated CIMDAG spectrum. This case describes a candidate heterozygous microtubule-interacting and trafficking domain variant in a child with hypomyelination and regression; its contribution to the phenotype remains unconfirmed.

title: From hypoxia to thrombosis: a hypothesis-driven framework for pulmonary embolism risk in deep underground environments.
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. These factors may interact dynamically with oxygen sensing, cardiopulmonary compensation, venous return, endothelial function, and coagulation-inflammation pathways. However, the relationship between deep underground exposure, thrombogenesis, PE recognition, and prevention remains insufficiently conceptualized. Direct epidemiological evidence linking deep-underground occupational exposure to incident venous thromboembolism or PE remains scarce, and existing PE prediction tools have not been specifically validated in deep-underground occupational populations. Therefore, this review does not assume that underground exposure independently increases PE incidence or that established clinical tools are inadequate. Instead, we develop a hypothesis-driven framework to examine whether exposure-related factors-including oxygen fluctuation, heat and dehydration, restricted mobility, altered hemodynamics, and inflammatory stress-could modify thrombotic susceptibility, symptom interpretation, or the operational performance of conventional PE pathways. We summarize the environmental and physiological stressors relevant to PE, examine how they may amplify Virchow's triad, and discuss research questions concerning symptom recognition, anticoagulation, reperfusion decision-making, preventive interventions, and the staged development of dynamic risk warning models. This review aims to provide a conceptual foundation for future surveillance, prevention, and clinical research on PE in deep underground occupational populations.

title: Anticoagulation management in a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute pulmonary embolism undergoing ECMO-supported intervention: a case report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Protein S deficiency is a predominant form of hereditary thrombophilia in Asian populations. Pediatric venous thromboembolism (VTE) is exceedingly rare, with an incidence of only 0.2%-0.6%, and acute massive pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support in children with thrombophilia presents exceptional clinical challenges. The core therapeutic dilemma lies in reconciling the hypercoagulable state inherent to protein S deficiency with the high bleeding risk following thrombolytic therapy, compounded by the obligatory anticoagulation requirement during ECMO. This case report describes the nursing management of a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute PE who successfully underwent ECMO-supported interventional treatment under high bleeding risk. OUTCOME: The patient was successfully weaned from ECMO after 98 h of support, extubated on day 6, and discharged in stable condition after 30 days of hospitalization. At 6-month follow-up, no thrombus recurrence was observed, and the patient had fully resumed normal life and academic activities. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that an individualized low-dose heparin anticoagulation strategy, guided by the PEACE consensus and supported by meticulous monitoring, can effectively balance the competing risks of thrombosis and hemorrhage in pediatric ECMO patients with underlying thrombophilia and recent thrombolysis. Notably, as a single case report, this finding cannot be broadly generalized to all pediatric ECMO patients with thrombophilia. Instead, this case provides a potential framework for individualized anticoagulation and nursing management that requires further validation in larger pediatric cohorts. The nursing experience provides a practical reference for managing similar complex cases in pediatric critical care.

title: Dietary aromatic amino acids, their food sources, and incident hypertension in Chinese adults: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prospective evidence linking dietary aromatic amino acids (AAAs), including phenylalanine (Phe), tyrosine (Tyr), and tryptophan (Trp), to incident hypertension currently remains limited, particularly regarding their individual components and food sources. Herein, we examined the association between dietary AAAs, their food sources, and incident hypertension among Chinese adults. METHODS: Using the China Health and Nutrition Survey database, this prospective cohort study collected data from 10,087 adults without hypertension at baseline. Baseline dietary intake was assessed using three consecutive 24-h dietary recalls, combined with household food weighing; the energy-adjusted AAA intake was expressed in g/1,000 kcal. Incident hypertension was defined as measured blood pressure, physician diagnosis, or use of antihypertensive medication. Mixed-effects Cox proportional hazards models with household identifiers as random intercepts were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Dose-response, food-source-specific, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: During the 95,153 person-years of follow-up, 3,531 participants developed hypertension. In fully adjusted models, the highest quartile of total AAA intake was associated with a modestly higher risk of incident hypertension compared with the lowest quartile (HR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.31; P for trend = 0.006). Positive associations were more consistent for Phe (HR for Q4 vs. Q1, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44) and Trp (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.14-1.46) individually, while Tyr intake showed no significant association with hypertension. Dose-response analyses indicated approximately linear positive associations for total AAA, Phe, and Trp. The association for total AAA was attenuated following additional adjustment for baseline province (HR for Q4 vs. Q1, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.97-1.24), while the positive associations for Phe and Trp persisted. Cereals were the predominant contributors to AAA intake, and plant-derived Phe and Trp were positively associated with the risk of hypertension. CONCLUSION: Higher dietary intakes of Phe and Trp showed consistent positive associations with incident hypertension, while Tyr showed no clear association. The modest association for total AAA was attenuated after adjusting for baseline province and should therefore be interpreted cautiously in relation to potential regional confounding factors. These findings support the component-specific interpretation of dietary AAAs and consideration of their regional and food source contexts.

title: Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation. METHODS: A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations. RESULTS: Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance. DISCUSSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.

title: From revascularization to multimodal integrated therapy for peripheral arterial disease: immunomodulation, metabolic correction, and tissue engineering.
abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD), a critical manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis (AS), poses substantial therapeutic challenges. Despite pharmacological interventions and revascularization, efficacy remains constrained by high restenosis rates and suboptimal functional recovery. These limitations underscore a necessary transition from localized structural revascularization toward integrated systemic repair, with a particular focus on the underlying immunopathology. The progression of PAD is driven by a dysregulated immune response, characterized by an imbalance in macrophage polarization (M1/M2), overactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and a vicious cycle of immune-metabolic coupling. Current research trajectories emphasize the synergistic orchestration of the vascular microenvironment through immunomodulation. Beyond modulating localized inflammatory responses, emerging strategies target metabolic homeostasis and advanced tissue engineering, including spatiotemporal growth factor delivery, extracellular vesicle-based therapies, and bioengineered scaffolding systems. These interdisciplinary developments point toward a multimodal integrated therapeutic strategy for PAD. Such a strategy would build on conventional revascularization and may address its limitations, including restenosis, through targeted immunomodulation and local tissue regeneration. Whether this approach can improve long-term outcomes compared with revascularization alone remains to be tested. If validated, it could shift the clinical standard beyond vessel patency toward comprehensive, long-term vascular health.

title: Staphylococcus aureus -associated infected subclavian artery pseudoaneurysm treated with dual bare-metal stent implantation: a case report.
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus Infected subclavian artery aneurysms are exceedingly rare, life-threatening vascular lesions associated with high risks of rupture and mortality. We report a 70-year-old male presenting with intermittent hemoptysis, who was diagnosed with a pseudoaneurysm of the left subclavian artery adjacent to the dominant vertebral artery. Blood cultures confirmed methicillin-sensitiveinfection. The patient underwent endovascular repair with dual bare-metal stents to preserve vertebral artery perfusion. Hemoptysis completely resolved post-intervention. Complete thrombosis and occlusion of the aneurysm sac were achieved at the 3-month follow-up, with remarkable sac shrinkage observed at 6 months. This case suggests that dual bare-metal stents may represent a feasible potential treatment alternative for highly selected patients with infected subclavian artery aneurysms. Long-term safety and efficacy remain to be further verified. Long-term antimicrobial therapy and close surveillance remain mandatory.

title: Quality and reliability of short videos about type A aortic dissection on Bilibili and TikTok: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Short-video platforms such as TikTok and Bilibili have become important channels for health information dissemination, but the quality and reliability of TAAD-related videos remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the quality and reliability of TAAD-related short videos on TikTok and Bilibili, with particular attention to platform differences and uploader characteristics. METHODS: The top 250 videos ranked by comprehensive ranking on each platform were screened using the Chinese keyword "A." A total of 391 eligible videos were included. Uploaders were classified as medical practitioners, individual users, or institutions. Video quality and reliability were assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmarks, and Video Information Quality Instrument (VIQI). Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with video quality. RESULTS: TikTok videos showed higher engagement, whereas Bilibili videos were longer and provided broader coverage of epidemiology, etiology, and clinical presentation-related content. TikTok remained independently associated with higher VIQI scores after adjustment. Medical practitioners and institutions generally achieved higher VIQI and JAMA scores than individual users, and content coverage score was independently associated with higher video quality. However, mDISCERN scores did not differ significantly among uploader types. CONCLUSION: TAAD-related short videos demonstrated moderate overall quality but limited reliability. Platform characteristics, uploader type, and content coverage were associated with assessed information quality. Professional participation may improve some aspects of health communication, but uploader identity alone does not ensure higher reliability or transparency.

title: Yeast Mitochondrial Escape 1-Like as a Mitochondrial Gatekeeper in Aging-Related Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of aging and is closely linked to the progression of cardiovascular disease. Yeast mitochondrial escape 1-like (YME1L) is an adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent i-AAA (intermembrane space AAA, AAA=ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) protease embedded in the mitochondrial inner membrane that maintains mitochondrial homeostasis by regulating proteostasis, cristae architecture, and metabolic adaptation. Notably, YME1L influences mitochondrial fusion-fission dynamics, respiratory chain supercomplex organization, and oxidative phosphorylation efficiency through the regulated processing of optic atrophy protein 1 (OPA1). Accumulating evidence suggests that age-associated impairment of YME1L function contributes to mitochondrial fragmentation, energetic insufficiency, and reduced stress tolerance, particularly in long-lived, high-energy demand tissues. In the cardiovascular system, experimental models indicate that YME1L deficiency disrupts cristae organization, promotes maladaptive metabolic remodeling, and promotes heart failure-like phenotypes. Conversely, preservation of YME1L activity supports mitochondrial integrity and enhances cardiac resilience under hemodynamic stress. In addition to cardiomyocytes, YME1L also supports endothelial mitochondrial homeostasis, thereby linking mitochondrial proteostasis to vascular aging and diastolic dysfunction. Although YME1L has been extensively studied in cancer biology, its relevance to aging-related cardiovascular vulnerability is increasingly recognized, especially in cardio-oncology, where therapy-induced mitochondrial stress may be exacerbated by age-dependent decline in mitochondrial quality control. This review integrates current evidence supporting YME1L as a context-dependent regulator of mitochondrial stress adaptation, with particular emphasis on the roles of YME1L in cardiovascular aging, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and stress tolerance. Rather than positioning YME1L as a universal therapeutic target, we discuss how modulating YME1L-associated pathways may help preserve mitochondrial resilience and mitigate age-related cardiovascular dysfunction.

title: Trends, outcomes and patient- and hospital-level factors associated with sepsis following cesarean delivery: a propensity-matched nationwide inpatient analysis (2016-2022).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health concern and a serious complication of cesarean delivery. However, contemporary nationwide data describing both the temporal trend in post-cesarean sepsis and its downstream clinical and economic burden-particularly in propensity-matched comparisons-remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, propensity-matched analysis of all adult inpatients undergoing cesarean delivery recorded in the U.S. Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2016-2022). Sepsis and cesarean delivery were defined using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. After 1:5 propensity-score matching on demographics, comorbidity burden and hospital characteristics, we compared in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), total hospitalization costs, and the incidence of perioperative complications between septic and non-septic patients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify patient- and hospital-level factors independently associated with sepsis. RESULTS: n P P P Of 1,619,187 hospitalizations for cesarean delivery, 1,589,186 adults met the inclusion criteria. Annual sepsis prevalence rose from 0.058% in 2016 to 0.136% in 2022. In the 1:5 propensity-matched cohort ( = 10,050), septic patients had markedly higher in-hospital mortality (2.4% vs. 0.0%, < 0.001), longer median LOS (6 vs. 3 days, < 0.001), and approximately 2.6-fold higher median total hospitalization costs (USD 71,466 vs. USD 27,063, < 0.001). Non-elective admission, treatment in teaching hospitals, a higher comorbidity burden, Asian/Pacific Islander race, and hospital region were independently associated with sepsis. After propensity matching, septic patients also showed substantially elevated adjusted odds of pulmonary embolism (OR 61.7), postoperative shock (OR 28.7), deep-vein thrombosis (OR 24.6), urinary tract infection (OR 25.5), and chronic respiratory diseases (OR 13.2). CONCLUSIONS: In this large U.S. study, sepsis after cesarean section was linked to much higher death rates, twice the hospital stay, about 2.6 times higher costs, and more severe problems like blood clots, shock, infections, and heavy bleeding. These results show that post-cesarean section sepsis is a growing concern, remind us to spot at-risk mothers early, and offer a benchmark against which prevention and cost-effective care can be evaluated.

title: Endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction in the setting of mechanical thrombectomy: a conceptual link between cardiometabolic vulnerability and microvascular reperfusion failure.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has made macrovessel reopening achievable in acute ischemic stroke, but angiographic success does not ensure effective tissue-level reperfusion or microvascular oxygen delivery. This narrative review examines endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction as a plausible blood-facing interface that may connect pre-existing cardiometabolic vulnerability with post-thrombectomy microvascular dysfunction. Targeted English-language literature from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar through 30 April 2026 was synthesized, with emphasis on MT, impaired microvascular reperfusion (IMR), no-reflow, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular-unit (NVU) biology, glycocalyx-related biomarkers, cardiometabolic risk, perfusion imaging, and microcirculatory rescue. The evidence base is heterogeneous and is explicitly separated into direct human MT/LVO evidence, indirect human biomarker or imaging evidence, experimental cerebral evidence, non-cerebral/cross-disease vascular evidence, and hypothesis-generating mechanistic inference. Ischemic priming, abrupt reperfusion, oxidative and inflammatory stress, complement activation, metabolic stress, distal embolization, device-endothelial trauma, and host vulnerability may converge on the luminal endothelial surface. Glycocalyx dysfunction may amplify leukocyte adhesion and capillary plugging, platelet adhesion and microthrombosis, impaired mechanosensing and nitric-oxide signaling, BBB destabilization, and heterogeneous capillary flow; however, direct causal proof in human MT is lacking. Circulating syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan are therefore best interpreted as time- and compartment-dependent systemic signals rather than direct readouts of the cerebral glycocalyx. Post-EVT microcirculatory rescue trials show that downstream perfusion may remain therapeutically actionable, but they do not demonstrate glycocalyx repair as the operative mechanism. A practical translational strategy is to combine serial, compartment-annotated biomarkers with prespecified early perfusion/barrier imaging and tissue endpoints, while explicitly modeling cardiometabolic vulnerability and competing microvascular mechanisms. The glycocalyx framework should therefore be considered a testable network hypothesis rather than an established primary cause of post-thrombectomy no-reflow or futile recanalization.

title: Perforated marginal ulcer after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a national analysis of operative approaches, outcomes, and practice variations, 2018-2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perforated marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer is an uncommon but life-threatening complication after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Evidence is limited to single-center series and one 2022 systematic review of approximately 600 patients; contemporary national International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10)-era data are lacking. METHODS: We queried the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2022) for adults with a perforated gastrojejunal ulcer and a code indicating prior bariatric surgery. Operative approach was classified as laparoscopic patch, open patch, revisional gastrojejunostomy/reversal, or non-operative management. Survey-weighted statistics, negative-binomial (length of stay), gamma (total charges), and logistic (predictors of operative repair) models were estimated with hospital cluster-robust standard errors. RESULTS: The cohort included 1,669 unweighted admissions (8,345 weighted). Operative repair was performed in 28.9% (laparoscopic patch 12.6%, open patch 7.2%, revisional/reversal 9.2%); 71.1% were managed non-operatively. Crude in-hospital mortality was 1.1% overall. Non-operative management rose from 64.1% (2018) to 72.0% (2022), while laparoscopic patch declined from 18.1% to 12.1%. Open patch was associated with longer length of stay than laparoscopic patch [incidence-rate ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.13-1.77] and higher complication rates after correction for multiple comparisons of sepsis, acute kidney injury, respiratory failure, and venous thromboembolism. Elective admission strongly predicted operative repair (adjusted odds ratio 2.58, 95% CI 1.74-3.83), elective admissions were concentrated in the revisional group, but the reason for elective admission could not be determined from administrative data. Operative rates declined modestly each year (adjusted odds ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98). Case mix differed between laparoscopic-first and open-first centers. CONCLUSIONS: In the largest contemporary national cohort to date, non-operative management dominated and increased during 2018-2022. Among operatively managed patients, laparoscopic patch repair was associated with shorter length of stay and a more favorable complication profile than open repair. Because operative approach was not randomized and patients selected for open repair may have carried greater physiologic severity or technical complexity, these associations support-but do not establish-a laparoscopic-first approach where anatomy and physiology permit. Prospective evidence is needed to refine operative vs. non-operative triage.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: Traditional Chinese medicine for diabetic lower extremity arterial disease: A review of recent advances.
abstract: Diabetic lower-extremity arterial disease (LEAD) is a prevalent macrovascular complication of diabetes and a critical pathological foundation for diabetic foot lesions. Its pathogenesis involves glycolipid metabolic disturbance, excessive oxidative stress, persistent vascular inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, leading to limb ischemia, refractory foot ulcers, and increased amputation risk. Current standard treatments, including glycemic and lipid control, antiplatelet therapy, and endovascular revascularization, have improved clinical outcomes but still face challenges in fully ameliorating microcirculatory impairment and preventing long-term restenosis. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against diabetic LEAD. This review summarizes pharmacological advances in representative TCM agents, including Salvia miltiorrhiza, Astragali Radix, and their bioactive constituents (e.g., tanshinone IIA sulfonate, salvianolic acid B, astragaloside IV, and Astragalus polysaccharide), as well as classical formulas and patent medicines such as Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction, Tongxinluo capsule, Tangbi capsule, and Danggui Sini Decoction. Their mechanisms involve protecting vascular endothelium, regulating glycolipid metabolism, suppressing vascular inflammation via NF-κB and NLRP3 pathways, and activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense, HIF-1α/VEGF, PI3K-AKT, and Ang-1/Tie-2 signaling to restore microcirculation and promote angiogenesis. Clinically, TCM-assisted endovascular intervention reduces postoperative restenosis and improves lower-limb perfusion; external preparations promote diabetic foot ulcer healing; acupuncture, moxibustion, and mind-body exercises improve microcirculation and long-term management. TCM is a promising adjunctive strategy for diabetic LEAD, and further mechanistic and clinical studies are needed to advance its standardized application and improve patient prognosis.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.
