title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging-based prediction models for hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a major complication after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM/SinoMed were searched from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-driven imaging-based prediction models for predicting HT after MT in AIS, including both pre- and post-procedural imaging predictors, were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the curve (AUC), while a bivariate random-effects model was used to jointly estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity and construct the SROC curve. Subgroup analyses explored potential sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: N I p 2 Eleven studies (total = 3,541) were included, 10 studies contributed eligible AUC estimates, with evaluation cohorts ranging from 18 to 261 participants. The pooled AUC was 0.891 (95% CI: 0.853-0.928), with low between-study heterogeneity ( = 29.0%, = 0.238). The bivariate random-effects model yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.666 (95% CI: 0.578-0.744) and a pooled specificity of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.842-0.960). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide robust evidence supporting the superiority of any specific subgroup, and their interpretation was limited by small subgroup sizes and methodological heterogeneity. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies within individual subgroups. CONCLUSION: AI-driven imaging-based prediction models showed generally favorable discrimination in predicting HT after MT in AIS. However, current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific model type. The predominance of retrospective studies, limited external validation, and methodological heterogeneity limit the generalizability of current findings. Large, multicenter prospective studies with rigorous external validation are needed before clinical implementation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: The systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261441463).

title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear. METHODS: NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for confounding. Analyses are exploratory. DISCUSSION: This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more individualized management strategies in this high-risk population. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07365930.

title: Total hip arthroplasty in the presence of peri-articular pellets due to an old shotgun injury: case report and literature review.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gunshot injuries to the hip can result in devastating outcomes, leading to post-traumatic arthritis and presenting a significant surgical challenge during total hip arthroplasty (THA) due to metallic fragments and damaged soft-tissue structures. However, there is a lack of studies in the literature specifically addressing gunshot or shotgun injuries to the hip joint. CASE PRESENTATION: A 29-year-old woman, 13 years after a shotgun injury, presented with severe pain, a limp, and a 5 cm limb-length discrepancy. Imaging revealed chronic dislocation and avascular necrosis, with multiple pellets around the hip. The infection workup (white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate) was normal. She underwent lateral THA via the Hardinge approach, including trochanteric osteotomy, femoral shortening, and wire fixation. Early mobilization, 24 hours of antibiotics, and 14 days of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis were initiated. DISCUSSION: Complete extraction of all pellets was not feasible; infection was excluded pre-operatively. At 18-month follow-up, there were no infections, dislocations, or DVTs; limb-length discrepancy was less than 1 cm, and gait was pain-free, supporting the safety of single-stage THA when soft-tissue conditions are optimized and infection has been ruled out. CONCLUSION: When retained peri-articular shotgun pellets are present, carefully planned single-stage THA can restore function with a low risk of complications, provided infection is ruled out and limb length is corrected with femoral-shortening osteotomy.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p = 0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown. METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications. RESULTS: All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091385; registered 28 October 2024).

METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each).

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE. METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index. RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

title: Noninvasive hemodynamics of nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions are disturbed in patients with a history of deep vein thrombosis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVLs) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein (LCIV) stenoses greater than 20% were included and categorized by history of left lower-extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or previous venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t-tests, with statistical significance defined as P < .05. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 Forty-five patients were included, comprising nine patients with previous DVT and 36 without. Among all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed LCIV showed the strongest associations with a history of previous DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio [logfold change (FC), -1.539; P = .007], peak velocity (logFC, -0.999; P = .002), and mean velocity (logFC, -0.989; P = .002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (logFC, 0.363; P = .033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the LCIV at the compression point was the strongest predictor of previous DVT, whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device (IVID; InVera Medical) is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during nonthermal, nontumescent ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes based on a Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, and Itching (HASTI) symptom questionnaire, and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 and 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months postprocedure. Baseline and 12-month postprocedures were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively. RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted P = .03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The IVID provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient-reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID.

title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes. METHODS: This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. RESULTS: A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes.

title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood. METHODS: We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis. RESULTS: Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI. CONCLUSIONS: This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

title: Unintended shifts in high-priority adult heart transplant listings after the OPTN's September 2025 policy change.
abstract: The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network amended Status 2 heart allocation criteria in September 2025, requiring documented failure of high-dose inotropes before candidates could qualify via intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous endovascular ventricular assist device (PEVAD) support. Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024 to June 2025, n=4206) and post-policy (September 2025 to June 2026, n=4231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001). Consequently, combined initial Status 1/2 listings were unchanged (44.5% vs 44.0%, p=0.71). Furthermore, overall transplant volume remained similar, but status at transplant shifted from standard Status 2 toward Status 2 exceptions and Status 1. Tightening standard Status 2 eligibility was associated with redistribution across high-priority pathways rather than reduced high-priority listings.

title: Plasma neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin levels and risk of future incident venous thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although neutrophils are suggested to play a role in the pathogenesis of venous thromboembolism (VTE), no study has investigated whether neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a marker of neutrophil activation, is associated with future VTE risk in the general population. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007). Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for VTE according to quartiles of plasma NGAL, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, arterial cardiovascular disease, cancer, and C-reactive protein. Separate analyses with follow-up restricted to the first 2 and 5 years after cohort inclusion were conducted to investigate potential short-term associations. RESULTS: We found no association between NGAL levels and risk of future VTE when analyzing the entire study period (OR for highest vs lowest quartile of NGAL: 1.02, 95% CI, 0.70-1.51). However, when follow-up was restricted to 2 years, higher NGAL levels were associated with increased risk of future VTE (OR, 3.87; 95% CI, 1.15-13.03). The association was attenuated when follow-up was extended to 5 years (OR, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.82-2.80). CONCLUSION: Higher plasma NGAL levels were associated with a transiently increased risk of future VTE.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007).

title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin. METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IRs) per 100 person-years and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) comparing aspirin use with no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n = 1760 with aspirin, n = 367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in patients with JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 1.59-4.65; I= 93%), with pooled IRR receiving aspirin vs no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI, 0.40-0.86; I= 16%). The pooled IR of major and nonmajor bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI, 1.06-3.65; I= 90%) per 100 person-years, with a pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI, 1.15-5.11; I= 43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low. CONCLUSION: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence to better define the role of aspirin in JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Moderate-to-Severe Psoriasis Receiving Biologic Therapy: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular benefits, but their association with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with psoriasis remains insufficiently studied. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the global TriNetX research network. Patients older than 40 years with plaque psoriasis receiving biologic therapy were categorized according to SGLT2 inhibitor use. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, kidney disease, and concomitant antidiabetic medications. RESULTS: After matching, 2016 patients were included in each cohort. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a significantly lower incidence of acute myocardial infarction (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.426-0.849), stroke (HR, 0.553; 95%CI, 0.381-0.804), heart failure (HR, 0.751; 95%CI, 0.581-0.970), peripheral artery disease (HR, 0.648; 95%CI, 0.470-0.894), and angina pectoris (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.404-0.894). No significant association was observed for transient ischemic attack. CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy. These findings support further prospective investigation of SGLT2 inhibitors as a potential strategy for cardiovascular risk reduction in this population.

Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular benefits, but their association with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with psoriasis remains insufficiently studied. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the global TriNetX research network.

title: Arabidopsis Loss of tRNA uridine thiolation affects mRNA translation, protein production, and metabolite accumulation in.
abstract: Arabidopsis thaliana 34 It is well established in yeast and animal system that the level of uridine thiolation at position 34 of tRNA anticodon loops can impact the decoding potential of the corresponding codons. Using, we confirm that the ability of the plant ribosome to decode AAA, GAA, and CAA codons is impaired when this thiol group is lost, leading to a reduction in protein production, especially for genes enriched in these codons. Interestingly, we observed that loss of tRNA thiolation results in variations in the levels of numerous proteins involved in sulfur-compound metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These variations, in turn, affect the accumulation of several sulfur-containing metabolites and amino acids, suggesting that the level of tRNA thiolation has a direct and profound impact on plant metabolism. We also demonstrate that Uthiolation is essential for adjusting plant growth in response to sulfur limitation and that its absence directly affects the plant's interaction with bacteria, including both pathogens and beneficial organisms. Our results support the hypothesis that the level of tRNA thiolation can be used in plant to link nutritional status to translation.

title: Lipid control in a cohort of patients with cardiorenal disease (LIPID-REN): a subanalysis of the CARDIOREN registry.
abstract: AIMS: Advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) confers a very high cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, requiring comprehensive risk factor assessment. However, real-world data on current practices in patients with cardiorenal disease remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the control of cardiovascular risk factors, with a focus on lipid management, in a contemporary cardiorenal cohort. METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis was conducted within the CARDIOREN Registry, which enrolled patients with chronic heart failure from 13 tertiary hospitals in Spain (2021-2022). Of 1107 patients, 885 with complete data on low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), albuminuria, and atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD) were eligible. The present analysis was restricted to the patients who met the definition of advanced CKD, defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <30 ml/min/1.73 m² or eGFR 30-45 ml/min/1.73 m² with albuminuria >30 mg/g. ASCVD was defined as prior ischemic heart disease, stroke, or peripheral arterial disease. The proportion of patients with LDL-C <55 mg/dl was assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models, including a parsimonious primary model and sensitivity analyses, were used to identify factors associated with lower LDL-C levels. RESULTS: P Advanced CKD was present in 221 patients (25%); median age was 79 years, 58.8% were male, and 52.9% had ASCVD. Median LDL-C was 73 mg/dl, and only 22.6% achieved an LDL-C <55 mg/dl. Achievement of LDL-C <55 mg/dl was significantly lower in patients without ASCVD compared with those with ASCVD (13.4% vs. 30.7%; = .002). In multivariable analysis, ASCVD was independently associated with a higher likelihood of achieving LDL-C <55 mg/dl, whereas female sex was independently associated with a lower likelihood of achieving this level. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with advanced CKD, lipid control was below cardiology guideline recommendations for patients at very high CVD risk, particularly among those without ASCVD and in women.

title: The ECMO-PoCS Score: Derivation and Internal Validation of an Implantation-Time Model for In-Hospital Mortality in Postcardiotomy Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To derive and internally validate a mortality score (ECMO-PoCS) for use at venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) implantation for postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS), hypothesizing that a few implantation-time variables would discriminate in-hospital mortality better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II), Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II), or pre-ECMO lactate. DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary cardiac surgical center. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 149 consecutive adults receiving VA-ECMO for PCS (2007-2024), excluding 7 bridged directly to transplantation. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Hospital mortality was 65.8% and 1-year survival 33.4%. A 4-variable logistic model (age, pre-ECMO lactate, peripheral artery disease [PAD], and any preoperative right ventricular [RV] dysfunction) was fitted in 133 complete cases; PAD (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 4.58; p = 0.022) and RV dysfunction (adjusted OR = 3.16; p = 0.020) were independently associated with mortality. In 130 patients with all comparators, ECMO-PoCS (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.715) discriminated better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II) (0.583; DeLong p = 0.043) and lactate alone (0.601; p = 0.030) but not significantly better than APACHE II (0.610; p = 0.13); adding these variables to APACHE II increased its AUC to 0.727 (likelihood ratio p = 0.002). Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.687 and the shrinkage factor 0.82. A 0- to 5-point score defined low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (mortality 23.1%, 63.6%, and 86.0%, respectively; trend p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: ECMO-PoCS, based on 4 variables available at implantation, discriminated in-hospital mortality better than EuroSCORE II and lactate alone and added information to APACHE II. Internally validated only, it is intended for risk description, research stratification, and benchmarking, not for decisions to initiate or withdraw support, pending external validation.

DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary cardiac surgical center.

title: Long-Term Durability of Bare-Metal Stenting in Complex Iliac Disease: External Iliac Artery Involvement as the Principal Determinant of Late Patency Loss.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term durability after endovascular treatment of complex aortoiliac disease remains incompletely defined. The present study evaluated late primary patency after bare-metal stenting (BMS) in Trans-Atlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C-D lesions and examined whether anatomical extension beyond the common iliac artery influences long-term outcomes independently of traditional TASC classification. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted including 153 consecutive iliac limbs with TASC C-D occlusive disease treated with BMS between 2014 and 2024. Covered stents, kissing configurations, and acute occlusions were excluded to ensure a homogeneous technical cohort. The primary end point was primary patency. Kaplan-Meier estimates were reported through 72 months. Restricted mean survival time (RMST) regression at τ = 72 months and Firth penalized logistic regression were applied to identify independent predictors while minimizing small-event bias. RESULTS: Technical success exceeded 97%, with no perioperative mortality. Primary patency remained high and comparable between TASC C and D lesions at 72 months (86% vs 84%; log-rank P = 0.8). In contrast, extension into the external iliac artery (EIA) was associated with progressive late attrition. Adjusted RMST analysis demonstrated a 7.6-month reduction in mean primary patency at 72 months for EIA-involved lesions (95% confidence interval -11.6 to -3.6; P < 0.001). Firth regression confirmed increased late risk of patency loss at 60 months (odds ratio [OR] 10.5; P = 0.034) and 72 months (OR 25.8; P = 0.003). Technical optimization (best-practice stenting) showed limited and model-dependent mitigation, without consistent protection across time points. CONCLUSION: In complex iliac BMS reconstruction, long-term durability appears primarily determined by distal anatomical extension rather than TASC class. EIA involvement identifies a subgroup at risk for late failure and may represent a more clinically meaningful stratification parameter for endovascular planning.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Long-term durability after endovascular treatment of complex aortoiliac disease remains incompletely defined. The present study evaluated late primary patency after bare-metal stenting (BMS) in Trans-Atlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C-D lesions and examined whether anatomical extension beyond the common iliac artery influences long-term outcomes independently of traditional TASC classification. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted including 153 consecutive iliac limbs with TASC C-D occlusive disease treated with BMS between 2014 and 2024.

title: Limb salvage is possible in select patients with arterial injuries and elevated mangled extremity severity scores.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity trauma with vascular compromise is frequently associated with other injuries and requires emergent and complex decision-making. The Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS) is widely utilized to predict the need for amputation in these cases. As the tool was developed >30 years ago, its accuracy in the modern trauma setting remains a topic of investigation and discussion. This study investigated the correlation of an elevated MESS with the need for amputation in patients with traumatic lower extremity arterial injuries. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed for patients ≥18 years old with traumatic lower extremity arterial injuries at a level I trauma center from July 2012 to December 2023. Demographics, injury characteristics, interventions, and outcomes including amputation upon presentation, amputation during hospitalization, and amputation after discharge following limb salvage attempts were recorded. RESULTS: In our cohort of 238 limbs with lower extremity arterial injury, the median age was 33 years, and the majority of patients were male (84.1%). The predominant mechanism was penetrating (65.1%). Concomitant injuries were noted in 84 cases of lower extremity injures (35.3%). The median MESS was 5 (interquartile range, 3-6). Vascular repair was performed for 179 lower limbs (75.2%); 168 underwent open repair (93.9%), 9 endovascular (5.0%), and 2 hybrid (1.1%). Ninety-two limbs underwent concomitant orthopedic repair (38.7%). Six limbs underwent primary amputation (2.5%) after a multidisciplinary consensus, all of which had a MESS of ≥7. Of the 179 lower limbs that underwent vascular repair, 8.4% required amputation before discharge, and another 2.8% required amputation after discharge. Thirty-three lower extremities with a MESS of ≥7 underwent vascular repair. The majority did not require a subsequent amputation (22/33, 66.7%). In the entire cohort, a MESS of ≥7 was significantly associated with any amputation (P < .0001) when compared with MESS < 7. MESS ≥ 7 was associated with a significantly higher odds of amputation in both univariable (odds ratio, 10.6; 95% confidence interval, 4.65-24.1; P < .0001) and multivariable analyses after adjustment for age, ischemia time, mechanism of injury, concomitant injuries, arterial injury location, and fracture status (adjusted odds ratio, 5.40; 95% confidence interval, 1.79-16.3; P = .003). CONCLUSIONS: Lower extremity arterial injuries are frequently associated with complex orthopedic and soft tissue trauma. An elevated MESS, blunt mechanism, and the presence of multiple vascular injuries are significantly associated with the risk of limb loss. Although a MESS of 7 or greater is predictive of an increased risk of amputation, limb salvage can still be achieved in many patients with prompt vascular repair despite high MESS.

The Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS) is widely utilized to predict the need for amputation in these cases. As the tool was developed >30 years ago, its accuracy in the modern trauma setting remains a topic of investigation and discussion.

title: Optimizing pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis in medical inpatients using sequential IMPROVE risk assessment models: Clinical, economic and environmental implications.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients. Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the discrepancy between real-world thromboprophylaxis prescribing and a prespecified sequential IMPROVE-based strategy and assess its economic and environmental implications. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in internal medicine over one month. Adults hospitalized for>48h were included, excluding those receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. IMPROVE VTE and Bleeding scores were calculated retrospectively. Pharmacologic prophylaxis was supported by the strategy for patients with an IMPROVE Bleeding score<7 and IMPROVE VTE score≥2. Observed prescriptions were compared with the prespecified strategy using contingency analysis and Fisher's exact test. RESULTS: 2 Among 99 patients, 79.8% received pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, whereas 46.5% met the strategy criteria. Among treated patients, 46.8% did not meet these criteria. Strict application of the strategy would theoretically result in 292 fewer doses over one month, corresponding to €233.60 in estimated savings and approximately 405kg COeq. CONCLUSION: Real-world prescribing differed substantially from the prespecified strategy. Strict application would theoretically reduce anticoagulant use, costs, and carbon emissions. However, clinical outcomes were not assessed, and RAMs should complement rather than replace clinical judgment. Prospective studies incorporating VTE and bleeding outcomes are required to assess the safety of this approach.

Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment.

title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD. METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

title: Clinical significance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index in glycemic control and ischemic limb damage in type 2 diabetes with chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical relevance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) complicated by chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) . METHODS: A total of 520 patients with CLTI were collected and divided into two groups based on the history of T2DM: the combined T2DM group and the non-T2DM group. The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed. RESULTS: P P P P P The CTI in the combined T2DM group was significantly greater than that in the non-T2DM group ( < 0.001). The CTI in the poorly controlled blood glucose group was significantly greater than that in the well controlled blood glucose group ( < 0.001). Regardless of whether CLTI patients had T2DM, the CTI in the overweight group was greater than that in the non-overweight group ( < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the CTI discriminating the high wound, ischemia, and foot infection (WIfI) classification was 0.813 ( < 0.001). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses showed that an increased CTI was an independently associated factor for the high WIfI classification in CLTI patients (OR = 6.409, < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with CLTI and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels. CONCLUSIONS: The CTI was closely related to the presence of T2DM, blood glucose control level, and overweight status in CLTI patients. The CTI has certain clinical value in discriminating the degree of ischemia in CLTI, and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed.

title: "Not so Minor" - Digital Amputation as a Precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish Tertiary Vascular Center.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for 5-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality. METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017 and 2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality. RESULTS: A total of 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least 1 minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (±12.7). 70% had peripheral arterial disease and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n = 73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major reamputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischemic heart disease (IHD) (odds ratio [OR] 2.796, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136), and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularization at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8%, and 48% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for 5-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality.

title: Spatial Organization of Disturbed Flow after Carotid Endarterectomy and Carotid Artery Stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) and carotid artery stenting (CAS) create distinct postoperative geometries. Conventional wall shear stress (WSS)-derived biomarkers quantify disturbed-flow magnitude but not its spatial organization. We evaluated whether spatial organization provides complementary hemodynamic information after CEA and CAS. METHODS: In this retrospective, patient-specific computational fluid dynamics study, 9 carotid geometries (3 healthy, 3 post-CEA, and 3 post-CAS) were reconstructed from computed tomography angiography. Identical pulsatile boundary conditions were applied to isolate morphological effects. Time-averaged WSS (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), relative residence time (RRT), and endothelial cell activation potential (ECAP) were computed. Regions of adverse flow were defined using percentile thresholds (P90, P95, and P99). Spatial organization was quantified by total area at risk, largest connected hotspot area, hotspot number, and the Spatial Dominance Index (SDI), defined as the largest hotspot area divided by total area at risk. RESULTS: ECAP, OSI, and RRT colocalized with low TAWSS, and spatial descriptors were consistent across biomarkers. Healthy carotids showed the most focal pattern (SDI approximately 0.22; 8-12 hotspots). CEA had the largest total area at risk and largest hotspot but retained relatively high dominance (SDI, 0.16-0.17; 48-75 hotspots). The Roadsaver-treated CAS geometries had the smallest total area at risk but the most fragmented pattern, with smaller hotspots and the lowest dominance (SDI, 0.09-0.12; 39-70 hotspots). These patterns persisted across P90-P99 thresholds. CONCLUSION: Spatial organization distinguished carotid revascularization strategies beyond biomarker magnitude. CEA largely preserved a focal, dominant pattern, whereas the Roadsaver-treated CAS geometries showed fragmented, distributed disturbed flow. The simple, dimensionless SDI may complement established WSS-derived biomarkers in patient-specific hemodynamic assessment.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) and carotid artery stenting (CAS) create distinct postoperative geometries. Conventional wall shear stress (WSS)-derived biomarkers quantify disturbed-flow magnitude but not its spatial organization. We evaluated whether spatial organization provides complementary hemodynamic information after CEA and CAS.

title: Postoperative Complications Following Carotid Endarterectomy are Differentially Impacted by Sex and Plaque Instability.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in postcarotid endarterectomy (CEA) outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for CEA rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing CEA for clinical indications. We performed multivariable binary logistic regression to examine the relationship of biological sex and plaque instability with postoperative outcomes. RESULTS: Data of 394 participants (31% female) were analyzed. Plaque instability was independently associated with decreased odds of hemorrhagic complications at 1 month and 1 year postsurgery, as well as with decreased respiratory complications at 1 year postsurgery. Plaque features accounting for these associations were lipid core, cap infiltration, and plaque inflammation. Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of restenosis at 1 month and 1 year postsurgery. In addition, females with unstable plaques had more cerebrovascular complications at 1 month than males with unstable plaques, and females with stable plaques had double the odds of any complication at 1 month compared with males with unstable plaques. CONCLUSION: Our findings show that sex and plaque instability differentially impact postendarterectomy outcomes, with males with unstable plaques experiencing the least postoperative complications. Sex and plaque instability may therefore be important factors that play a role in postoperative complications, highlighting their importance in the context of surgical decision-making.

Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for CEA rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing CEA for clinical indications.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events, and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. We aimed to conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluation the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD. METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)/Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses literature search extension (PRISMA-S) guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: 2 Ten studies were included. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% confidence interval, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I= 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.84. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than nonregistry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; P = 0.004). All models had a high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low. CONCLUSION: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to artificial intelligence reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction.

title: Association between Increased Superficial Calcification Clusters in Carotid Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Events after Carotid Artery Stenting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on computed tomography angiography. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P = 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P = 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P = 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P = 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P = 0.0256, HR = 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P = 0.0265, HR = 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert for Detecting Peripheral Arterial Disease in People with Suspected Intermittent Claudication Referred to Secondary Care: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Manual ankle-brachial pressure index (ABI) assessment reqiuires significant time and expertise, precluding its use in primary care. Automated vascular assessment tools may offer a simple and efficient alternative for detecting peripheral arterial disease (PAD). However, further evidence is needed before they can be recommended. This study considers the diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop vascular expert (BVE) in people with suspected intermittent claudication. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional cohort study including people referred to our nurse-led intermittent claudication clinic. BVE measurements were compared to the manual resting ABI/toe brachial index (TBI) method, using traditional cutoff values of <0.9 and < 0.7, respectively. RESULTS: 217 participants and 430 limbs were included, with an overall PAD prevalence of 46%. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictor values (PPVs) and negative predictor values (NPVs) for the BVE were 88.5%, 80.7%, 81.3% and 88.1% respectively, when compared to the manual ABI. When compared to the manual TBI, the sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV for the BVE were 45.5%, 88%, 62.5%, and 78.6% respectively, though this analysis included only 38 limbs. No BVE diagnoses were based on ABI alone, 71% were based on waveform alone and 29% were based on a combination of ABI and waveform. The BVE assessment was significantly quicker to perform than the manual method (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The BVE demonstrated favorable sensitivity and specificity for detecting or excluding PAD compared to the manual ABI. Further work is needed comparing this device to others, across a range of clinical populations and settings before it can be considered in routine clinical practice.

title: Endoscopic versus open great saphenous vein harvesting for lower extremity arterial bypass: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing lower extremity arterial bypass (LEAB) for peripheral artery disease with endoscopic great saphenous vein harvest (EVH) vs open vein harvest (OVH), and to investigate the impact of publication year on bypass patency. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH vs OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. Binary and continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses by publication year (≤2015 vs >2015) were performed to explore temporal trends in patency. RESULTS: 2 Thirteen retrospective cohort studies comprising 12,401 patients were included. EVH was associated with higher risk of primary patency loss compared with OVH (hazard ratio [HR], 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04-1.68; P = .030) and a borderline longer operative time (mean difference, 58.98 minutes; 95% CI, 0.63-117.32; P = .050; I= 96%), but significantly lower wound complications (risk ratio, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.57-0.80; P < .001). No differences were observed in primary-assisted patency, secondary patency, length of stay, major amputation, limb salvage, or mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the primary patency disadvantage was driven by studies published up to 2015 (HR, 1.49; P = .010), with no significant difference in studies published after 2015 (HR, 0.97; P = .900), although the interaction test was not significant (P = .100). Meta-regression did not demonstrate an association between publication year and primary patency effect size (P = .890). CONCLUSIONS: EVH significantly reduces wound complications but is associated with lower primary patency and potentially longer operative times compared with OVH, disadvantages that do not translate into differences in secondary patency, limb salvage, major amputation, or mortality. Further prospective studies are needed to define the role of EVH to better inform LEAB operative planning.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH vs OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models.

title: Clinical outcomes of transperitoneal versus retroperitoneal approaches of open aortic repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm with iliac bifurcation involvement (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared with OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study compared the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting. METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as having AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes, such as overall 30-day mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, and stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses and a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression were performed. RESULTS: Of all the reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA and 1791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with a higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (odds ratios [OR], 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.49; P = .011) and of MACE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44; P = .001) and a lower 1-year survival rate (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.09-1.39; P = .001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia (OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.25-0.91; P = .024), without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; P = .485), MACE (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.52-1.42; P = .563), and 1-year survival (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.59-1.47; P = .768). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, iliac bifurcation involvement in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. In contrast, for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) nonthoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with nonthoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with <2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: Adherence to the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines for the Management of Neck of Femur Fractures.
abstract: Introduction Over 72,000 hip fractures occur annually in the United Kingdom, costing over £2 billion, with 10% mortality at 30 days and 30% annually. Therefore, the study aimed to compare hip fracture care at North Manchester General Hospital with the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) guidelines. Methodology A retrospective review of electronic patient records at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust was conducted from September to November 2025. Patients aged >60 years with native intracapsular or extracapsular femoral neck fractures, or those aged >60 years with pathological femoral neck fractures, were included. Descriptive analysis was performed to ascertain compliance with BOAST guidelines. Results The management of 51 patients was audited against 13 BOAST parameters. 100% compliance was achieved in seven parameters: certainty of diagnosis, a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach to patient care, preoperative optimisation by an orthogeriatric team within 72 hours, documented weight-bearing status, falls risk assessment, bone health assessment, and data entry into the National Hip Fracture Database (NHFD). Parameters with less than 100% compliance were post-operative physiotherapy (50, 98%), venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis (50, 98%), analgesia (46, 91%), VTE assessment (45, 88%), post-operative delirium assessment (43, 84%), and surgery within 36 hours (32, 62.8%). Reasons for non-compliance included transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU) for post-operative physiotherapy; workload-related delays in VTE prophylaxis; unfamiliarity with local analgesia protocols among newly appointed National Health Service (NHS) doctors; inconsistent documentation of VTE assessment; and inconsistent completion of post-operative delirium assessments, with unclear responsibilities between doctors and coordinators. Limited theatre capacity and the need for medical optimisation accounted for non-compliance with the 36-hour surgery target. Conclusions BOAST compliance was good overall, but gaps in documentation, timing, and role clarity remain. Improvements include enforcing admission checklists, recording arousal, attention, and acute change using the abbreviated mental test-4 (4AT), pharmacist incident reporting, trauma coordinator oversight, and neck of femur training.

Methodology A retrospective review of electronic patient records at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust was conducted from September to November 2025.

title: Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Stationarity in Predicting TEVAR Response.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for type B aortic dissections and rupture, with guidelines recommending systolic blood pressure (SBP) control below 130 mmHg to improve outcomes. While post-TEVAR blood pressure is often managed with a focus on mean SBP, little is known about temporal hemodynamic patterns and their association with surgical success. This study investigates blood pressure and heart rate (HR) time-series metrics within 24 hours post-TEVAR and their predictive potential for outcomes. METHODS: Blood pressure (n = 560) and HR (n = 680) time-series data from 31 patients were analyzed alongside preoperative aortic geometry metrics. Exploratory data analysis identified correlations between BP variability and outcomes. Stationarity tests were performed on time-series data to assess statistical properties. Logistic regression models incorporating hemodynamic metrics, along with CT-derived features, were used to predict TEVAR outcomes. RESULTS: Successful outcomes correlated with greater diastolic blood pressure variability and strictly stationary SBP. Logistic regression models combining these metrics along with heart rate standard deviation and preoperative aortic geometry achieved 96.67% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy in predicting outcomes. CONCLUSION: Post-TEVAR behaviors of hemodynamic variables are critical predictors of TEVAR success, with higher DBP standard deviation and strict stationarity of SBP significantly associated with favorable outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of hemodynamic variability and stationarity in optimizing post-TEVAR patient care.

title: Preoperative White Matter Lesions and Functional Recovery after Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoring ambulation is an important goal of revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), but predictors of functional recovery remain limited. We investigated whether preoperative white matter lesion (WML) burden was associated with ambulatory recovery after revascularization. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 196 patients with CLTI, tissue loss, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection ischemia grade 2 or 3, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) within 3 months before revascularization. Preoperative brain MRI was routinely obtained in patients considered for open surgical revascularization for cerebrovascular risk assessment. Periventricular and deep subcortical white matter hyperintensities were graded using the Fazekas scale; a total score of 3 or greater defined a high-grade WML burden. The primary outcome was the achievement of a Functional Ambulation Category score of 3 or greater within 180 days. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox models. RESULTS: High-grade WML burden was present in 120 patients. Six-month ambulatory recovery was lower in the high-grade group than in the low-grade group (63.1% vs 82.4%; P = 0.019). High-grade WML burden was independently associated with slower ambulatory recovery (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.96; P = 0.032) and delayed final discharge (adjusted HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.43-0.92; P = 0.017), but not with wound healing or wound-free functional limb achievement. CONCLUSION: High-grade WML burden was associated with impaired ambulatory recovery and delayed discharge after CLTI revascularization. When preoperative brain MRI is available, WML assessment may complement limb staging and help anticipate rehabilitation and discharge needs.

title: Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage during bridging anticoagulation in primary antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a major cause of acquired thrombophilia and is frequently associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism requiring long-term anticoagulation. We report a 42-year-old man with primary APS and recurrent pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis who developed acute right upper-quadrant abdominal pain during peri-procedural bridging anticoagulation with enoxaparin. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute-to-subacute unilateral right adrenal haemorrhage without evidence of abdominal trauma, malignancy or infection. The patient remained haemodynamically stable and did not develop adrenal insufficiency. This case highlights the complexity of anticoagulation management in high-risk APS patients and emphasises the importance of considering adrenal haemorrhage in APS patients presenting with abdominal pain during anticoagulation modification. A review of previously reported unilateral APS-associated adrenal haemorrhage cases is also presented. Key Points • Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a rare manifestation of primary antiphospholipid syndrome. • Bridging anticoagulation may represent a vulnerable period for adrenal haemorrhage in high-risk APS. • Early CT/MRI imaging and assessment of adrenal function are essential. • Conservative management with careful reintroduction of anticoagulation may lead to favourable outcomes.
