title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.
englishSummary: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX.

title: In Vitro Development and Evaluation of an Endovascular Islet Cell Stent for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the in vitro development and benchtop evaluation of the IsletStent, an endovascular biological stent graft incorporating expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) semipermeable membranes, designed for portal venous delivery of pancreatic islets as a treatment for Type 1 diabetes mellitus. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22-μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQs]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQs) islets. A benchtop normothermic perfusion circuit simulated intravascular deployment. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion was assessed in a repeated-measures design (n = 4 devices per experiment); murine islet-seeded devices were perfused under zero (0 mM), low (2.8 mM), and high (28 mM) glucose, and human islet-seeded devices were perfused under low and high glucose only, with insulin quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Computational fluid dynamics modeling under idealized, nonphysiologic single-fluid conditions evaluated candidate device geometries. RESULTS: Murine islet-seeded devices demonstrated glucose-responsive insulin secretion: 3-hour insulin concentrations were 83 μIU/mL (SD ± 8) versus 145 μIU/mL (SD ± 20) under low versus high glucose (P = .02), and secretion rates were 5,344 μIU/h (SD ± 144) versus 6,795 μIU/h (SD ± 503) (P = .008). Human islet-seeded devices responded concordantly, with 3-hour insulin concentrations of 229 μIU/mL (SD ± 13) versus 300 μIU/mL (SD ± 17) (P = .014). CONCLUSIONS: In this benchtop perfusion model, islets housed within an ePTFE-based endovascular stent graft retained glucose-responsive insulin secretion. In vivo evaluation of islet viability, direct immunoisolation, hemodynamic impact, and long-term function is required before clinical translation.

title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Decompensated Aortic Stenosis accompanied by Cardiogenic Shock.
abstract: Patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) often present acutely with decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest requiring immediate intervention. Treatment options for these patients include palliative care, balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV), emergency transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), or surgical aortic valve replacement. TAVI procedure is performed electively in majority of the patients. However, it can be considered a rescue therapy in patients with cardiogenic shock secondary to acutely decompensated valvular AS. Here, we report the successful use of emergent TAVI for a patient presenting with cardiogenic shock secondary to decompensated AS.

Treatment options for these patients include palliative care, balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV), emergency transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), or surgical aortic valve replacement. TAVI procedure is performed electively in majority of the patients.

title: Comparison of a Novel Geometric Landmark Method Versus Conventional Palpation Technique for Central Venous Cannulation: A Comparative Observational Study of Two Techniques.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a novel geometric landmark technique with the conventional palpation technique for central venous cannulation. STUDY DESIGN: Comparative observational study. PLACE AND DURATION OF THE STUDY: This study was conducted at National Medical Centre (NMC) from January 01, 2025 to June 30, 2025. METHODS: A total of 100 adult patients requiring central venous cannulation were enrolled and allocated into two groups based on the technique used. Group A (n = 50) underwent cannulation using the geometric landmark method, while Group B (n = 50) underwent cannulation using the conventional palpation technique. First-attempt success rate was the main outcome. Secondary outcomes were the number of attempts, arterial puncture, and change of technique. SPSS software was used for analysis. Chi-square test was used to compare categorical variables whereas the Mann-Whitney U test was applied to the non-normally distributed continuous variables. A P value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: First-attempt success was significantly higher in the geometric landmark group compared to the palpation group (98% vs. 86%; P = 0.027). The geometric landmark technique was associated with fewer cannulation attempts (mean 1.00 ± 0.00 vs. 1.18 ± 0.57; P = 0.012). Arterial puncture occurred in one patient (2%) in each group, with no statistically significant difference (P = 1.000). Technique change was required in one patient (2%) in each group, with no statistically significant difference between the two techniques (P = 1.000). The two groups had similar baseline demographic and clinical characteristics. CONCLUSION: The geometric landmark technique significantly improves first-attempt success and reduces the number of cannulation attempts compared with the conventional palpation method while maintaining a comparable safety profile. This technique represents a practical and cost-effective alternative for central venous cannulation, particularly in resource-limited settings.

STUDY DESIGN: Comparative observational study. PLACE AND DURATION OF THE STUDY: This study was conducted at National Medical Centre (NMC) from January 01, 2025 to June 30, 2025.

title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair in hyperacute type B aortic dissection: a mini review.
abstract: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is established as the preferred treatment for many patients with complicated acute type B aortic dissection (TBAD). However, its role during the hyperacute phase (within 24 hours of symptom onset) remains controversial, as the acutely dissected aortic wall may be vulnerable to device-related injury. Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR. In patients with rupture, malperfusion, impending aortic rupture, persistent pain, refractory hypertension, or progressive true-lumen collapse, prompt entry-tear coverage can restore perfusion and prevent irreversible organ injury. Similarly, in patients without initial complications, high-risk anatomical features may help identify those who could benefit from early intervention. However, evidence supporting routine TEVAR within the first 24 hours remains limited and is predominantly observational. To ensure safe hyperacute TEVAR, careful assessment of the landing zones, conservative device sizing, avoidance of aggressive balloon molding, preservation of branch-vessel and spinal cord perfusion, and prompt recognition of retrograde type A dissection, stroke, spinal cord ischemia, and stent-graft-induced new entry are required. Ultimately, hyperacute TEVAR may be a reasonable option for selected patients with complicated TBAD, with a potential role in high-risk uncomplicated TBAD. Future prospective randomized trials integrating multimodal imaging and dynamic biomarkers are warranted to establish definitive criteria for timing and candidate selection.

However, its role during the hyperacute phase (within 24 hours of symptom onset) remains controversial, as the acutely dissected aortic wall may be vulnerable to device-related injury. Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR.

title: Cerebral Air Embolism After Navigational Bronchoscopy Treated With Aspiration Thrombectomy: A Case Report.
abstract: Systemic arterial air embolism is a rare but potentially devastating complication of bronchoscopic lung biopsy. A 68-year-old man with severe emphysema developed abrupt bradycardia, hypotension, and failure to regain consciousness after navigational bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia. Computed tomography demonstrated air within the left middle cerebral artery, and angiography confirmed proximal large-vessel occlusion. Urgent aspiration thrombectomy achieved complete reperfusion after one pass, with retrieved material compatible with thrombus. Despite technically successful reperfusion, major neurological deficits persisted. This case highlights haemodynamic collapse and delayed emergence as warning signs and supports rapid neuroimaging with selective endovascular treatment when an accessible large-vessel occlusion is present.

title: Recognizing Pelvic Venous Disease in Chronic Pelvic Pain: A Primary Care Case Report.
abstract: Chronic pelvic pain is a common and challenging condition with a broad differential diagnosis and a substantial impact on quality of life. Pelvic congestion syndrome (PCS) is a clinical manifestation of pelvic venous disease that may involve venous reflux, obstruction, collateralization, and dilation across different pelvic venous territories. Its non-specific clinical presentation and overlap with gynecological, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal disorders may lead to significant diagnostic delay. A 42-year-old woman presented to a general and family medicine consultation with a six-year history of chronic pelvic pain, progressively worsening over the previous six months. She described persistent pressure-like pelvic pain, rated 7/10 in intensity, aggravated by prolonged standing and associated with severe deep dyspareunia, which prevented sexual intercourse, associated with low back pain radiating to the pelvis and both thighs, lower-limb heaviness, and significant sleep disturbance. She denied urinary symptoms or a relationship with the menstrual cycle. During the previous six years, she had undergone repeated medical assessments, with symptoms being attributed to recurrent gynecological infections, probable irritable bowel syndrome, and other non-specific causes. Previous investigations, including colonoscopy and emergency department assessments, had not identified a clear etiology for her symptoms. Physical examination revealed hypogastric tenderness and mild superficial lower-limb varicosities, without vulvar or perineal varices. Pelvic and lumbar computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral dilated periuterine veins measuring up to 13 mm, raising suspicion for a symptomatic pelvic venous disorder. The patient was referred to vascular surgery for further assessment; however, specialist evaluation remained pending at the time of manuscript revision. Pelvic venous disease should be considered in women with persistent pelvic pain, particularly when symptoms worsen with prolonged standing or sexual intercourse and are accompanied by low back pain or lower-limb heaviness. The absence of vulvar varices or previous inconclusive investigations does not exclude a possible pelvic venous etiology. This case illustrates how the non-specific presentation of pelvic venous disease may result in years of fragmented investigation and delayed recognition. Continuity of care in general and family medicine facilitated a longitudinal review of the patient's symptoms and previous investigations, allowing recognition of a pattern suggestive of pelvic venous disease. Greater awareness of pelvic venous disease in primary care may facilitate earlier consideration and appropriate specialist referral in women with otherwise unexplained chronic pelvic pain.

Pelvic congestion syndrome (PCS) is a clinical manifestation of pelvic venous disease that may involve venous reflux, obstruction, collateralization, and dilation across different pelvic venous territories. Its non-specific clinical presentation and overlap with gynecological, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal disorders may lead to significant diagnostic delay.

title: Limb Salvage Outcomes Following Endovascular Revascularization for Peripheral Artery Disease in a Southern Indian Population: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background Peripheral artery disease (PAD), particularly chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), is associated with a high risk of limb loss and significant morbidity. Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population. Materials and methods This retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary vascular care center and included 142 patients with symptomatic PAD who underwent endovascular intervention between July 2023 and June 2025. Clinical severity and lesion complexity were assessed using the Rutherford classification and the TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) classification, respectively. The primary endpoint was limb salvage at one year, defined as freedom from major amputation. Secondary endpoints included technical success, restenosis, and procedure-related complications. Results The study population was predominantly male (87.3%) with a mean age of 61.11 ± 12.90 years. Most patients (78.1%) presented with CLTI. Technical success was achieved in 87.3% of procedures. At one-year follow-up, limb salvage was achieved in 95.8% of patients, with major amputation occurring in 4.2% and minor amputation in 9.1%. Restenosis was observed in 14.7% of cases. Procedure-related complications were infrequent and mostly minor, with one all-cause death during follow-up. Conclusions ET is a safe and effective modality for limb salvage in PAD patients, particularly in populations with a high prevalence of diabetes and advanced disease at presentation. High limb salvage rates can be achieved even in cohorts predominantly comprising patients with CLTI, supporting an endovascular-first approach in appropriately selected patients.

Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population.

title: Cerebral Hemodynamic Changes in Older Adults With Cognitive Complaints According to the Presence of Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: As a systemic expression of atherosclerosis, peripheral artery disease (PAD) has the potential to alter cerebral hemodynamics in elderly individuals presenting with cognitive concerns. However, how PAD status shapes the longitudinal trajectory of cerebral hemodynamics has not been well characterized. METHODS: We conducted a single-center longitudinal observational study enrolling 132 participants (21 controls, 39 mild cognitive impairment, 72 mild Alzheimer's disease). All participants underwent transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography, ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement, brain MRI, and cognitive assessments at baseline and follow-up (~13.45 months). PAD was defined as ABI < 0.90. Bilateral mean flow velocity (MFV), pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI) of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) were tracked longitudinally across both time points. RESULTS: p p PAD was identified in 13 participants (9.8%). Baseline TCD parameters, vascular risk factors, white matter lesions on brain MRI, and cognitive measures were comparable between groups. At follow-up, the PAD group showed significantly higher MCA MFV after age adjustment (left < 0.001; right = 0.005). MFV increased in the PAD group (left +16.45 cm/s) but decreased in the non-PAD group (left -3.37 cm/s), with a significant between-group difference. PI and RI did not change in either group. Cognitive and functional outcomes were similar across groups throughout the study. CONCLUSION: These findings identify PAD as a condition associated with progressive MCA MFV elevation in the context of preserved cognition, implying that subclinical cerebrovascular changes are detectable by TCD before overt clinical worsening. Future research involving larger cohorts and extended follow-up is required to determine whether such hemodynamic changes forecast eventual cognitive deterioration.

However, how PAD status shapes the longitudinal trajectory of cerebral hemodynamics has not been well characterized. METHODS: We conducted a single-center longitudinal observational study enrolling 132 participants (21 controls, 39 mild cognitive impairment, 72 mild Alzheimer's disease).

title: Outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff undergoing revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia, and the role of peroneal communicating branch quality.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Data evaluating outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff are limited. Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches (PCBs) affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population. METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, and PT). Primary outcomes were wound healing, major amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and amputation/death, assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. A subset analysis stratified single-vessel peroneal runoff patients into a three-tiered, PCB grade: Both branches present with at least one robust (PCB grade 1), a single robust branch (PCB grade 2), or no robust branch (PCB grade 3), and compared each with the single-vessel AT/PT reference group. RESULTS: Overall, 732 patients had single-vessel below-knee runoff: 225 AT, 315 peroneal, and 192 PT. Groups differed significantly in age, sex, and diabetes prevalence. Unadjusted 2-year major amputation rates were significantly higher in the peroneal group [19% vs 9.4% (AT) vs 8.7% (PT); P < .001], as were MALE rates (30% vs 14% vs 26%; P = .01). After adjustment, peroneal runoff was independently associated with higher risk of major amputation [hazard ratio (HR), 1.81; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.04-3.13] and MALE (HR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.03-2.25) compared with AT/PT runoff. These associations persisted in the endovascular cohort (major amputation: HR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.06-4.13; MALE: HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.08-2.35) but did not reach significance in the bypass cohort, which was limited by low-event rates. When patients with single-vessel peroneal runoff were stratified by PCB grades, unadjusted 1-year major amputation rates followed a clear anatomically-driven pattern [6.9% (AT/PT) vs 5.4% (PCB grade 1) vs 15% (PCB grade 2) vs 32% (PCB grade 3); P < .001]. After adjustment, when compared with AT/PT runoff, patients without any robust branch (PCB grade 3) had significantly higher risk of major amputation (HR, 3.21; 95% CI, 1.76-4.84) and MALE (HR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.53-3.79), whereas those with two communicating branches with at least one being robust (PCB grade 1) demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.09-2.62) and no difference in major amputation or MALE. CONCLUSIONS: Peroneal runoff is independently associated with worse limb outcomes following revascularization for CLTI, but this risk may be primarily driven by patients with absent or diminutive communicating branches. Patients with robust branching demonstrate outcomes comparable with AT/PT runoff, underscoring the importance of further evaluation and preoperative assessment of PCB quality - using the proposed PCB grading system - in revascularization planning.

Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches (PCBs) affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population. METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, and PT).

title: Impact of prior antithrombotic therapy on safety and outcomes of endovascular therapy in large-core acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Evidence on whether prior antithrombotic drug (ATD) use affects outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT) is limited in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) within 48 hours, symptomatic ICH, 90-day mortality, ordinal mRS shift, and ≥8-point improvement in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score at 48 hours. Logistic regression models were used to assess treatment effects and interactions between ATD and EVT. RESULTS: interaction interaction A total of 202 patients were included (ATD, n = 70; no ATD, n = 132). There was no significant interaction between use of ATD and the effect of EVT in terms of the primary outcome (p=0.944) or secondary outcomes (p=0.218-0.752). In the EVT cohort, prior ATD use was not associated with the primary outcome (adjusted OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.41-3.23). Results were consistent for antiplatelet drugs (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.18-2.71) and anticoagulants (adjusted OR 1.52, 95% CI 0.45-5.20). CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory subanalysis, prior ATD use did not significantly modify the observed treatment effect of EVT in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. These findings suggest that prior ATD use alone should not preclude consideration of EVT.

title: Achieving an endovascular therapy door-to-device time under 90 minutes in patients with ischemic stroke was associated with 90-day mRS.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The American Heart Association (AHA) has a current goal of performing 50% of endovascular therapy (EVT) procedures with a door-to-device (DTD) time of 90 minutes or less for direct arriving patients. Initiatives to improve DTD times need evidence of patient benefit to justify long-term adoption. METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke. The likelihood of a favorable patient outcome was quantified for patients with a DTD time ≤90 minutes compared to patients with a DTD time >90 minutes. RESULTS: DTD ≤90 minutes was associated with an increased odds of having a more favorable (0-2) modified Rankin Score at 90-days (AOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.15-2.00; P = .004) post stroke compared to DTD >90 minutes. We did not find that DTD under or over 90 minutes had a significant association with discharge home (AOR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.00-1.46; P = .051) or patients' length of stay (β, -0.48; 95% CI, -1.30-0.34; P = .20). CONCLUSIONS: Our study supports that EVT completed with DTD time ≤90 minutes was associated with better functional outcomes for patients.

Initiatives to improve DTD times need evidence of patient benefit to justify long-term adoption. METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke.

title: Unexpected Position of a Hemodialysis Catheter.
abstract: Central venous catheterization is frequently employed to obtain urgent hemodialysis access, and catheter malposition due to unrecognized venous anomalies is an underappreciated complication. We describe the case of a 77-year-old man with end-stage renal disease and an extensive vascular access history who required a temporary hemodialysis catheter after thrombosis of his arteriovenous graft. The catheter was placed uneventfully in the left internal jugular vein under ultrasound guidance, but control radiography showed its tip lying in the left hemithorax, and blood gas analysis from the catheter was compatible with arterial blood. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed the catheter tip within the left superior pulmonary vein, which drained into the left brachiocephalic vein, consistent with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return, a rare congenital anomaly usually discovered incidentally. The catheter was removed without complications, and the patient was managed without hemodialysis until his arteriovenous graft was successfully salvaged two days later. This case highlights that an atypical catheter trajectory combined with an arterialized blood gas does not imply arterial puncture and that anomalous venous anatomy should be in the differential diagnosis.

title: Hypoxia and right ventricular dysfunction in patients with acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE), hypoxia may increase pulmonary vascular resistance and worsen right ventricular dysfunction (RVD), which is a key prognostic factor. However, associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes have not been well described. AIM: To describe associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes in patients with PE. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of patients treated by the Massachusetts General Hospital Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) from 10/2012 to 08/2021. Inclusion criteria included confirmed PE, recorded oxygen saturation prior to PERT activation, and echocardiogram within three days of PERT activation. Patients were categorized into four subgroups based on (1) hypoxia status (SaO₂ below vs. above 95%) and, (2) oxygen support (below vs. above 3 L/min). Our primary outcome was the presence of RVD on echocardiogram. Our secondary outcome was clinical deterioration within 7 days. RESULTS: We included 894 PE patients. The mean age was 61 (± 16 SD), 614/894 (69%) were hypoxic, and 624/894 (70%) had RVD on echocardiogram. Overall, hypoxic patients were more likely to have RVD than non-hypoxic patients (467/614 [76%] vs. 157/280 [56%], p < 0.0001). On subgroup analysis, RVD prevalence was highest in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group (n = 216/266, 81%) followed by the "not hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group 53/70 (76%); 198/278 (71%) in the "hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" and 157/280 (56%) in the "not hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" groups. Clinical deterioration occurred in 199/894 (22%) patients and was more common in hypoxic patients than non-hypoxic patients (157/614 [26%] vs. 42/280 [15%], p < 0.0001), and most common in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" subgroup 88/266 (33%). CONCLUSIONS: Hypoxia is associated with RVD and clinical deterioration in patients with PE. More research is needed to understand the risk associated with hypoxia and the physiology of supplemental oxygen support in PE. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title: Post-thrombotic syndrome after thrombotic venous thoracic outlet syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thrombotic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (T-vTOS), including Paget-Schrotter syndrome, is a rare form of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis that mainly affects young, active individuals. Its optimal management remains debated, and the medium-term outcomes have been poorly documented. METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive patients diagnosed with T-vTOS at the vascular medicine department of a university hospital between 2014 and 2024. Patients were stratified according to the presence of post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) using the modified Villalta score at the last follow-up (<5 vs ≥5). Clinical characteristics, therapeutic strategies, and outcomes were systematically assessed through a standardized evaluation performed by the same physician. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses, using Firth's penalized-likelihood method to account for the limited number of events, were performed to identify the factors associated with PTS. RESULTS: A total of 50 patients were included: 28 with a Villalta score of <5 and 22 with a Villalta score of ≥5 at the last follow-up. Patients with a Villalta score of <5 achieved higher rates of complete subclavian vein recanalization at follow-up (63% vs 32%; P = .045) and were less likely to have persistent subclavian vein occlusion (26% vs 59%; P = .023). Patients with a Villalta score of ≥5 more often required prolonged anticoagulation (73% vs 29%; P = .004) and more frequently underwent acute-phase endovascular treatment (36% vs 4%; P = .007). In the multivariable analysis, endovascular treatment alone without thoracic outlet surgery was associated with an increased risk of PTS (odds ratio, 10.6; 95% confidence interval, 1.15, 98.09) (P = .037), whereas no association was found between the risk of PTS and patients who had undergone both endovascular treatment and TOS surgery (odds ratio 1.3; 95% confidence interval, 0.26, 6.87) (P = .736). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the central role of venous patency in the clinical course of T-vTOS, with persistent subclavian vein occlusion associated with an increased risk of PTS. The association observed between acute-phase endovascular treatment alone and the risk of PTS does not support a clear benefit of this strategy. However, endovascular therapy in conjunction with surgical decompression of the thoracic outlet may reduce the risk of PTS.

Its optimal management remains debated, and the medium-term outcomes have been poorly documented. METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive patients diagnosed with T-vTOS at the vascular medicine department of a university hospital between 2014 and 2024.

title: A comparison of aspiration thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis in the management of Paget-Schroetter syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet syndrome (Paget-Schroetter syndrome [PSS]) requires the prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein through catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded based on the degree of luminal encroachment and vessel irregularity: mild (<10%), moderate (10%-50%), and severe (50%-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of the procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency on the last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. Of these patients, 54 met the inclusion criteria: 28 underwent CDT and 26 underwent ASP. At 1 week following the procedure, rethrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 6 (23.1%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8% of patients who underwent ASP. The composite rate of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Before PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 8 (30.8%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .05). PTC was mild in 13 (46.4%) patients receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP (P < .05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (32.1%) receiving CDT and 8 (30.8) receiving ASP. At early follow-up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) patients receiving CDT and 4 (23.5) receiving ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) receiving CDT and 1 (5.9%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (39.1%) receiving CDT and 6 (35.3%) receiving ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) patients receiving CDT and 6 (35%) receiving ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency in 22 (95%) patients receiving CDT and 15 (88%) receiving ASP. CONCLUSIONS: Both ASP and CDT may be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS; however, they differ in early efficacy, PTC, and patency. Our results suggest that while often more rapid and convenient, ASP may be inferior to CAT in the management of PSS.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP.

title: Sex-specific association between preoperative foot infection and vein graft stenosis after distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Sex differences in lower-extremity bypass outcomes remain controversial, and the mechanism is unclear. We examined whether female sex is associated with vein graft stenosis (VGS), predominantly due to intimal hyperplasia, after distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and whether preoperative foot infection contributes. METHODS: We studied 318 limbs with CLTI undergoing para- or inframalleolar autogenous vein bypass at a single center (2000-2014; 74 women, 23%). All analyses were restricted to single-vein grafts; after excluding grafts occluding within 30 days, 232 formed the analytic cohort (182 men, 50 women). Female vs male outcomes were compared by 1:1 optimal matching (Mahalanobis distance within a propensity-score caliper on six covariates) and by inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, which was the primary inference; death was treated as a competing risk. Stenosis was diagnosed by duplex surveillance, with histologic examination of excised segments. Wound, ischemia, and foot infection grades and preoperative C-reactive protein and fibrinogen were analyzed by sex with sex-by-exposure interaction terms; wound cultures were reviewed. RESULTS: After matching (48 pairs), the 5-year cumulative incidence of VGS remained higher in women (44% vs 9%; log-rank P = .004), and primary patency was lower (52% vs 88%; P = .003); secondary patency (85% vs 98%; P = .06) and limb salvage (P = .60) did not differ significantly. Weighting confirmed the excess [adjusted hazard ratio (HR), 2.13; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-4.02; P = .019]. Five-year mortality was 55% in men vs 35% in women; with death as a competing risk, stenosis incidence remained higher in women (34% vs 16%). Preoperative high-grade foot infection was associated with stenosis in women (HR, 4.27; 95% confidence interval, 1.56-11.70; P = .005) but not men (HR, 0.87; P = .74), with a significant sex-by-infection interaction (P = .026); wound and ischemia grades showed no sex difference. C-reactive protein and fibrinogen showed the same direction without a significant interaction. All 25 excised stenotic segments showed intimal hyperplasia without active inflammation, and organism type was unrelated to stenosis. In women, foot infection, poor vein quality, and run-off resistance were independent correlates. CONCLUSIONS: Women undergoing single-vein distal bypass for CLTI have a higher incidence of VGS despite balanced baseline risk, with the excess concentrated in those with preoperative foot infection. The findings suggest a sex-specific vein-wall response to infection-related inflammation and support intensified, infection-aware graft surveillance in women.

METHODS: We studied 318 limbs with CLTI undergoing para- or inframalleolar autogenous vein bypass at a single center (2000-2014; 74 women, 23%).

title: Emerging precision techniques in technology-assisted customized endovascular management of thoracoabdominal aneurysms with anomalous arch branching.
abstract: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is highly complex, especially in the presence of rare aortic arch branching anomalies that complicate fenestrated graft deployment. Emerging technologies such as robotic-assisted vascular surgery with haptic feedback and advanced imaging aim to improve precision and reduce technical errors in these challenging cases. Patient-specific 3D-printed vascular models further enhance preoperative planning and intraoperative navigation by improving anatomical understanding in complex arch variants. Spinal cord ischemia remains a major complication after TAAA repair, and reduced operative time through minimally invasive and robotic-assisted approaches may potentially lower this risk, although evidence is still limited. While these innovations show promise in improving surgical accuracy and efficiency, robust multicenter studies are needed to validate their effectiveness and define their role in standard clinical practice.

title: Floating Atheromatous Plaque in the Common Femoral Artery: A Rare Case With Implications for Diagnosis and Management.
abstract: Floating plaques are well recognized in the carotid artery but are rarely described in the femoral circulation. We present the case of a 73-year-old man with advanced peripheral arterial disease and features of chronic limb-threatening ischemia, including chronic left foot ulceration with a non-healing second-toe ulcer with exposed bone, in the background of prior transmetatarsal amputations and delayed wound healing. A mobile plaque was identified in the left common femoral artery on dynamic B-mode ultrasound, whereas computed tomography angiography showed eccentric calcified stenosis without a definite floating component. The patient underwent femoral endarterectomy with patch repair, and histology confirmed a ruptured calcified atheromatous plaque. Recovery was uneventful, and 12-month follow-up showed no restenosis. This case highlights the diagnostic value of dynamic B-mode ultrasound for detecting mobile femoral atheromatous lesions.

title: Aortoduodenal Syndrome: A Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Causing a Small Bowel Obstruction With Stroke-Like Symptoms.
abstract: Aortoduodenal syndrome is a rare complication of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) in which extrinsic compression of the duodenum results in gastric outlet or small bowel obstruction. We present the case of a 73-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with dizziness, profuse vomiting, cerebellar neurologic findings, and absent palpable lower-extremity pulses. Imaging demonstrated a large infrarenal AAA with findings concerning for contained rupture and extrinsic compression of the duodenum, resulting in gastric and duodenal dilation and at least a partial small bowel obstruction. The patient underwent emergent endovascular aortic repair with stent graft placement and was successfully discharged home on postoperative day 1. This case highlights the variable presentation of aortoduodenal syndrome, which may include gastrointestinal obstructive symptoms, hemodynamic instability, vascular compromise, and stroke-like exam findings. Given the rarity of this condition, clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for aortic pathology when these findings occur concurrently. Although computed tomography angiography is generally preferred when feasible, the choice of imaging modality should account for patient stability, availability, and diagnostic accuracy. Prompt recognition and definitive vascular intervention are essential to prevent catastrophic complications associated with ruptured AAA.

title: Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Upadacitinib in Patients with Psoriatic Arthritis: 5-Year Results from the Phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In the phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 study, treatment with upadacitinib (UPA), an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, improved signs and symptoms of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) from weeks 12 through 152. We now report the long-term extension phase, evaluating safety and efficacy of upadacitinib versus adalimumab (ADA) up to week 260 (~ 5 years). METHODS: Data on treatment-emergent adverse events and all primary and secondary endpoints were collected through week 260 for patients who received a placebo or ≥ 1 dose of UPA at either 15 mg (UPA15) or 30 mg (UPA30) daily, or ADA 40 mg every other week. For non-radiographic binary endpoints, both observed data and non-responder imputation methods were used, whereas for radiographic binary endpoints, the observed data method was used. For continuous endpoints, observed data and mixed-effects model repeated-measures analyses were employed. RESULTS: A total of 1704 patients received at least one dose of study drug, with 983 (57.7%) completing 260 weeks of treatment. The safety profile of UPA through week 260 was consistent with data from weeks 104 and 152. UPA treatment was associated with higher rates of serious infections, herpes zoster, lymphopenia, creatine kinase elevation, and non-melanoma skin cancer compared with ADA treatment. The exposure-adjusted incidence rates for major adverse cardiovascular events (n/100 PY [95% CI]: UPA15, 0.4 [0.2, 0.8]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.3 [0.1, 0.7]) and venous thromboembolism (UPA15, 0.2 [0.0, 0.5]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.2 [0.0, 0.6]) were low and comparable across treatment groups. Efficacy improvements observed with UPA at weeks 56 and 104 were maintained through week 260 and were comparable to those achieved with ADA. CONCLUSIONS: The safety profile of UPA over 5 years remained consistent with that observed at weeks 104 and 152, with no new signals identified. title: Endovascular magnetic filters for removing excess chemotherapeutic drugs from blood flow using dimensionless scaling laws.
abstract: CE Intra-arterial chemotherapy (IAC) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by the escape of chemotherapeutic agents into systemic circulation, causing severe side effects such as heart failure. This study aims to develop and optimize endovascular magnetic filtration devices to enhance IAC efficacy, by targeted removal of excess drug-coated ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) particles from circulation. Device performance was evaluated through multi-physics simulations that coupled the transport of drug-coated magnetic particles in blood flow with magnetic interactions and magnetophoretic forces. A dimensional analysis framework was applied to characterize particle capture efficiency () across alternative device designs, and numerical predictions were compared with published benchtop experiments. Optimized multi-stage filters achieved up to ~80% predicted capture efficiency, while reducing the risk of intravascular device collapse. These results demonstrate a novel strategy for reducing systemic toxicity in IAC through endovascular magnetic filtration, indicating its potential to improve the safety and effectiveness of HCC treatment.

title: Beyond Absolute Blood Pressure Targets During Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Narrative Review of Intraprocedural Hemodynamics.
abstract: Hemodynamic management is a central component of procedural care for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) during endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT. However, definitions, baseline reference pressures, measurement intervals, and BPV metrics vary widely across studies, and associations with neurological outcomes are inconsistent. Importantly, these systemic BP parameters do not directly establish cerebral perfusion. This limitation supports investigating cerebral autoregulation as a complementary, patient-specific assessment. Evidence linking individualized autoregulatory limits to outcomes remains predominantly post-EVT, with very limited evidence during the pre-recanalization phase under anesthesia. This review examines intraprocedural BP during EVT under anesthesia beyond absolute pressure targets. It considers relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, pressure-time burden, BPV, and individualized autoregulatory limits in relation to cerebral perfusion. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed for studies evaluating hemodynamics during EVT under anesthesia, supplemented by screening of selected reference lists. Studies examining intraprocedural BP targets, relative changes, hypotension duration, pressure-time burden, and BPV in relation to neurological or imaging outcomes under anesthesia were prioritized, with emphasis on the pre-recanalization period. Post-EVT hemodynamic studies were not included in the primary synthesis, except where they informed the discussion of cerebral autoregulation and future research. Intraprocedural hemodynamic variables during EVT characterize different aspects of systemic arterial-pressure exposure that may be relevant to cerebral perfusion in the ischemic penumbra. Absolute pressure, relative change, magnitude and duration of hypotension, pressure-time burden, and BPV should be regarded as complementary rather than interchangeable measures. Differences in reference pressures, definitions, measurement intervals, exposure periods relative to recanalization, and anesthesia techniques limit comparisons and standardization across studies. Future prospective studies, particularly during general anesthesia (GA), should integrate clearly defined systemic BP metrics with dynamic cerebral autoregulation. This may help determine which parameters or combinations best reflect cerebral physiological vulnerability. Individualized autoregulation-guided BP targets remain investigational and require prospective validation before they can inform routine clinical hemodynamic management.

Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT.

title: Endovascular hemorrhage control as a bridge to definitive open repair of a tracheoinnominate fistula.
abstract: A tracheoinnominate fistula (TIF) is an uncommon but lethal complication of tracheostomy that requires rapid intervention to prevent exsanguination. Here, we report the management of a tracheoinnominate fistula using bronchial blockade and endovascular tools to protect the airway, stop bleeding, and stabilize the patient. Twelve days later, repair was performed through a sternotomy with debridement of the injured innominate and reconstruction of the right carotid and subclavian arteries using a rifampin-soaked Dacron graft from the ascending aorta. The tracheal injury was repaired and soft tissue coverage achieved with a thymic flap. The patient recovered without complications and is in good general condition 2 years after the event.

title: Endovascular repair of iatrogenic popliteal artery injury with acute limb ischemia during unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
abstract: Iatrogenic popliteal artery injury is a rare but severe complication of knee arthroplasty. A 75-year-old woman developed massive bleeding and acute limb ischemia during unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. Angiography showed severe popliteal flow impairment with thrombus and absent distal runoff. Because bleeding was controlled and guidewire crossing appeared feasible, an endovascular-first strategy was chosen. After successful crossing, an intravascular ultrasound scan confirmed severe arterial wall disruption and an adequate distal landing zone. VIABAHN stent grafts excluded the injured segment, and tibial thrombus aspiration restored distal perfusion. The patient was discharged without gait impairment. Endovascular-first treatment may be effective in selected patients.

title: Primary Aortic Wall Myxoma Presenting With Recurrent Systemic Embolization: A Hybrid Surgical Management Strategy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary aortic wall myxoma is exceptionally rare and may mimic mural thrombus or acute aortic dissection. CASE SUMMARY: A 38-year-old man presented after approximately 12 hours of acute left lower-limb ischemia with concomitant left upper-limb occlusion. Computed tomography angiography showed filling defects in the ascending and descending thoracic aorta. Recurrent embolization after peripheral thromboembolectomy prompted emergency ascending aortic exploration. A friable intramural myxoma was excised with ascending aortic graft replacement; the descending lesion was excluded by staged thoracic endovascular aortic repair while therapeutic anticoagulation was maintained. DISCUSSION: Histopathology confirmed an aortic wall myxoma. The case illustrates the limitations of imaging and an individualized hybrid strategy for suspected multifocal aortic involvement. TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Recurrent embolization after embolectomy should prompt urgent proximal-source control. Hybrid repair may be considered when anatomy and clinical urgency support it.

title: Perioperative management of DOAC in elective orthopedic surgery: a prospective cohort analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Treatment with direct oral anticoagulants is usually interrupted prior to surgery to reduce bleeding risk. Current guidelines recommend standardized interruption protocols, but the actual preoperative plasma levels and their clinical implications in real-world surgical populations are not well characterized. The aim of this study was to assess preoperative DOAC plasma concentrations and postoperative bleeding and thromboembolic outcomes in patients undergoing elective orthopedic surgery. METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study at Danderyd Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden. Adults (≥ 18 years) treated with apixaban, rivaroxaban, or dabigatran for atrial fibrillation or venous thromboembolism and scheduled for high-bleeding-risk orthopedic procedures were included. DOAC interruption followed national guidelines. Plasma DOAC levels were measured preoperatively using LC-MS/MS. Clinical outcomes, including bleeding and thromboembolic events, were recorded up to 30 days postoperatively. RESULTS: A total of 54 patients receiving ongoing DOAC therapy (mean age, 75.5 years; 54% male) were included, of whom 87% were on apixaban. Plasma DOAC concentrations had a mean of 6.7 ng/mL (range, <1.9 to 23.1 ng/mL), and 38% of patients had levels below the limit of detection (< 2.0 ng/mL). One patient had a concentration >30 ng/mL. Five patients (16%) experienced clinically relevant non-major bleeding; four of these had undetectable DOAC levels. No major bleeding, thromboembolic events, or deaths were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Standardized interruption protocols for DOAC therapy result in low or undetectable plasma levels in most patients undergoing high-risk elective orthopedic surgery. Routine preoperative DOAC level testing appears unnecessary in the general population but may be valuable in subgroups at high risk of bleeding.

Current guidelines recommend standardized interruption protocols, but the actual preoperative plasma levels and their clinical implications in real-world surgical populations are not well characterized. The aim of this study was to assess preoperative DOAC plasma concentrations and postoperative bleeding and thromboembolic outcomes in patients undergoing elective orthopedic surgery.

title: Morphological, clinical, and procedural determinants of embolization outcomes in non-cavernous cerebral dural arteriovenous fistulas: A retrospective study.
abstract: PURPOSE: The purpose of this retrospective study was to determine whether dAVF (dural arteriovenous fistula) characteristics influences treatment indication, embolization techniques, complications, radiation burden, and outcome. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Patients treated by embolization for a brain dAVF were included. Excluded were cavernous sinus and surgically treated dAVF. Patients' demographics, clinical and treatment data were retrieved. dAVF clusters were formed: haemorrhagic versus non-haemorrhagic onset and sinus versus non-sinus type and impact on treatment indication, complications, radiation burden, functional and angiographic outcome was analyzed. RESULTS: In a study involving 119 dAVF in 115 patients, 33 patients (mean age 62 years ± 1.8, 72.7% males) presented with a haemorrhagic onset, while 82 (mean age 58 years ± 1.6, 57.3% females) exhibiting 86 dAVF had no bleeding. The sigmoid sinus was over-represented in the latter (52.3%), whereas a cerebrocortical occipital vein was frequently involved in the former group (27,3%). All but one haemorrhagic dAVF demonstrated a Borden-III classification. At six months, the prevalence of mRS class "0" was significantly higher in the non-haemorrhagic dAVF group (70.7% versus 32.3%) compared to the sinus-type clusters, where no such difference was observed. Six months angiography revealed occlusion in 88.2% of 102 catheterized fistulae, similar for all groups. Onyx volume and injection time was significantly higher in non-haemorrhagic and sinus-type dAVF. In non-haemorrhagic dAVF, fluoroscopy time (66.16 versus 40.48 minutes) and the number of acquisitions (68 versus 50) was significantly higher, but not radiation exposure. Although rare, mortality occurred only in sinus-type non-haemorrhagic dAVF. Facial nerve palsy was the major adverse event in non-haemorrhagic dAVF. CONCLUSION: Employing comparable techniques, occluding non-haemorrhagic onset dAVF takes longer and requires a larger embolic volume, yet it presents a higher likelihood of achieving an excellent functional outcome. Occlusion rates are high in all dAVF clusters. Managing non-haemorrhagic, sinus-type dAVFs requires careful attention.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: Patients treated by embolization for a brain dAVF were included. Excluded were cavernous sinus and surgically treated dAVF.

title: D-dimer in Routine Hospital Practice: Diagnostic Accuracy for Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: Background D-dimer is a sensitive rule-out test for venous thromboembolism (VTE), but most validation data come from selected cohorts with suspected embolism, and its performance in unselected hospital populations is less well characterized. We assessed the diagnostic performance of plasma D-dimer for VTE in an unselected hospital population, with pulmonary embolism (PE) as a subgroup, and evaluated the impact of an age-adjusted D-dimer threshold. Methods In this one-year retrospective study (May 2025-April 2026), 100 patients were included from 143 consecutive plasma D-dimer requests at a tertiary university hospital in Tangier, Morocco, irrespective of department or clinical indication. D-dimer was measured by immunoturbidimetric assay (threshold 500 ng/mL) and compared with CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) for PE and venous Doppler ultrasound for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with a documented reference standard, with PE as a pre-specified subgroup. Results The study population (53% female; mean age 55.6 years) had D-dimer requested across many departments, most often adult emergency (54%). Values were right-skewed (median 814 ng/mL); 65% were positive. Imaging confirmed thromboembolic disease in 15 patients, including 12 venous events (nine PE, three DVT), and excluded it in 26. For VTE, sensitivity was 91.7% (95% CI 61.5-99.8) and negative predictive value (NPV) 92.9% (95% CI 66.1-99.8), with specificity 50.0% (95% CI 29.9-70.1), positive predictive value (PPV) 45.8% (95% CI 25.6-67.2) and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.72 (95% CI 0.55-0.87). For PE, sensitivity and NPV both reached 100% (95% CI 66.4-100.0 and 73.5-100.0), with specificity 52.2% (95% CI 30.6-73.2). An age-adjusted D-dimer threshold raised specificity for VTE to 65.4% without loss of sensitivity. Conclusion In this unselected hospital population, plasma D-dimer showed high sensitivity for PE but low specificity, in keeping with its established role as a rule-out test. Its use in routine practice should be guided by clinical pretest probability and, where appropriate, age-adjusted thresholds.

We assessed the diagnostic performance of plasma D-dimer for VTE in an unselected hospital population, with pulmonary embolism (PE) as a subgroup, and evaluated the impact of an age-adjusted D-dimer threshold. Methods In this one-year retrospective study (May 2025-April 2026), 100 patients were included from 143 consecutive plasma D-dimer requests at a tertiary university hospital in Tangier, Morocco, irrespective of department or clinical indication.

title: One-year outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis in acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed up for up to 1 year or until death. RESULTS: A total of 724 patients were included in this study: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of patients. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index of >0 (73% vs 60%; P < .001). Age and the rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between the groups. The median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, interquartile range, 46-89) than for CDT (58 minutes, interquartile range, 40-77; P = .003). The median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs 0%; P = .048), and CDT was associated with higher intensive care unit admission rates (83% vs 36%; P < .001). However, the 30-day mortality rate was similar between the groups (CDT: 2.6% vs MT: 4.6%; P = .27). Additionally, the 1-year incidence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (MT: 4.5% vs CDT: 3.4%; P = .69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%; P = .31), and all-cause mortality (MT: 7.8% vs CDT: 5.8%; P = .41) were not statistically significantly different between the MT and CDT groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable 30-day mortality rates and 1-year recurrence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and PE. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative cardiac complications, and CDT was associated with more frequent intensive care unit admission.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

title: Intraosseous venous malformation of the distal fibula treated with image-guided sclerotherapy and embolization.
abstract: n Intraosseous venous malformations are rare slow-flow vascular lesions in which involvement of lower-extremity long bones is uncommon. A 51-year-old woman with antithrombin III deficiency and post-thrombotic syndrome presented with focal left leg pain initially attributed to chronic venous disease. Computed tomography venography demonstrated a serpiginous intraosseous lesion within the distal fibula communicating with the peroneal venous system. Image-guided selective embolization was performed using foam sclerotherapy and-butyl cyanoacrylate. Postprocedural imaging confirmed exclusion of the lesion. At follow-up, the patient reported resolution of focal bone pain without radiographic recurrence. This case illustrates diagnostic considerations and technical management of symptomatic lower-extremity intraosseous venous malformations.

title: A Compact Unified Model for Moderate-to-Severe Carotid Artery Stenosis Using Image Segmentation: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a new artificial intelligence model, the compact unified model (CU-Model), for moderate-to-severe carotid artery stenosis using digital subtraction angiography (DSA) images compared to clinical reference standards. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, 156 patients with confirmed moderate-to-severe carotid artery stenosis were included. A pretrained CU-Model (trained on public non-clinical datasets for optical flow and stereo matching) was applied to raw DSA images without any fine-tuning on clinical data to avoid data leakage. The model served exclusively as a post-acquisition support tool: cardiologists applied it immediately after procedures for automated vessel segmentation and highlighting. Final North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) measurements and interpreta-tions were performed manually under expert supervision by 2 blinded researchers. RESULTS: The CU-Model identified left internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis in 84 patients and right ICA stenosis in 72. It misclassified only 1 moderate left ICA stenosis case as normal, achieving 99.4% sensitivity (155/156) for any stenosis detection. For stenosis severity grading, strong agreement with DSA was observed (moderate: 57.68 ± 5.94 vs. 57.71 ± 6.19, r = 0.83, P < .001, 95% CI: 0.76-0.88; severe: 86.96 ± 5.97 vs. 87.02 ± 6.18, r = 0.91, P < .001, 95% CI: 0.85-0.95). Of 156 cases, 106 were moderate (50%-69%) and 50 severe (≥70%), using NASCET-adapted thresholds accounting for measurement variability. Hypertension (77%), smoking, and syncope were common, with significant association in symptomatic patients (P < .05). CONCLUSION: The CU-Model demonstrates strong concordance with DSA as a practical, post-procedure support tool for vessel segmentation. Pending larger validation studies, it shows promise for enhancing clinical workflow efficiency.

A pretrained CU-Model (trained on public non-clinical datasets for optical flow and stereo matching) was applied to raw DSA images without any fine-tuning on clinical data to avoid data leakage.

title: Retained Guidewire Following Perforator Vein Ablation.
abstract: Wire embolization is a rare but potentially serious complication of endovascular procedures. Endovenous thermal ablation is a minimally invasive procedure widely used to treat chronic venous insufficiency. Herein, we report a case of guidewire embolization into the posterior tibial and popliteal veins during endovenous laser ablation treatment that was successfully managed with open surgical retrieval. Because of the extensive length and location of the retained guidewire, inability to obtain reliable distal venous access, and concern for further migration or venous injury with percutaneous manipulation, open surgical retrieval was selected. The guidewire was successfully removed through popliteal vein exploration without perioperative complications. This case highlights the importance of recognizing retained intravascular foreign bodies promptly and maintaining open surgical retrieval as an option when endovascular techniques increase procedural risk.
englishSummary: Wire embolization is a rare but potentially serious complication of endovascular procedures. Endovenous thermal ablation is a minimally invasive procedure widely used to treat chronic venous insufficiency. Herein, we report a case of guidewire embolization into the posterior tibial and popliteal veins during endovenous laser ablation treatment that was successfully managed with open surgical retrieval.

title: Emergency management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy: a systematic review.
abstract: Postoperative airway obstruction after carotid endarterectomy presents a significant challenge to anaesthetists. Airway oedema, with or without haematoma, may rapidly develop with life-threatening consequences. This systematic review aims to inform best practice in the management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy. A literature search was conducted for manuscripts published between 01/01/2000 and 01/07/2025. Articles describing the anaesthetic management of adult patients who developed postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy were included. Reference lists of the reviewed articles were also scrutinised for additional relevant sources. Outcome measures were the presentation of airway obstruction, success rate of airway interventions, duration of tracheal intubation and incidence of airway-related morbidity and mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The literature search yielded 284 articles, of which 32 full papers were reviewed. Six papers were deemed pertinent, in addition to five identified from review of references, for a total of 11 included in this systematic review (five case reports, three case series and three retrospective observational studies) detailing the management of airway compromise post-carotid endarterectomy in 84 cases. Clinical signs correlate poorly with anatomical distortion, and laryngeal oedema is generally more severe than anticipated. Prompt haematoma evacuation improved the success rate of airway management, without associated morbidity or mortality. Surgical exploration under local anaesthesia was efficacious and may avoid the need for airway intervention. Awake tracheal intubation was associated with fewer complications than asleep tracheal intubation and should be considered where time and patient cooperation allow. Emergency front-of-neck access should not be delayed for repeated attempts at tracheal intubation with a high chance of failure. Patients' tracheas should remain intubated for sufficient time after surgical exploration, allowing airway oedema to resolve prior to extubation.
englishSummary: Postoperative airway obstruction after carotid endarterectomy presents a significant challenge to anaesthetists. Airway oedema, with or without haematoma, may rapidly develop with life-threatening consequences. This systematic review aims to inform best practice in the management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy.

title: Herpes zoster as a trigger of cardiovascular events: A systematic review of epidemiological evidence and pathophysiological mechanisms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Herpes zoster (HZ) has been associated with acute cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, particularly stroke. We systematically reviewed epidemiological evidence and biological mechanisms linking HZ to vascular outcomes. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched for observational studies evaluating cardiovascular or cerebrovascular events after HZ or herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO). Cohort, case-control, self-controlled case-series, and case-crossover studies were eligible. Mechanistic reports were considered separately to assess biological plausibility. RESULTS: Of 594 records identified, 204 were screened, 11 full-text reports were assessed, and 5 epidemiological studies were included in the primary synthesis. Stroke showed the most consistent association with HZ. Risk was greatest during the first weeks and months after infection, with self-controlled analyses indicating a peak approximately 3-4 weeks after HZ onset. HZO was associated with greater cerebrovascular risk than general HZ. Evidence for myocardial infarction and peripheral arterial disease was suggestive but less consistent. Mechanistic evidence supported roles for varicella-zoster virus-associated vasculopathy, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, thrombosis, vascular remodeling, and plaque destabilization. CONCLUSIONS: Clinically manifest HZ is associated with a transient increase in vascular risk, most consistently for stroke. The temporal pattern and stronger association after HZO support HZ as a potential acute vascular trigger, while evidence for myocardial infarction and other vascular outcomes remains less robust.

We systematically reviewed epidemiological evidence and biological mechanisms linking HZ to vascular outcomes. title: Higher fibrosis-4 index is associated with 1-year in-stent restenosis after carotid artery stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) is a clinically important complication of carotid artery stenting (CAS); however, practical risk markers remain understudied. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with atherosclerotic risk, and the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, a non-invasive marker of liver fibrosis, has been linked to carotid atherosclerosis progression. Therefore, this study examined whether the FIB-4 index was associated with ISR after CAS. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 132 patients who underwent CAS between 2010 and 2023. ISR was defined as peak systolic velocity ≥175 cm/s on at least two consecutive duplex examinations. The primary analysis evaluated FIB-4 continuously per 1-SD increase using Cox models. Secondary exploratory analyses used a cohort-derived cutoff determined by the Youden index. RESULTS: ISR occurred in 16/132 (12%) patients. When analyzed continuously, FIB-4 was not significantly associated with ISR in univariable analysis (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.34; 95% CI, 0.88-2.04; p = 0.172) or in a parsimonious model adjusted for sex and stent design (adjusted HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 0.89-2.21; p = 0.142). The cohort-derived cutoff was 2.08. In secondary exploratory analysis, FIB-4 ≥ 2.08 was associated with higher ISR risk after adjustment for sex and stent design (adjusted HR, 3.93; 95% CI, 1.42-10.9; p = 0.008). CONCLUSIONS: Although continuous FIB-4 was not significantly associated with ISR, exploratory cutoff-based analyses suggested an association between higher FIB-4 and 1-year ISR after CAS. Further validation is required before clinical use.

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with atherosclerotic risk, and the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, a non-invasive marker of liver fibrosis, has been linked to carotid atherosclerosis progression. Therefore, this study examined whether the FIB-4 index was associated with ISR after CAS.

title: Proton pump inhibitor use was not associated with reduced gastrointestinal bleeding risk in ischemic stroke patients treated with dual antiplatelet therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use and gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 3,122 AIS patients with large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) treated with DAPT at Qingdao University Affiliated Hospital (September 2020-December 2023). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics. To address confounding by indication, we additionally performed 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) as a sensitivity analysis, with conditional logistic regression applied to the matched cohort. RESULTS: 45.0% (n = 1,404) received concomitant PPI. No significant difference in GIB incidence was observed between PPI users and non-PPI users (2.1% vs. 1.3%, p = 0.12). Subgroup analyses revealed that PPI use was significantly associated with increased GIB risk in non-endovascular therapy patients (aOR = 2.08, p = 0.03), particularly those with posterior circulation infarction (aOR = 5.96, p = 0.006). These findings were further supported by propensity score matching analysis (conditional OR = 1.64, 95% CI 0.87-3.09, p = 0.124 for the overall cohort; conditional OR = 12.29, 95% CI 1.59-94.90, p = 0.016 for posterior circulation infarction in the non-endovascular subgroup). No significant association between PPI use and GIB risk was found in endovascular therapy or age-stratified subgroups. CONCLUSION: PPI use was not associated with reduced overall GIB risk in DAPT-treated AIS patients. Routine PPI prophylaxis may be unnecessary for low-bleeding-risk populations, while the association observed in posterior circulation infarction remains hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 3,122 AIS patients with large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) treated with DAPT at Qingdao University Affiliated Hospital (September 2020-December 2023). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics.

title: Pyridinium tri-bromido-stannate(II).
abstract: 5 6 3 3 2 1 3 P n tpy tetrel via II Single crystals of the title compound, (CHN)[SnBr] or [PyH][SnBr], were grown from aqueous solutions of pyridinium bromide, [PyH]Br, and tin dibromide, SnBr. The compound crystallizes in the monoclinic space group2/with two formula units in the asymmetric unit. The cations have bond lengths and angles similar to those found in other pyridinium salts. In its first coordination sphere, the anions have a trigonal-pyramidal () shape with the Snatoms at the apex and the three bromine atoms at the base. The tin-bromine bond lengths are all greater than 2.5 Å, and the bond angles are all less than 92°, which indicates the presence ofbonds. These occur along the twofold screw axis and extend the coordination sphere of the tin atoms to highly distorted, 3-aaa octa-hedra. In the crystal, the two pyridinium cations are aggregatedweak π-π inter-actions into centrosymmetric dimers, which form angles of 61.4 (4)° between them. Additional N-H⋯Br hydrogen bonds between cations and anions are bifurcated and weak.
