title: Selective endovascular aortic repair in connective tissue disease patients within a multidisciplinary program achieves comparable outcomes in high-risk patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Endovascular aortic repair (ENDO) in patients with connective tissue disease (CTD) has historically been discouraged in society guidelines because of durability concerns. However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. METHODS: In this study, 92 patients with CTD undergoing aortic intervention at a single high-volume aortic center between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Patients were stratified by ENDO (n = 50) vs open repair (OPEN; n = 42). The primary outcome was freedom from aortic-related mortality (ARM). The secondary outcomes included technical success, complications, secondary aortic intervention (SAI), and overall survival. A prespecified contemporary analysis (2018-2023) was conducted to evaluate the outcomes following the establishment of a multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate survival and freedom from SAI. RESULTS: The mean age was 48 ± 16 years, and 34% (n = 31) were female. Diagnoses included Marfan syndrome (69%), Loeys-Dietz syndrome (15%), familial aortopathy (11%), and vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (5%). Patients who underwent ENDO more frequently had prior sternotomy/open cardiac surgery (68% vs 19%; P < .0001), prior aortic surgery (70% vs 33%; P = .0007), and urgent presentation (50% vs 14%; P = .0004). Overall, 60% of these patients were deemed unfit for open repair by the multidisciplinary aortic team because of physiologic risk, anatomic complexity, or urgent presentation. The technical success rate was lower after ENDO (82% vs 98%; P = .02), and the 30-day reintervention rate was higher (16% vs 0%; P = .01). The median follow-up period was 2.3 years [interquartile range, 1.1-4.7]. SAIs occurred more frequently following ENDO (56% vs 12%; P = .0001), including planned staged procedures (ENDO: 28.6% vs OPEN: 20%; P = 1) and unplanned reinterventions (ENDO: 71.4% vs OPEN: 80%; P = 1). In the full cohort, patients undergoing ENDO had lower 3-year survival rates (71% ± 7% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .03). In the contemporary cohort, survival at 2 years following ENDO (n = 17) was poorer than that after OPEN (n = 42), although the difference did not reach significance (71% ± 14% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .1). Similarly, the rate of freedom from ARM was lower, but not significantly different (88% ± 12% vs 98% ± 2%; log-rank P = .4). CONCLUSIONS: Open repair remains the gold standard for connective tissue disease-associated aortic disease. In carefully selected high-risk patients, ENDO serves as a complementary strategy with acceptable contemporary survival and comparable freedom from ARM. Higher secondary intervention rates reflect both planned staged repair and unplanned surveillance-detected failure modes, underscoring the need for lifelong follow-up within multidisciplinary programs.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Endovascular aortic repair (ENDO) in patients with connective tissue disease (CTD) has historically been discouraged in society guidelines because of durability concerns. However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program.

title: Chocolate Balloon Versus Conventional Balloon for Vessel Preparation Before Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Lesions: A Real-World Propensity Score-Matched Study.
abstract: To evaluate the procedural and 1-year clinical outcomes of the Chocolate balloon versus conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) for vessel preparation before drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment of femoropopliteal lesions. This retrospective subgroup analysis of the multicenter PROMISING registry included patients with femoropopliteal lesions treated with DCB. Before propensity score matching (PSM), 817 patients underwent POBA and 379 underwent Chocolate balloon angioplasty. After 1:1 PSM, 254 patients were included in each group. The primary endpoint was bailout stenting. Secondary endpoints included maximum DCB diameter, stent length, postprocedural ankle-brachial index (ABI), 1-year clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), major amputation, all-cause mortality, amputation-free survival (AFS), and major adverse events (MAE). After PSM, bailout stenting occurred less frequently in the Chocolate balloon group than in the POBA group (20.47% vs 29.92%, p = 0.014). The Chocolate balloon group also showed a trend toward shorter stent length (20.67 ± 9.75 cm vs 23.71 ± 10.62 cm, p = 0.097) and allowed use of larger DCBs (4.96 ± 0.52 mm vs 4.74 ± 0.61 mm, p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression identified Chocolate balloon use as an independent protective factor against bailout stenting, whereas chronic total occlusion and severe calcification were independent predictors of bailout stenting. No significant differences were observed in 1-year clinical outcomes. Compared with POBA, Chocolate balloon vessel preparation reduced bailout stenting and enabled use of larger DCBs, suggesting potential procedural advantages in complex femoropopliteal lesions. However, these procedural benefits did not translate into improved 1-year clinical outcomes.

This retrospective subgroup analysis of the multicenter PROMISING registry included patients with femoropopliteal lesions treated with DCB. Before propensity score matching (PSM), 817 patients underwent POBA and 379 underwent Chocolate balloon angioplasty.

title: Closing the Gap in Thromboprophylaxis: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Approach Among Medical Inpatients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of a multidisciplinary quality improvement (QI) framework on guideline-directed venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis adherence among hospitalized patients. STUDY DESIGN: A prospective, pre-post interventional study conducted in internal medicine wards with historically low baseline prophylaxis rates. METHODS: Following a retrospective baseline assessment, a multicomponent QI initiative was executed across 2 Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles in adult internal medicine wards at a university hospital between September and November 2022. Interventions included the following: (1) physician education on the Padua Prediction Score and International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism Bleeding Risk Score; (2) implementation of an electronic health record clinical decision-support tool prompting VTE risk assessments; and (3) integration of clinical pharmacists into daily multidisciplinary rounds to provide active audit and feedback. RESULTS: At baseline, 62.1% of high-risk patients received guideline-recommended VTE prophylaxis. Post intervention, this rate increased to 79.1% in the first cycle and 82.1% in the second cycle ( P  = .006). Among clinical pharmacists' 27 recommendations, 70.4% were accepted and implemented. The multidimensional strategy demonstrated sustained improvements in guideline adherence with minimal adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: Implementing a multidisciplinary QI framework significantly enhanced guideline-directed VTE prophylaxis use among hospitalized patients. This collaborative approach underscores the value of electronic decision support, clinical audit-feedback loops, and pharmacist-physician integration in driving patient safety. Ultimately, this system-level strategy provides a scalable model for improving preventive care protocols across diverse hospital settings.

title: [Lower-body Malperfusion Following Surgery for Stanford Type A Acute Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
abstract: The patient was an octogenarian woman who presented with sudden-onset chest pain and was diagnosed with Stanford type A acute aortic dissection. She underwent an emergency Bentall procedure with ascending aortic replacement. On postoperative day three, she developed rapid deterioration of renal function and bilateral lower-limb ischemia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed severe narrowing of the true lumen of the thoracic aorta, which caused malperfusion of the lower body. An entry was identified in the right common carotid artery (RCCA), and a stent-graft was deployed to close the entry;however, lower-limb perfusion did not improve sufficiently. Therefore, left axillo-bilateral femoral (or external iliac) artery bypass (axillo-bifemoral bypass) was subsequently performed. After the bypass procedure, expansion of the aortic true lumen and improvement in organ perfusion were obtained. To treat postoperative malperfusion following surgery for acute aortic dissection, closure of a branch entry alone may be insufficient, and extra-anatomic bypass can be a reliable option.

She underwent an emergency Bentall procedure with ascending aortic replacement. On postoperative day three, she developed rapid deterioration of renal function and bilateral lower-limb ischemia.

title: Topologically complex knotted proteins are processed differentially by ATP-dependent proteases ClpXP and ClpAP.
abstract: 1 1 2 Knotted proteins can present a distinct topological and mechanical challenge to the AAA+ cellular degradation machineries, determined by the relative size of the knot and the pore dimensions of these enzymes. In this study, we investigated the degradation mechanism of knotted proteins of different topological complexities by two E. coli. AAA+ proteases ClpXP and ClpAP. While ClpXP efficiently degraded all knotted substrates, regardless of their topology, ClpAP exhibited a striking functional divergence. Despite its robust double-ring ATPase architecture, ClpAP failed to degrade the 4-knotted miRFP and degraded the 3-knotted CAIX and more complex 5-knotted UCHL1 slower than ClpXP. We have demonstrated that this disparity is not dictated merely by absolute knot complexity, but is critically governed by the length of the knot tail, which determines whether a knot can spontaneously unthread or is forced to tighten during the translocation. Furthermore, based on the slower processing of a sterically constrained covalent dimeric substrate Arc-ssrA, we propose that ClpAP's hindered processing of knotted substrates stems from its smaller axial pore. Overall, we propose a unified physical model in which the successful degradation of a knotted protein relies on a delicate interplay among knot compaction, tail-mediated unthreading, and the architectural permissiveness of the unfoldase pore.

title: Temporal Net Water Uptake Evolution and Its Association with Functional Outcome in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Subacute lesion growth after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with worse functional outcomes. The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes. In this study, we aimed to determine how associations between NWU and functional outcome vary across imaging times up to 1 week after stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included patients from the Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial of Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Netherlands (MRCLEAN-NO IV) trial with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who were treated with endovascular treatment and had baseline, 24-hour, and 1-week follow-up noncontrast CT scans. Functional outcome at 90 days was evaluated using the mRS, analyzed both as functional independence (mRS 0-2) and across the full ordinal distribution (mRS 0-6). In the primary analysis, associations between NWU measured at different imaging time points and functional independence were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models. To evaluate temporal changes in NWU, ΔNWU was calculated at different time intervals (baseline to 24 hours, 24 hours to 1 week, and baseline to 1 week), and its association with outcomes was analyzed using analogous regression models. RESULTS: 1wk-BL Of 539 MRCLEAN-NO IV patients, 115 were included in this study. The median time from stroke onset to randomization was 92 (IQR, 70-140) minutes. The median NWU evolved from 4.3% (interquartile range [IQR], 2.1%-6.8%) at baseline to 9.0% (IQR, 3.0%-13%) at 24 hours and 15% (IQR, 11%-19%) at 1 week. The median patient-level change (ΔNWU) from baseline to 1 week was 10% (IQR, 5.3%-16%). NWU measured at 1 week, but not at baseline or 24 hours, was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an adjusted OR (aOR) of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.90) per 5-percentage-point increase in NWU. Furthermore, a higher increase in NWU from baseline to 1-week imaging was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an aOR of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.86) per 5-percentage-point increase in ΔNWU. CONCLUSIONS: In our population, NWU measured at 1 week is associated with 90-day clinical outcomes, suggesting that lesion evolution continues in the first week after stroke onset and may therefore represent a target for secondary treatments to improve clinical outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Subacute lesion growth after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with worse functional outcomes. The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes.

title: Deep Learning-Based Noncontrast CT Imaging Markers Enhance Posttransfer DWI Core Volume Prediction.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Deep learning enables the extraction of ischemic lesion size and hypodensity imaging markers from deep learning-based NCCT (DLNCCT) assessment in patients with acute ischemic stroke, but it remains unclear whether those markers can predict posttransfer core volume. MATERIALS AND METHODS: R 2 We performed a post hoc analysis of prospectively enrolled patients transferred from a primary stroke center (PSC) to a comprehensive stroke center (CSC) for endovascular treatment (EVT). Using a validated DLNCCT segmentation method, we quantified total lesion volume (per 10 mL), modified net water uptake (mNWU %), and severely hypodense volume (≤26 Hounsfield units [HU] per 10 mL) and compared these markers with core lab rated ASPECTS (per point decrease) and CTP-based evaluation for their association with (adjusted regression coefficient [95% CI]) and predictive performance in addition to baseline variables (± SEs) for posttransfer CSC admission DWI core volume. RESULTS: P R R P R R P R P 2 2 2 2 2 We included 420 patients (239 [57%] men) with a median age of 72 years (interquartile range: 61-80). We observed 11.2 mL (95% CI, 8.3-14.1] larger posttransfer core volumes per point decrease in ASPECTS, and 10.0 mL (95% CI, 6.8-13.3), and 20.0 mL (95% CI, 12.7-27.2) larger posttransfer core volumes per 10-mL increase in total and severely hypodense DLNCCT volume, respectively. mNWU was not associated with posttransfer core volume (= .63). In addition to clinical baseline and CTA variables, posttransfer core volume prediction with ASPECTS (: 0.49 ± 0.02) and DLNCCT (: 0.50 ± 0.02) did not differ significantly (= .58). Compared with using CTP imaging markers (: 0.56 ± 0.02), adding ASPECTS (: 0.63 ± 0.02;< .01) and DLNCCT (: 0.65 ± 0.01;< .01) improved performance for posttransfer core volume prediction. CONCLUSIONS: Total and severely hypodense DLNCCT volumes are independent predictors for posttransfer core volume. These DLNCCT markers improved CTP-based posttransfer core volume prediction.

title: Impact of Balloon-Guided Catheter Position on First-Pass Effect in Mechanical Thrombectomy for Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The first-pass effect (FPE; complete or near-complete reperfusion [extended TICI 2b-3] after a single thrombectomy pass) is a key functional outcome determinant. This study identified factors associated with FPE and quantitatively evaluated how balloon-guided catheter (BGC) positioning relates to FPE achievement during anterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of consecutive patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy using a BGC between May 2022 and February 2025. The BGC tip to the proximal petrous ICA distance was measured using lateral angiography at the initial BGC position. Factors associated with FPE were evaluated using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis determined the optimal cutoff value for predicting FPE. RESULTS: P r P P Among 110 patients (median age, 81 years; 54% men), 56% achieved FPE. A shorter BGC tip to proximal petrous ICA distance was independently associated with higher FPE rates (adjusted OR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.98;< .001). Greater distance correlated with longer procedure time (= 0.3;< .001) and more thrombectomy passes (< .001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified 24 mm as the optimal cutoff (area under the curve, 0.7). Distal BGC positioning was associated with fewer distal emboli and shorter recanalization time without serious complications. CONCLUSIONS: Distal BGC placement within 24 mm of the proximal petrous ICA independently predicted higher FPE achievement and greater procedural efficiency. Quantitative BGC position assessment may provide a practical intraoperative metric to optimize mechanical thrombectomy strategies.

title: SELECT-CT: Symptom Evaluation, Lesion Estimation, and Curated Triage to CT-A Simple Algorithm to Select the Right Patients for Emergent Code Stroke CT.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The intended purpose of multimodal Code Stroke CT (CSCT) is to rapidly identify patients with acute ischemic stroke who are likely to benefit from mechanical thrombectomy. This study aimed to evaluate a new clinical algorithm for reliably identifying thrombectomy candidates while reducing the number of CSCT scans that are currently inundating radiology services. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was performed on consecutive patients who underwent mechanical thrombectomy at a comprehensive stroke center during a 2-year period. The Symptom Evaluation, Lesion Estimation, and Clinical Triage for CT (SELECT-CT) algorithm, ie, an NIHSS score threshold of ≥2 and/or any posterior circulation or disabling symptoms, was applied to identify patients with large and distal medium vessel occlusions who may benefit from thrombectomy. The performance of SELECT-CT and 6 different NIHSS score thresholds (from ≥1 to ≥6) for reducing CSCT scan numbers, while correctly identifying patients treated with thrombectomy, was also assessed. RESULTS: During the study period 4921 patients had CSCT scans, yielding a 5% thrombectomy rate. Of 240 patients (median age 73; 54.6% male) who underwent thrombectomy, the NIHSS score ≥6 captured only 198 (83%), including 151 of 166 patients (91%) with an anterior circulation large vessel occlusion. Conversely, the threshold of ≥2 alone captured 229 of 240 (95%) thrombectomy patients. Using SELECT-CT, performance improved to correct identification of 232 of 240 (97%) thrombectomy patients, including all who should be treated based on current evidence. Applying NIHSS score thresholds of ≥6 and ≥2 for patient triage to CSCT reduced scan volume by 76% and 47%, respectively. The more cautious and nuanced approach using SELECT-CT achieved a 30% reduction in scan numbers. CONCLUSIONS: The SELECT-CT algorithm can reduce CSCT scan workload while still identifying patients who should be treated with thrombectomy.

title: Impact of direct-to-operating room transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of a direct-to-operating room (DOR) transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) on surgical volume, interhospital transfer patterns, and surgical outcomes at a tertiary referral center. METHODS: P This retrospective, single-institution cohort study used institutional databases and the Vascular Quality Initiative registry to identify all patients undergoing rAAA repair between 2014 and 2024. In January 2020, a multidisciplinary rapid-response transfer protocol was implemented to facilitate DOR transfers. Patients were stratified into pre- and postimplementation cohorts. Differences in case volume, transfer patterns, transfer distance, time to treatment, and surgical outcomes between groups were assessed using univariable analysis, with statistical significance set at< .05. RESULTS: P P P P P P A total of 96 patients underwent rAAA repair during the study period, with 28.1% treated before and 71.9% treated after implementation of the transfer protocol. Baseline characteristics were similar between cohorts, except for a higher prevalence of diabetes (40.7% vs 14.5%;= .005) and former smokers (59.3% vs 34.8%;= .029) in the preimplementation group. The annual rAAA repair volume increased threefold after implementation, from a mean of 4.5 to 13.8 cases/year. Overall, 86.5% of patients were transferred from outside hospitals, with a significant increase in the proportion of external transfers after implementation (70.4% vs 92.8%;= .007). Median transfer distance increased from 23.7 to 49.1 miles (= .017) and time from transfer acceptance to operating room arrival decreased from 173 to 124 minutes (= .145). Distance-adjusted transfer time decreased significantly from 9.5 to 4.1 min/mile (= .017). Endovascular repair was performed in 68.8% of patients, with no difference between cohorts. In-hospital stroke (6.2%), myocardial infarction (7.3%), and mortality (22.9%) rates were similar between groups. Median length of stay was 6.6 days. Thirty-day outcomes did not differ between cohorts, with readmission in 13.5%, reintervention in 36.5%, and mortality in 25.0% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a multidisciplinary DOR protocol for rAAA was associated with a sustained increase in surgical volume, higher rates of interhospital transfer, expansion of the regional referral network, and lower distance-adjusted transfer times, with perioperative outcomes remaining within contemporary benchmarks.

In January 2020, a multidisciplinary rapid-response transfer protocol was implemented to facilitate DOR transfers.

title: Drug-Eluting Resorbable Scaffolds for Infrapopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD. Most recently, randomized evidence from the LIFE-BTK trial has demonstrated superior patency and reduced rates of revascularization with DRS-treated lesions as compared with plain balloon angioplasty. In this state-of-the-art review, we summarize the existing evidence evaluating DRS devices for BTK PAD and present an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical outcomes for DRS-based endovascular interventions.

title: Incremental prognostic and risk-stratification value of ultrasound-based Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) classification for recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) is a system for stroke risk assessment. However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis. METHODS: Between January 2020 and December 2022, 231 patients with carotid plaque ipsilateral to the prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis were retrospectively screened, of whom 158 were included in the final analysis. US-based Plaque-RADS classification was assigned based on duplex US assessment of plaque features. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories and recurrent ischemic stroke. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC), and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis. The association between increasing US-based Plaque-RADS categories and the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke was assessed by trend analysis. The incremental risk-stratification value of refined high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds was quantified with net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: vs. During the 3-year follow-up period, recurrent ischemic stroke occurred in 33 patients. High-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, after adjusting for smoking, homocysteine, and intraplaque neovascularization [adjusted hazard ratio: 3.56; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-11.83, P=0.038]. No statistically significant interactions were observed across the subgroups (all P for interaction >0.05). The Plaque-RADS ≥3 model demonstrated a higher AUC than the conventional US model [0.816 (95% CI: 0.731-0.901)0.810 (95% CI: 0.720-0.899)] and provided a slight net benefit across selected threshold probabilities. Additionally, the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke increased with higher Plaque-RADS categories (P for trend <0.001). Among the models using different high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds, the Plaque-RADS ≥3b model showed the best predictive performance (0.865, 95% CI: 0.799-0.930), compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model and the Plaque-RADS ≥3c model [0.824 (95% CI: 0.740-0.906)]. The Plaque-RADS ≥3b model also showed moderate improvements in NRI [0.250; (95% CI: 0.088-0.557), P=0.017] and IDI [0.090; (95% CI: 0.000-0.185), P=0.049], compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model. Bootstrap internal validation indicated limited optimism across all models. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke. The US-based Plaque-RADS may help identify plaque phenotypes associated with an increased risk of recurrent ipsilateral ischemic stroke, while refined high-risk thresholds, particularly Plaque-RADS ≥3b, may provide additional value for risk stratification.

title: Time-zero multimodal risk stratification for in-hospital mortality in acute aortic dissection: two-centre development, temporal and external validation, and occult shock phenotyping.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) requires rapid anatomical diagnosis and early risk stratification, yet initial blood pressure alone may miss patients with concealed hypoperfusion. Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included 2,584 adults with first-time AAD who completed CTA and TTE during the initial 2-hour assessment after emergency department triage. Cohorts were development (n=1,678; 2007-2017), internal temporal validation (n=452; 2018-2021), and external geographic/later-era validation (n=454; 2022-March 2024). Candidate variables were restricted to information available during this initial assessment window. Four supervised algorithms were compared, with ablation analyses assessing modality-specific contribution. RESULTS: XGBoost achieved optimism-corrected development area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.88], internal validation 0.83 (0.79-0.87), and external validation 0.78 (0.74-0.82). Adding TTE to Clinical + CTA improved discrimination (Delta AUC +0.04, P=0.002) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) (+0.021, P=0.01). Normotensive occult shock occurred in 548/2,082 patients (26.3%) and was associated with mortality 15.9% versus 6.7% in metabolically stable normotension. CONCLUSIONS: In high-volume aortic centres where CTA and early TTE are routinely available, this initial 2-hour multimodal model showed temporal validation and moderate external discrimination for in-hospital mortality. TTE added prognostic information, particularly for type A disease, and normotensive hyperlactatemia identified a higher-risk subgroup; however, general use, type B performance, local recalibration, and action thresholds require prospective multicentre validation before clinical implementation.

title: Impact of different follow-up methods on prognosis of diabetic foot patients after endovascular treatment: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus, and endovascular treatment (EVT) has become the primary revascularization strategy. However, the impact of different post-procedure follow-up methods on clinical outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the effects of seven different follow-up approaches on prognosis in DFU patients after EVT. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at three tertiary hospitals in China between June 2022 and June 2025. A total of 868 DFU patients who underwent successful EVT were enrolled and categorized into seven groups based on their primary follow-up method. The primary outcomes were 12-month wound healing rate and amputation-free survival (AFS). Secondary outcomes included major adverse limb events (MALE), reintervention rate, patient satisfaction, and glycemic control. Multivariable Cox regression and propensity score matching were used to adjust for confounders. RESULTS: Among 868 patients, the surgical hospital outpatient group demonstrated the highest 12-month wound healing rate (75.0%) and AFS rate (80.1%). The no follow-up group had the poorest outcomes (45.2% wound healing, 56.4% AFS). No follow-up was associated with significantly increased risk of MALE [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 2.15, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.62-2.85]. WeChat follow-up (aHR 1.22, 95% CI: 0.88-1.69) showed non-significant differences compared with surgical hospital outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Structured follow-up significantly improves wound healing and AFS in DFU patients after EVT. Digital health tools such as WeChat showed no statistically significant difference compared with traditional follow-up, but these observational data should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent effectiveness. The absence of follow-up is associated with substantially worse outcomes. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant validation in prospective randomized trials.

title: Microvascular no-reflow after endovascular therapy: The molecular ceiling on hemodynamic optimization and the next therapeutic frontier.
abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy restores macrovascular patency but fails to achieve tissue-level perfusion in approximately 30% of cases, likely because of the no-reflow phenomenon. Even after optimized hemodynamic management, 40% of patients with angiographically successful recanalization fail to achieve functional independence, revealing a biological ceiling beyond blood pressure optimization. I propose that pericyte contraction via endothelin-1/ET-A receptor signaling, neutrophil CD11b/CD18-dependent capillary plugging, and platelet microthrombus, mechanisms operating orthogonally to systemic hemodynamics, define this ceiling. I review imaging and biomarker strategies for identifying microvascular failure and discuss endothelin receptor antagonism, integrin blockade, and intra-arterial thrombolysis as therapeutic priorities for next-generation of post-thrombectomy trials.

title: A lethal ORC ATPase mutation is suppressed by alterations in ORC and RNA Pol II transcription components.
abstract: The origin recognition complex (ORC) binds origins of replication and directs the loading of the Mcm2-7 replicative helicase at these sites. Five of the six ORC subunits are related to the AAA+ family of ATPases. Although functions for ATP hydrolysis by Cdc6 and the Mcm2-7 complex have been described, the essential role of ORC ATP hydrolysis remains unclear. We performed a genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae for suppressors of the lethal phenotype of the orc4-R267A allele, which disrupts ORC ATP hydrolysis in vitro. We identified six causative mutations, five of which are distributed across different ORC subunits. The suppressor mutations in Orc1 and Orc4, but not those in other ORC subunits, increase the in vitro helicase loading activity of ATPase-defective ORC (ORC4R). Allele specificity studies show the alleles specifically suppress defects at ATPase interfaces within the ORC-Cdc6 complex. The sixth allele is a mutation in TOA2, a subunit of the TFIIA general transcription factor. Mutations in the general transcription factors TBP and TFIIB, and the large subunit of RNA Polymerase II also suppress orc4-R267A lethality, suggesting that reducing transcription is sufficient for suppression. Our study identifies multiple pathways to suppress the lethal phenotype of an ATPase-defective ORC allele and reveals a connection between ORC ATP hydrolysis and transcription.

title: Giant splenic arteriovenous shunt with arterial and venous aneurysmal dilatation causing portal hypertension and gastric varices.
abstract: A 59-year-old woman presented with recurrent hematemesis and generalized weakness. Imaging revealed a giant high-flow arteriovenous shunt between markedly dilated splenic arterial and venous systems, associated with an 8 × 5 cm splenic arterial aneurysmal component, portal hypertension, and gastric fundal varices. Angiography demonstrated high flow through markedly dilated vessels, precluding safe endovascular embolization. The patient underwent open splenectomy with complete excision of the vascular lesion, achieving full symptom resolution and complete resolution of gastric varices at 6-month follow-up. Giant splenic arteriovenous shunts are exceedingly rare, and no consensus on their optimal management has been established. Management should be individualized according to vascular anatomy and flow characteristics, with splenectomy reserved for lesions unsuitable for endovascular treatment. The etiology of the arteriovenous shunt remained uncertain, as neither a congenital origin nor a remote post-traumatic origin could be established.

title: Concurrent treatment of iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis and submassive pulmonary embolism through a single popliteal venous access.
abstract: Concomitant extensive iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and submassive pulmonary embolism (PE) present a therapeutic challenge for endovascular management. We report the case of a 74-year-old man presenting with extensive right iliofemoral and inferior vena cava DVT associated with bilateral PE and right ventricular strain. Using right popliteal venous access, thrombus was successfully removed from the inferior vena cava and iliofemoral venous system, and both pulmonary arteries. This case demonstrates the feasibility of treating both extensive lower-extremity DVT and submassive PE concurrently through a single popliteal venous access using one thrombectomy platform.

title: Repair of iatrogenic subclavian injury through paracorporeal endovascular access.
abstract: As the number of patients supported with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) continues to rise, vascular surgeons are challenged to adopt alternative endovascular access strategies to manage life-threatening ischemic or hemorrhagic complications. We present the case of a pediatric patient maintained on central venoarterial ECMO who developed a left hemothorax in impending cardiorespiratory collapse. A 11F Y-connector was fashioned into a Berlin arterial cannula (Berlin Heart GmbH) for endovascular access to the mid-ascending aorta and was used to treat proximal subclavian artery extravasation. This approach demonstrates the utility of maintaining arterial outlet pressures while simultaneously providing endovascular access to urgently treat patients on ECMO.

title: PERT implementation and the changing profile of patients undergoing catheter-based pulmonary embolism treatment: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Despite growing evidence supporting pulmonary embolism response teams (PERT) in high-income countries, published experience from Latin America remains scarce. We assessed the association between PERT implementation and 30-day clinical outcomes in patients with acute PE treated with catheter-based therapy (CBT) in a Latin American university hospital. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with confirmed acute PE treated with CBT between 2004 and 2025. Patients were stratified by treatment era (pre-PERT: 2004-2020; PERT: 2021-2025). The primary endpoint was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, stroke, or major bleeding (BARC grade ≥3). RESULTS: A total of 53 patients were included: 26 (49%) pre-PERT and 27 (51%) PERT era. ESC high-risk patients predominated in the pre-PERT era (17 (65%) vs 6 (22%); p = 0.002), while intermediate-high risk predominated in the PERT era (9 (35%) vs 21 (78%); p = 0.002). Dedicated thrombectomy devices were used universally in the PERT era (14 (54%) vs 27 (100%); p < 0.001). MACE occurred in 10 (38%) vs 4 (15%) patients (p = 0.06). In a subanalysis restricted to intermediate-high risk patients, 30-day mortality was 0/21 (0%) in the PERT era versus 3/9 (33%) in the pre-PERT era (p = 0.021). CONCLUSIONS: In one of the few Latin American reports on PERT-guided CBT, implementation was associated with a shift toward intermediate-high risk patients, greater use of mechanical thrombectomy, and lower thrombolytic exposure, without an increase in major bleeding. Among intermediate-high risk patients, 30-day mortality was significantly lower in the PERT era, supporting the safety and potential benefit of structured multidisciplinary PE management in resource-limited settings.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with confirmed acute PE treated with CBT between 2004 and 2025.

title: Cardiovascular involvement in gram-negative bloodstream infection: Timing, phenotypes, and mechanisms.
abstract: Gram-negative bloodstream infection (GN-BSI) is associated with a heterogeneous spectrum of cardiovascular manifestations extending beyond the hemodynamic consequences of sepsis. Epidemiological evidence identifies a transient period of heightened cardiovascular vulnerability, with myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke clustering close to BSI onset, alongside myocardial dysfunction, arrhythmias, thrombotic complications, and direct vascular or endovascular infection. These phenotypes likely reflect different interactions between systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, immunothrombosis, underlying cardiovascular disease, and pathogen-specific factors. Persistent bacteremia, prosthetic cardiovascular material, vascular disease, and selected Gram-negative pathogens may identify settings warranting greater cardiovascular attention. However, current evidence remains limited by predominantly retrospective designs, heterogeneous outcome definitions, non-standardized cardiovascular assessment, and limited integration of microbiological and cardiovascular data. This review integrates clinical, epidemiological, and mechanistic evidence to define the timing, phenotypes, and mechanisms of cardiovascular involvement in GN-BSI and proposes a phenotype-driven framework for cardiovascular interpretation and future research.

title: Pre-operative proton pump inhibitor use is associated with increased post-operative complications following anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are frequently prescribed in the perioperative setting for gastrointestinal prophylaxis. However, emerging evidence suggests that pre-operative PPI exposure may influence post-operative outcomes through effects on host immune function, nutritional status, and bone metabolism. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between pre-operative PPI use and post-operative complications following anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adult patients undergoing primary anatomic TSA between 2005 and 2023 were stratified by pre-operative PPI use. Patients with a history of gastrointestinal bleeding were excluded. Propensity score matching was performed for demographic characteristics, modified frailty index variables, additional comorbidities, medications, and body mass index, yielding 7,075 patients per cohort. Ninety-day medical and 1-year and 2-year surgical complications were compared using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: P P P P P P Within 90 days, PPI exposure was associated with increased risks of readmission and acute kidney injury. Rates of emergency department utilization were also higher among patients receiving PPIs, whereas differences in pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, post-operative infection, and stroke did not reach statistical significance. At 1 year, perioperative PPI use was associated with significantly higher rates of periprosthetic joint infection (1.7% vs. 1.2%; RR, 1.45;= .008), dislocation (2.0% vs. 1.5%; RR, 1.33;= .027), aseptic loosening (0.8% vs. 0.4%; RR, 1.71;= .016), and mortality (1.2% vs. 0.9%; RR, 1.40;= .044). At 2 years, PPI use remained associated with increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (2.4% vs. 1.6%; RR, 1.52;< .001) and mortality (2.5% vs. 1.7%; RR, 1.48;= .001). No significant differences were observed in revision arthroplasty, periprosthetic fracture, dislocation, or aseptic loosening at 2 years. CONCLUSION: Pre-operative PPI use following TSA was associated with increased early medical complications and higher rates of implant-related complications at midterm follow-up. These findings highlight the importance of careful medication review and risk stratification in patients undergoing anatomic TSA.

title: Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Identifies Central Role for Inflammatory Pathways.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Epigenetic mechanisms underlying susceptibility to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) remain poorly understood. Identifying causal DNA methylation markers for AAA can elucidate the regulatory processes that drive aneurysm formation and accelerate translational applications. We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways. METHODS: We first conducted an epigenome-wide association study of incident AAA (1324 cases and 42 065 noncases), performed stratified analyses by population group and smoking status, and conducted Mendelian randomization to facilitate causal inference of the cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG)-AAA association. Chromatin state, island context, and transcription factor binding were implicated through functional annotation of identified CpGs. To identify genes impacted by change in methylation state, we aligned associations with transcriptional data obtained in blood, aorta, and liver. We performed expression quantitative trait methylation to capture CpG-gene-expression links across the genome. Network Mendelian randomization was used to test cardiometabolic and inflammatory mediation. Finally, we developed a methylation risk score for AAA using penalized regression and evaluated its performance against a clinical model in the Million Veteran Program and 2 external studies. RESULTS: AGER, C2 DDR1 LDLR TRIB1 Epigenome-wide association study identified 1253 CpGs associated with incident AAA, and Mendelian randomization supported a putative causal role for 143 of these associations. Functional annotation pointed to predominantly distal, enhancer-centered regulation and enrichment of inflammatory transcription factor programs (eg, activator protein-1 and nuclear factor κB). This distal architecture was consistent with expression quantitative trait methylation results, which showed a larger number of trans associations. Among 143 CpGs associated with AAA in Mendelian randomization analyses, we identified 213 CpG-gene expression pairs with strong colocalization support, including, and. Multi-trait colocalization further prioritized 8 CpG-gene expression-AAA links with evidence of a shared genetic signal. Network Mendelian randomization identified 135 putative mediation pathways linking CpGs to AAA, including 58 via cardiometabolic traits and 77 via inflammation-related traits. Blood lipid traits mediated >40% of the associations between AAA risk and CpGs near(cg19305903) and(cg14128479). Among inflammation-related mediators, circulating DAG1, NEXN, MMP9, IL1RN, and MMP13 were prioritized as potential intermediates. Additionally, a CpG selection process was used to develop a methylation risk score for AAA, which strongly associated with disease in both the discovery cohort and 2 external validation cohorts, even after adjustment for a full suite of clinical covariates. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified putative causal DNA methylation markers for AAA, and multi-omics analyses implicate activator protein-1-linked inflammatory transcriptional programs, blood lipids, and multiple inflammation-related proteins as key pathways underlying methylation-associated AAA risk.

title: The Association Between Hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center Designation Status and Stroke Rate Reporting in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Implications for Hospital Performance Assessment.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Michigan Structural Heart Consortium showed that transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) stroke rates were associated with hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) designation, suggesting that hospital structural factors affect stroke reporting. We sought to determine whether CSC designation is nationally associated with reported stroke rates and the potential impact on hospital performance and Transcatheter Valve Therapy National Data Registry (TVTR) public reporting. METHODS: Consecutive TVTR cases from January 2016 through June 2023 were included, excluding sites reporting to the TVTR <1 year or performing <20 total TAVR procedures. The primary outcome was in-hospital stroke rate. Secondary outcomes were disabling stroke and 30-day stroke. Major bleeding, death, acute renal failure, and a composite end point were falsification end points to determine whether CSC status was uniquely associated with stroke. Multivariable hierarchical models were created starting with patient covariates and sequentially adding hospital variables to account for determinants of stroke. The impact of CSC status on hospital performance was estimated by correcting CSC hospital stroke rates in the validated TVTR 30-day composite model. RESULTS: P P P P P A total of 525 919 TAVRs at 800 sites were included, and 10 963 strokes (2.1%) were reported within 30 days: 8284 (1.6%) in-hospital and 2679 (0.5%) after discharge. A total of 4733 (0.9%) were disabling strokes. Multivariate analysis showed that CSC status and participation in TAVR trials were independent predictors of in-hospital stroke rate (=0.033 and 0.012) and disabling stroke (=0.033 and 0.007), but not falsification end points (=NS). Participation in TAVR trials and operator volume were independent predictors of 30-day stroke (=0.039 and=0.041). The impact of CSC status on the 30-day composite model showed performance improvement for 8 of 153 CSC hospitals. CONCLUSIONS: CSC hospital status and participation in TAVR trials are significant predictors unique for stroke. Correcting for the association of CSC status on stroke rate resulted in an estimated 8 of 153 hospitals improving their TVTR 30-day composite model performance. Further work is needed to account for potential ascertainment bias for stroke in public reporting.

title: Endovascular Iliac Vein Revascularization Versus Conservative Management for Chronic, Symptomatic Iliac Vein Obstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To synthesize the existing evidence comparing endovascular iliac vein revascularization versus conservative management for chronic, symptomatic venous obstruction. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov for comparator-controlled studies of endovascular iliac vein revascularization versus conservative management. The primary outcome was the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS); secondary outcomes were the Villalta score, Venous Insufficiency Epidemiological and Economic Study Quality of Life (VEINES-QOL), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain. Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MD) using random-effects models with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Certainty was assessed with GRADE (PROSPERO CRD420261446246). RESULTS: 2 Four studies (three randomized trials, one cohort; 554 patients; n per outcome: VCSS 317, Villalta 479, VAS 267, VEINES-QOL 274) met eligibility. Revascularization reduced VCSS (MD - 2.24, 95% confidence interval [CI] - 3.86 to -0.63) and the Villalta score (MD - 3.48, 95% CI - 4.75 to - 2.21; both I= 0%). VAS pain and VEINES-QOL were inconclusive under the primary model. Technical success was 96.6%, stent thrombosis 1.9%. The largest trial showed threefold more bleeding (major and non-major, 11.6% vs. 3.6%), mainly non-major. Certainty was low for VCSS and Villalta and very low for VEINES-QOL and VAS pain. CONCLUSION: Revascularization reduced venous symptom severity under the primary model, though neither estimate was robust to omitting individual studies, and the VCSS prediction interval crossed the null. Bleeding risk was increased in the largest trial; quality-of-life and pain effects were inconclusive. The evidence offers modest support for revascularization in patients failing conservative therapy, with short follow-up.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov for comparator-controlled studies of endovascular iliac vein revascularization versus conservative management. The primary outcome was the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS); secondary outcomes were the Villalta score, Venous Insufficiency Epidemiological and Economic Study Quality of Life (VEINES-QOL), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain.

title: Cognitive impairment and cerebral hemodynamics in individuals with symptomatic peripheral artery disease.
abstract: NEW & NOTEWORTHY Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is highly prevalent in older adults. PAD is associated with cognitive impairment; however, the underlying mechanisms are unclear. The brain's metabolic needs rapidly change in response to neuronal activity, requiring adjustment of regional cerebral blood flow, termed neurovascular coupling (NVC). The microvascular endothelium contributes to NVC responses. Patients with PAD have endothelial dysfunction that may extend to the cerebral circulation, impairing NVC and cognitive function. The present study examined NVC responses to cognitive stimulation using transcranial Doppler ultrasonography (TCD) in older adults with PAD. Participants underwent bilateral TCD in the middle cerebral arteries during four recordings; baseline and tasks from Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination III and Digit Span. Mean absolute change in cerebral blood velocity (CBv) was measured at two time points (25-30 s; 30-40 s) from a 20 s baseline. Nineteen patients with intermittent claudication and 20 age-matched controls [mean: 68.4 (8.1) yr; female: 12] were included. CBv increased on all cognitive tasks; however, no significant differences were observed between patients (range: 0.9-7.4 cm/s) and controls (range: 1.1-6.9 cm/s). Patients with PAD had significantly poorer working memory and global cognitive function. Older adults with PAD had similar NVC responses to age-matched controls. The lack of differences may be due to the low prevalence of cognitive impairment, disease severity, small sample size, or the relatively simple cognitive paradigms. Future studies examining NVC in patients with PAD during tasks with higher cognitive load, and in more advanced disease stages, are needed to further understand whether impaired NVC contributes to PAD-related cognitive impairment (Clinicaltrials.gov registration number: NCT06369402).First study to examine neurovascular coupling (NVC) using transcranial Doppler ultrasonography in older adults with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Patients with PAD had similar cerebral hemodynamic responses to age-matched controls, suggesting preservation of NVC. However, patients with more severe claudication and cognitive impairment had smaller cerebral blood velocity increases. Patients had significantly worse cognitive function compared with controls, and associations were observed between reduced walking distance, lower ankle-brachial pressure index values, and poorer cognitive function.

title: Association between age and in-hospital mortality and arch repair strategy in acute type A aortic dissection: a dose-response analysis of a retrospective cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced age is a recognized risk factor in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but its dose-response relationship with in-hospital mortality and the optimal extent of arch repair in elderly patients remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to determine the age-mortality dose-response relationship and to assess arch repair strategies in elderly ATAAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. The association between age (as a continuous variable) and in-hospital mortality was assessed using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis. In a subgroup of elderly patients (≥60 years, n=115), perioperative outcomes between no/partial arch replacement and total arch replacement were compared after 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. RESULTS: vs. Among 1,042 included patients, overall in-hospital mortality was 3.7% (39/1,042), and median age was 51 (interquartile range, 40-59) years. Age was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.04 per year, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.07, P=0.01), and RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear association without evidence of a threshold effect (P overall =0.02; P for non-linearity =0.31). In the elderly subgroup (n=244), 115 patients met imaging eligibility criteria for PSM, yielding 30 matched pairs. In this small matched cohort, total arch replacement was associated with longer cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times, with no statistically significant differences in mortality (6.7%3.3%) or major complications. CONCLUSIONS: Age shows a continuous linear association with in-hospital mortality after ATAAD repair, without evidence of a threshold effect. In elderly patients, total arch replacement and limited arch repair showed no statistically significant differences in early outcomes in this small matched cohort, suggesting that operative strategy should be individualized based on anatomical and physiological risk rather than age alone-a finding that warrants validation in larger studies.

This study aimed to determine the age-mortality dose-response relationship and to assess arch repair strategies in elderly ATAAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024.

title: Sirolimus Versus Paclitaxel Drug-Coated Ballons for Femoropopliteal Disease: The LIMUS FLOW Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Drug-coated balloon treatment is the recommended strategy for endovascular peripheral artery disease treatment. Besides proliferation and migration of smooth muscle cells, endothelial dysfunction and inflammation are known contributors in the restenosis process. Sirolimus and paclitaxel are both antirestenotic agents, exerting different pharmacomechanic properties. METHODS: We investigated the differential effects of sirolimus- and paclitaxel-coated balloons (SCBs and PCBs, respectively) in the endovascular treatment of severe PAD on endothelial function and inflammation. Clinical outcomes were also assessed. LIMUS FLOW Trial (Sirolimus Versus Paclitaxel Drug-Coated Ballons for Femoropopliteal Disease: The LIMUS FLOW Randomized Trial) was a proof-of-concept investigator-initiated randomized controlled trial with 70 patients randomized to SCBs or PCBs. Endothelial function restoration was assessed via endothelial-dependent vasomotion measured by flow mediated dilatation of the superficial femoral artery. Inflammatory markers, perfusion, primary patency, and target lesion revascularization were evaluated. RESULTS: P At 12 months, SCBs led to a greater improvement in endothelial function compared with PCBs (40% improvement with SCBs versus 22% with PCBs,=0.023). The improvement in endothelial function was associated with reduced inflammatory markers following sirolimus application at 1-month follow-up. No differences were observed for primary patency or freedom from target lesion revascularization between the groups after 12 months. CONCLUSIONS: LIMUS FLOW explores a novel concept to achieve a more profound mechanistic understanding of vasomotion restoration after application of drug-coated balloons. Improved endothelial function restoration through 12 months, reduction of inflammatory markers through 30 days, with no difference in clinical outcomes, were observed following SCBs versus PCBs. title: Incidence and Predictors of Complications After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to VARC-3 Criteria: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite continuous advancements in devices and techniques, transcatheter aortic valve implantation remains associated with complications impacting outcomes. In 2021, the Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC) introduced the VARC-3 criteria to better classify procedural complications. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting transcatheter aortic valve implantation-related complications using VARC-3 definitions between 2021 and 2025. The primary end point was all-cause mortality at latest follow-up. Secondary end points included major VARC-3 complications and predictors of adverse events. RESULTS: A total of 57 studies with 73 588 patients were included. The cohort had a mean age of 81.7 years, 51.7% were women, and most had preserved ejection fraction (55.5%) and low-to-moderate surgical risk (Society of Thoracic Surgeons [STS] predicted risk of mortality [PROM] 4.1%). Technical and 30-day device success rates were 95% and 90%, respectively; early safety rate at 30 days was 66%. At average 12 months follow-up, all-cause mortality was 10.2%. The most common complication was permanent pacemaker implantation (13%), followed by type 2 or greater bleeding (9.7%), acute kidney injury stage 3-4 (4.7%), major vascular events (4.3%), and stroke (3.0%). Moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation and patient-prosthesis mismatch occurred in 4% and 8%, respectively. Study-level pooled predictor analyses showed that acute kidney injury, type 2 or greater bleeding, paravalvular regurgitation, non-structural valve dysfunction, and higher STS score were associated with higher mortality, while eccentric/severe aortic valve calcification was associated with significant paravalvular regurgitation. CONCLUSIONS: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation shows high procedural success but non-negligible complication rates under VARC-3 criteria. acute kidney injury, type 2 or greater bleeding, NSVD, periprocedural stroke and myocardial infarction after transcatheter aortic valve implantation were associated with higher mortality.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Valve Performance of Intra-Annular Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valve in Valve-in-Valve Procedures: Insights From the NAViV Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Most evidence for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) for valve-in-valve procedures comes from balloon-expandable and supra-annular self-expanding valves. However, data on intra-annular self-expanding valves remain limited. The objectives of this registry were to evaluate the short- and midterm outcomes of ViV-TAVR using the intra-annular self-expanding valve Navitor platform in a real-world setting. METHODS: The NAViV (Navitor Valve-in-Valve) registry is a retrospective, multicenter study that included 200 patients who underwent valve-in-valve TAVR with the Portico/Navitor systems. The primary end point was 30-day device success. Secondary outcomes included intraprocedural technical success, early safety, and all-cause death and major adverse events at 2 years. RESULTS: The cohort had a high-risk profile and a high prevalence of small surgical bioprostheses (internal diameter ≤21 mm in 86% of the patients). Technical success was achieved in 96%, with an in-hospital mortality rate of 2% and early safety at 30 days of 84%. Mean residual gradients after TAVR were low (14 [interquartile range, 10-20] mm Hg), and residual significant aortic regurgitation was rare (1%). Device success was 73.5%, with high residual gradients (≥20 mm Hg) being the main reason for device failure. Two-year survival and major adverse events were 85.6% and 69.8%, respectively; with low residual gradients and baseline significant AR being independently associated with higher survival. CONCLUSIONS: Valve-in-valve TAVR using the Portico/Navitor intra-annular self-expanding valve demonstrates a favorable procedural safety profile, sustained valve performance, and encouraging midterm survival in intermediate- and high-risk populations. Larger and comparative studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

However, data on intra-annular self-expanding valves remain limited. The objectives of this registry were to evaluate the short- and midterm outcomes of ViV-TAVR using the intra-annular self-expanding valve Navitor platform in a real-world setting.

title: Computed Tomography-Based Periaortic Adipose Tissue Imaging Phenotypes in Type B Aortic Dissection: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The periaortic microenvironment visible on routine computed tomography angiography remains incompletely characterized in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). We evaluated computed tomography angiography-based periaortic adipose tissue (PAAT) phenotypes associated with prevalent TBAD and explored a prespecified Tear Risk Index for post-thoracic endovascular aortic repair aortic dilation. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 100 patients with TBAD undergoing primary thoracic endovascular aortic repair and 50 normal controls frequency matched by age and sex. Deep learning-assisted, radiologist-reviewed segmentation quantified multilayer PAAT and aortic morphology. Interreader reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analyses. Group comparisons, receiver operating characteristic analyses, and adjusted logistic regression were performed. RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with TBAD had larger aortic volume and higher 3-mm PAAT volume, fat attenuation index, and fragmentation index. Aortic volume showed an area under the curve of 0.966 (95% CI, 0.941-0.991); corresponding values for 3-mm PAAT volume, fat attenuation index, and fragmentation index were 0.614, 0.819, and 0.716, respectively. Interreader intraclass correlation coefficients for selected 3-mm PAAT measures ranged from 0.822 to 0.907. Principal TBAD-control PAAT findings remained supported after false discovery rate correction, whereas post-thoracic endovascular aortic repair PAAT differences were not robust. Tear Risk Index showed limited exploratory discrimination for dilation status. CONCLUSIONS: Selected 3-mm PAAT measures characterize a reproducible computed tomography angiography-based imaging phenotype associated with prevalent TBAD and may complement conventional aortic morphology. These findings are hypothesis generating, and Tear Risk Index should not be used as a standalone clinical predictor.

We evaluated computed tomography angiography-based periaortic adipose tissue (PAAT) phenotypes associated with prevalent TBAD and explored a prespecified Tear Risk Index for post-thoracic endovascular aortic repair aortic dilation. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 100 patients with TBAD undergoing primary thoracic endovascular aortic repair and 50 normal controls frequency matched by age and sex.

title: Anti-Drug Antibody-Associated Biologic Switch in Bilateral Aggressive Mooren's Ulcer.
abstract: PURPOSE: To report a case of bilateral aggressive Mooren's ulcer (MU) requiring hospitalization, multimodal immunosuppression, and anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α biologic switching guided by therapeutic drug monitoring due to anti-adalimumab antibody (AAA) formation. METHODS: Observational case report prepared in accordance with the CARE guidelines. A 47-year-old man presented to the emergency department with bilateral corneal ulceration and high perforation risk. Comprehensive infectious and autoimmune evaluation was performed. Treatment included topical and systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, amniotic membrane grafting, tarsorrhaphy, and sequential biologic therapy. RESULTS: Bilateral aggressive MU was diagnosed after exclusion of infectious and systemic autoimmune etiologies, including the absence of scleritis. The patient required escalation from adalimumab to infliximab following AAA formation associated with secondary loss of response. Serum adalimumab trough concentration and AAA were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) at the time of suspected treatment failure. At two-year follow-up on continuous infliximab therapy, the right eye had dense corneal scarring with hand motion vision, while the left eye achieved 20/20 best-corrected visual acuity following cataract extraction during sustained disease quiescence, with no recurrence observed. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates AAA-associated biologic switching in MU-a phenomenon well described in uveitis but not previously reported in peripheral ulcerative keratitis. Therapeutic drug monitoring may have a role in optimizing biologic therapy for severe corneal autoimmune disease.

A 47-year-old man presented to the emergency department with bilateral corneal ulceration and high perforation risk.

title: Tinnitus in urban settings: insights into lifestyle and medical factors from the Hamburg City Health Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Tinnitus is a common and multifactorial auditory condition associated with considerable psychosocial burden. Evidence regarding its relationship with demographic, lifestyle, and medical factors remains inconsistent. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and correlates of tinnitus in an urban Western European population, focusing on lifestyle, socioeconomic, and clinical characteristics within the Hamburg City Health Study (HCHS). METHODS: We conducted a population-based cross-sectional analysis of data from 14,355 participants aged 45-74 years enrolled in the HCHS. Tinnitus status was defined by self-reported medical diagnosis. For statistical analyses we fitted age- and sex-adjusted logistic regression models with tinnitus status as the binary outcome. Odds ratios (ORs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) were derived from the model coefficients. Associations were examined across domains including demographics, comorbidities, medication, subjective hearing difficulties, and environmental noise exposure. RESULTS: The lifetime self-reported physician-diagnosed tinnitus was 19.3%. Male sex, older age, previous ENT surgery, sensorineural and conductive hearing loss, antidepressant use, night-shift work, sleep apnea, carotid stenosis, migraines, and shingles were associated with tinnitus. Participants with tinnitus reported greater hearing difficulties, more pronounced social consequences of hearing problems, and higher perceived environmental noise exposure. No relevant associations were observed for income, education, alcohol consumption, or occupational noise exposure. CONCLUSION: Tinnitus in urban populations is linked to auditory and psychological comorbidities and perceived environmental noise, but not to traditional socioeconomic factors. These findings highlight the multifactorial nature of tinnitus and emphasize the need for integrated medical, audiological, and psychosocial management approaches.

Evidence regarding its relationship with demographic, lifestyle, and medical factors remains inconsistent. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and correlates of tinnitus in an urban Western European population, focusing on lifestyle, socioeconomic, and clinical characteristics within the Hamburg City Health Study (HCHS).

title: Aortoesophageal fistula resulting from the treatment of the "Corkscrew esophagus" by serial endoscopic botulinum toxin injections.
abstract: An aortoesophageal fistula (AEF) is a rare condition and invariably lethal if not diagnosed and treated promptly. These fistulae usually occur from erosion of unsuspected thoracic aortic aneurysms into the adjacent esophagus, ingestion of foreign bodies, or after aortic surgery but can also develop after aggressive treatment of esophageal motility disorders. We report the case of a 69-year-old woman who developed an AEF after serial endoscopic injections of botulinum toxin into the esophagus for treatment of distal esophageal spasm or the "Corkscrew esophagus." Guidelines for treatment of this rare, previously undescribed presentation of a secondary AEF are currently ill-defined.

title: Novel endovascular management of a displaced aortic endograft component during transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old man with prior endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) of the abdominal aorta complicated by type Ia endoleak requiring two proximal aortic cuffs. Ten years later, he underwent transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) for severe aortic stenosis. During the delivery of the transcatheter aortic valve replacement device, one of the aortic cuffs was displaced into the distal thoracic aorta. This case report describes a rare complication of delayed device displacement during TAVR and demonstrates a novel strategy for endovascular salvage. It highlights the opportunity for endovascular repair during TAVR planning in patients with prior aortic stent grafts. In addition, close multidisciplinary collaboration is valuable for managing unexpected device interactions.

title: The first decade of data from the Irish National Orthopaedic Register: trends in hip and knee arthroplasty, implant utilisation and patient outcomes.
abstract: AIMS: The Irish National Orthopaedic Register (INOR) was established to monitor total hip (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) practice, implant utilisation and patient outcomes in Ireland following the recall of the Articular Surface Replacement (ASR) metal-on-metal implant. This study presents the first decade of INOR data (2015-2024) from participating hospitals, evaluating patterns in arthroplasty activity, implant fixation, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and clinical outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective descriptive analysis of aggregated data from the INOR National Report (2015-2024) and accompanying appendices was performed, including demographics, procedural activity, implant utilisation, fixation strategies, PROMs (Oxford Hip Score [OHS], Oxford Knee Score [OKS], EQ-5D-5L) and clinical outcomes (30-day surgical site infection, dislocation, periprosthetic fracture, venous thromboembolism, mortality, and one-year revision). RESULTS: A total of 43,291 arthroplasty procedures were recorded across 17 participating hospitals, including 22,249 primary THAs (51%), 18,102 primary TKAs (42%), 1,864 revision THAs (4%) and 1,076 revision TKAs (3%). Annual volume increased from 841 cases in 2015 to 10,266 in 2024. Cementless fixation in primary THA increased from 43% in 2015 to 71% in 2024. Mean OHS improved from 17.9 preoperatively to 44.0, and mean OKS from 19.5 to 40.5, at five years. Mean EQ-5D-5L improved from 0.265 to 0.818 following THA and from 0.364 to 0.793 following TKA at five years. The 30-day SSI rate was 0.5% for both THA and TKA; one-year revision occurred in 1.0% of THAs and 0.8% of TKAs, and 30-day mortality was 0.1% overall. CONCLUSION: During its first decade, INOR expanded its capture of arthroplasty procedures and generated data on implant utilisation, PROMs and clinical outcomes among participating hospitals. Because of phased onboarding and incomplete national coverage, these findings reflect practice at participating institutions rather than a complete national picture, and revision rate estimates should be interpreted cautiously given incomplete denominator capture. As participation grows, INOR is positioned to support implant surveillance, quality improvement and evidence-based arthroplasty practice in Ireland.

title: Development and external validation of risk prediction models for gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic dissection surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) following surgery for aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening complication associated with elevated mortality and increased healthcare resource utilization. However, reliable predictive tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database. METHODS: Patients who underwent AD surgery were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (MIMIC-IV; development cohort) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; external evaluation cohort). The primary outcome was postoperative GIB within 30 days, defined using a composite database-derived algorithm requiring either (I) a hemoglobin (Hb) decrease of ≥2 g/dL accompanied by at least one supporting indicator, including a transfusion record, hemostatic medication use, or endoscopic examination; or (II) the combination of a transfusion record and a GIB diagnosis. An isolated Hb decrease or transfusion record was not sufficient for outcome classification. Routinely available demographic, physiologic, laboratory, and disease-severity variables were extracted. Records with missing values in variables required for the final analysis were excluded before model development. Multivariable logistic regression served as the baseline model, with XGB and random forest employed as comparator models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, and decision-curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 935 patients (GIB incidence, 10.7%), whereas the eICU-CRD validation cohort comprised 542 patients (GIB incidence, 12.7%). In the development cohort, the AUCs were 0.887 for logistic regression, 0.962 for XGB, and 0.853 for random forest. In the eICU-CRD cohort, XGB yielded an AUC point estimate of 0.873. CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective two-database analysis developed prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery. The models showed discrimination in the analyzed data; however, prospective validation using predictors measured within prespecified pre-event windows is required before clinical implementation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) following surgery for aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening complication associated with elevated mortality and increased healthcare resource utilization. However, reliable predictive tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database.
